Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical Robin Problems on Manifolds with Noncompact Boundary
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We work on connected, noncompact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds $(\mathcal{M}, g), n \geq 3$, that are complete with respect to $d_g$ and have noncompact boundary and bounded geometry. We study the existence of positive solutions in $C^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{\infty}(\mathcal{M})$ to the Yamabe problem: $$ \left\{\begin{aligned} -Δ_g u+\frac{n-2}{4(n-1)} R_g u & =\mathscr{C}_0 u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} \quad \text { in } \mathcal{M}, \\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial ν}+\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)} H_g u & =\mathscr{C}_1 u^{\frac{n}{n-2}} \quad \text { on } \partial \mathcal{M}, \end{aligned}\right. $$ where $\mathscr{C}_0=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}), \mathscr{C}_1=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}) \mathscr{C} \bar{d}^{\frac{2}{n-2}}$, the parameter $\mathscr{C} \geq 0$ is fixed, and $$ Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}):=\inf _{u \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \backslash\{0\}} \frac{E_g(u)}{\left(\|u\|_{L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M})}^{2^*}+\mathscr{C}\|u\|_{L^{2^{\#}}(\partial \mathcal{M})}^{2^*}\right)^{2 / 2^*}} . $$ Here $E_g$ is the associated quadratic energy. We assume $Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M})<Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})$ and $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})>0$, where $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}$ is the corresponding variational level at infinity.
  We approach this problem using nonnegative solutions $u_j \in W_{\partial}^{1,2}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j)\right), j \in \mathbb{N}, j \geq j_0$, for which we prove that $$ \sup _{j \geq j_0}\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^{\infty}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j-1)\right)}<\infty . $$ For $\mathscr{C}>0$, we also prove that, along a subsequence, $\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^2{ }_{\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j) \cap \partial \mathcal{M}\right)}} \rightarrow \bar{d}$, with $0<\bar{d} \leq \mathscr{C}^{-1 / 2^*}$. For $\mathscr{C}=0$, we set $\bar{d}=0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $L^p$-theory for the exterior Stokes problem with Navier's type slip-without-friction boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we consider the stationary Stokes equations in an exterior domain three-dimensional under a slip boundary condition without friction. We set the problem in weighted Sobolev spaces in order to control the behavior at infinity of the solutions. In this work, we try to investigate the existence and uniqueness up to an element of a nontrivial kernel of the weak solutions related to this problem in $L^p-$theory when $p>3$. Our proofs are based on obtaining inf-sup conditions that play a fundamental role.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonuniqueness of the $2$D Euler Evolutions with $L^1\cap L^p$ Vorticity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For each prescribed $1<p<\infty$, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\cap L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)$ that admits two distinct evolutions under the unforced two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on $[0,1]$. Both vorticities are strongly continuous in $L^1\cap L^p$ and are transported exactly by their respective almost-everywhere invertible, measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flows. The construction couples unstable four-vortex configurations across increasingly small spatial scales, realizing them through concentrated signed vortex patches. At each finite cutoff, a prepared reference evolution remains close to rotating configurations, while a second evolution differs initially only at the finest scale. In the second evolution, the finest configuration consists of separating dipoles whose remote strain activates the instability of the next larger configuration. This process propagates through successive scales with summable transition times. As the cutoff tends to infinity, the two families of initial data converge strongly, along a subsequence, to the same datum, while a nonzero difference survives at a fixed larger scale and is detected by a fixed smooth observable at a positive limiting time. Quantitative concentration and relative comparison estimates establish this cascade for exact Euler patch solutions. Strong compactness through inverse-flow stability then preserves both exact vorticity transport and the positive-time distinction between the two limiting evolutions. The initial datum and construction parameters may depend on $p$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in $2$D Euler Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a sharp uniqueness--nonuniqueness criterion for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations within a class of stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices. Let $Θ$ be any finite nondecreasing envelope for the vorticity $L^p$ norms, and set $I_Θ=\int_{p_0}^\infty Θ(p)^{-1}\,dp$. If $I_Θ=\infty$, every array in the corresponding class admits a unique Euler evolution, even among bounded energy-admissible weak velocity solutions. If $I_Θ<\infty$, there exists a compactly supported array in the same class admitting two distinct unforced Lagrangian Euler evolutions from the same initial datum. The criterion holds for arbitrary nondecreasing envelopes $Θ$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp lifespan estimates for heat equations with Hörmander operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem $u_t-\mathcal L u=h(t)u^p$, $u(0)=\varepsilon u_0\ge0$, where $p>1$, $h\ge0$ is only locally integrable, and $\mathcal L=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j^2$ is a homogeneous Hörmander sum of squares on $\mathbb R^n$ of homogeneous dimension $q$. Diffusion spreads the solution out and weakens the nonlinearity, while the reaction $h(t)u^p$ may force blow-up. We prove that the outcome is decided by the single quantity $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T)=\int_0^Th(t)(1+t)^{-\frac q2(p-1)}\,d t$, in which the reaction at time $t$ is weighted by the factor by which diffusion has weakened the solution: small data are global if $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(\infty)<\infty$, while otherwise the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ satisfies $c\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}\le\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T_\varepsilon)\le C\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for small $\varepsilon$. Our technique of proof is based on a backward-semigroup functional combined with a Gaussian-envelope energy and an ODE cap telescoped along interlaced geometric grids. The result contains the Euclidean, Heisenberg, Carnot and Grushin cases, yields explicit lifespan laws for power, logarithmic, exponential, periodic and intermittent coefficients, and exhibits effects with no autonomous counterpart, such as a lifespan with no power law in $\varepsilon$. We also prove regularity and a priori estimates for classical solutions and discuss what remains true for a general nonlinearity $f(u)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Joint inviscid, incompressible, and continuous phenotype limit in nonlocal models of tissue growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a multispecies Brinkman tissue-growth system proposed by Debiec, Mandal, and Schmidtchen [J. Differential Equations 2025]. This system adopts a power pressure law determined by the total spatial density and models the effect of phenotype-dependent growth rates on the density dynamics of cells with different phenotypes. We examine the simultaneous vanishing-viscosity, stiff-pressure, and continuous-phenotype limit of this system. For families of bounded weak solutions with suitable initial conditions, every sequence converges, up to a subsequence, to a continuous-phenotype incompressible Darcy system, which presents a novel biological model. This result not only addresses connections between Brinkman tissue-growth systems with discrete phenotypes and those with continuous phenotypes, but also demonstrates the robustness of such connections under both the incompressible and inviscid limits.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: added a proof of vanishing defect measure, reorganized the manuscript

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Well-Posedness of Landau Equation in Bounded Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove global well-posedness of the Landau equation near a Maxwellian in bounded $C^3$ domains with in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundary conditions for $-3\leqγ\leq1$, including Coulomb interactions. Small compatible Gaussian perturbations generate global strong solutions, with uniqueness and continuous dependence among weak solutions. The proof combines energy estimates, the comparison principle, interior and weighted boundary estimates for velocity derivatives up to second order, and a logarithmic estimate for solution difference.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the existence of minimizers for the generalized liquid drop model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a broad class of generalized liquid drop models in which a perimeter term competes with repulsive nonlocal interactions with finite first moments. For all such kernels satisfying the natural physical assumption of reflection positivity we show existence of minimizers for all masses, in the (super-)critical regime. Moreover, in the subcritical regime we give the first quantitative estimate of the range of masses for which existence holds, which converges to the whole positive real line as one approaches the critical regime. This result builds on the nonlocal curvature approach introduced and developed in the periodic setting in \cite{dr24}.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and uniqueness of radial bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves the semilinear elliptic equation $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and for a broad class of nonlinearities $f$. Under further assumptions on the metric, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to the hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n_λ$ of any curvature $-λ^2$ and dimension $n\geq 3$, and to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An alternative proof of the Keel--Tao endpoint Strichartz estimates
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we give an alternative proof of the abstract endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by Keel and Tao. Our method is based on the near-far decomposition technique, which was developed in a recent work by Toyoshima and the author.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos on arbitrary finite time intervals for the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck (VRFP) equations on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unregularized interaction potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$. On every finite time interval on which the limiting classical solution satisfies the stated regularity assumptions, the particle marginals with a product initial law converge at an algebraic rate in the particle number, with constants growing at most exponentially in the marginal order. For the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a weighted $C^m$ initial probability density, $m\ge3$, with Gaussian velocity decay and polynomial spatial decay of order $M>3$ gives convergence to the global classical solution on every finite time interval. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law with weighted BBGKY estimates. A decomposition of the potential and a bounded modification of the far-field force yield weighted bounds growing geometrically in the marginal order on the prescribed interval. A centered second-moment estimate permits summation of the error hierarchy, and a synchronous coupling transfers the estimate to the original dynamics.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp $L^2$ stability for anisotropic radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish quantitative stability for radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities involving the anisotropic radial derivative and the Minkowski functional of a smooth, strictly convex body in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. Here, the convex body need not be origin-symmetric. For the $L^2$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, we establish the sharp stability constant $|b+1-a|$ for $a\ne b+1$, and classify all equality cases in the natural weighted completion spaces, by optimizing over the angular coefficients and a common dilation parameter. We also obtain the sharp stability constants $2$ and $4$ for the scale-invariant and scale-noninvariant $L^2$-Heisenberg inequality, respectively. For $2\le p<\infty$, we also establish weighted stability of the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities when $a\neq b+1$ and $(b+1-a)(N-p(b+1))\geq0$, and the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Heisenberg inequalities. As a byproduct, we establish weighted $L^p$-Poincaré inequalities for Gamma measures, which serve as the main tool for our stability estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stationary Structures of the Boussinesq equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the steady configurations supported by the inviscid two-dimensional Boussinesq equations in the periodic channel. We show steady laminar velocity fields (closed non-contractible fluid trajectories) coupled to non-decreasing density stratifications are necessarily stratified shear flows. The direction of density monotonicity along level sets is in fact fundamental: in striking contrast with the Euler equations, we exhibit laminar non-stagnant non-shear stationary solutions in the periodic channel. We also provide distinct flexibility and rigidity results (laminar persistence or appearance of islands for nearby non-shear solutions) close to stratified shear flows according to their stagnation points. As a by-product of our analysis, we establish a uniform Crandall-Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem that might be of independent interest.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Relativistic collision geometry and global near-vacuum solutions at critical transverse regularity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish global well-posedness near vacuum for the relativistic Boltzmann equation with soft and hard potentials in the range $γ\in(-2,1]$. The initial data have critical Besov regularity of order $2/r$ in the transverse spatial variables for an admissible range of $r$ depending on $γ$, together with weighted integrability in the longitudinal and momentum variables. The proof combines a fixed-direction div--curl lemma with bilinear collision estimates. In particular, to control the gain term, we combine localization to spherical caps with energy-weighted angular estimates. The key relativistic estimate controls the singularity associated with the first component of the post-collisional relative velocity. These bounds yield the required time decay.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonuniqueness and failure of positivity preservation for doubly critical semilinear heat equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
At the Fujita exponent $p=1+2/N$ we construct a strictly positive mild solution of $u_t-Δu=|u|^{p-1}u$ in $\mathbb R^N$ whose initial trace in $L^1$ is zero. In similarity variables the solution approaches a Gaussian profile, and $$\|U(t)\|_1\sim C_N(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},\qquad
  \|U(t)\|_\infty\sim c_Nt^{-N/2}(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},$$ with explicit constants $C_N$ and $c_N$. In particular, uniqueness fails at the borderline logarithmic rate, and the solution lies outside every stronger logarithmic uniqueness class; this answers two questions raised by Miyamoto [J. Evol. Equ. 21 (2021), 151--166, Remark~1.6]. We also prove that, up to time translation, this is the only ancient solution of fixed sign of the rescaled equation that decays in a Gaussian weighted supremum norm. On a bounded smooth domain the whole-space solution can be localized at finitely many interior points, with independently chosen signs, on top of an arbitrary bounded initial datum. The resulting solutions are classical for $t>0$ and continuous at $t=0$ in $L^1$. Consequently, uniqueness fails for every bounded datum, and positivity is lost for every bounded nonnegative datum, $u_0\equiv1$ included. These results provide affirmative answers to Open Problems~3 and~4 posed by Brezis and Cazenave in [J. Anal. Math. 68 (1996), 277--304].

Analysis of PDEs.title: Drift-diffusion equations with saturation on $\mathbb{R}^d$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a class of nonlinear drift--diffusion equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with saturation-type mobilities, not necessarily concave. Under structural assumptions on the mobility and potentials, bounded-domain approximations and local Caccioppoli estimates yield weak solutions for all positive times and an $L^1$-contraction estimate. The same estimates provide local space--time compactness of time translates, whose subsequential limits are weak solutions. Under additional confinement assumptions, uniform mass-tail estimates yield a mass-preserving, free-energy dissipating $C_0$-semigroup of $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$-contractions. In this confining setting, every trajectory converges strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to a stationary state with the same mass, and the resulting time-limit operator is an $L^1$-contraction. Under the same assumptions, we also identify the unique global and $L^1$-local minimiser of the free energy at each fixed mass and prove that it is stationary under the semigroup.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary-Driven Nonequilibrium for the Coulomb Landau Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a nonlinear theory of the Coulomb Landau equation in smooth bounded domains with non-isothermal diffuse reflection. We construct a stationary state, prove its perturbative uniqueness and global nonlinear stability, and establish exponential convergence when the wall temperature approaches its stationary profile exponentially. We also establish stationary and global nonlinear well-posedness for prescribed inflow, together with asymptotic stability. The analysis combines a critical kinetic integrability gain with finite-exponent velocity-gradient estimates near grazing, allowing the nonlinear Coulomb estimates to close without $L_x^\infty$ control of velocity gradients.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This arXiv preprint provides a detailed companion to the more concise journal-submission version of the same title. This version is not intended for separate journal publication. 413 pages. v2: minor revisions; results unchanged

Analysis of PDEs.title: Second variation of the fractional torsion energy and linear stability of the ball
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We compute the second shape derivative of the fractional torsion. It is an explicit quadratic form on the boundary, which involves a Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator for half-harmonic functions blowing up at the boundary. We deduce an explicit formula for volume preserving variations on the ball and show
  that as in the local case, the shape Hessian is negative and coercive in \(H^{1/2}\) modulo translations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The fractional Faber--Krahn inequality in sharp quantitative form
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the fractional Laplacian satisfies the sharp quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality. This was conjectured by Brasco, Cinti and Vita, who proved the inequality with a sub-optimal exponent. The proof adapts to the non-local setting the level-set argument recently introduced by Guerra, Machado and Ramos for the Laplacian. It is carried out on the horizontal level sets of the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of the torsion function, where the asymmetry appears only as a boundary value at the corner of the extension variables.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A decay estimate for cubic defocusing non-linear Schrödinger equation in three dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this short note, we prove a decay estimate for non-linear solutions of the 3D cubic defocusing non-linear Schrödinger equation.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 16 pages. [v3] Final version. Published in J. Evol. Equ

Analysis of PDEs.title: Energy equality and renormalization of Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study weak solutions of the incompressible and the compressible Navier--Stokes--Vlasov systems on a bounded domain, where a viscous fluid is coupled to a dispersed particle phase through a drag force; the fluid obeys the no-slip boundary condition and the particles are subject to specular reflection. For solutions with Besov regularity, we show that the Vlasov equation is renormalizable in the sense of DiPerna--Lions, and we give regularity thresholds for the validity of the global energy equality. If the distribution function $f$ belongs to $B_p^{α,\infty}$ in space and velocity with time integrability $p$, and the fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to $B_q^{β,\infty}$ jointly in space and time with integrability $q$, then the energy equality holds provided $α+β>1$ and $β$ exceeds an explicit bound depending on $p$, $q$ and the dimension, under a natural integrability assumption on the pressure; an analogous criterion holds for the compressible system when the density is bounded from above and below. The condition $αp>1$ imposed on $f$ is not merely technical: it is exactly the range in which the macroscopic momentum flux possesses a boundary trace, so that the specular reflection condition passes to the macroscopic energy balance. When the particle phase is absent, our thresholds coincide with the criteria $β>\frac12+\frac1q$ and $β>\frac3q$ obtained by Yu for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations alone. The proofs combine a boundary cutoff argument with commutator estimates based on a scale-localized Besov modulus, together with a boundary-strip analysis.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Submitted to Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal

Analysis of PDEs.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local $Tb$ theorems in non-homogeneous metric spaces, and applications to caloric measure
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calderón-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators.
  As an application in the parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(σ)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $σ$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Blow up and Concentration without Quantization: sharp Harnack type inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Motivated by the Onsager statistical mechanics description of turbulent Euler flows with point singularities, we refine the blow up analysis for sequences of solutions of a class of perturbed singular Liouville equations which share the phenomenon of ``blow up and concentration without quantization". The problem is delicate because we are dealing with the exact threshold value above which one meets the well known ``concentration without quantization" phenomenon, as recently pushed forward in [C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris} (2016)] and in [Y. Lee, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, W. Yang, {\em Comm. PDE.} (2017)]. We overcome these difficulties by developing different strategies for ``fast" and ``slow" blow up, combining refined Pohozaev identities, elliptic estimates and ``Sup+CInf" inequalities in the same spirit of [C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, {\em Comm. An. Geom.} (1998)]. In the process, we also derive a new sharp Harnack type inequality by using a moving-plane method, following the ideas in [D. Bartolucci, C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em Comm. P.D.E.} (2002)].

Analysis of PDEs.title: Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A particle system approach towards the global well-posedness of master equations for potential mean field games of control
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper studies the $N$-particle systems as well as the HJB/master equations for a class of generalized mean field control (MFC) problems and the corresponding potential mean field games of control (MFGC). A local in time classical solution for the HJB equation is generated via a probabilistic approach based on the mean field maximum principle. Given an extension of the so called displacement convexity condition, we obtain the uniform estimates on the HJB equation for the $N$-particle system. Such estimates imply the displacement convexity/semi-concavity and thus the prior estimates on the solution to the HJB equation for generalized MFC problems. The global well-posedness of HJB/master equation for generalized MFC/potential MFGC is then proved thanks to the local well-posedness and the prior estimates. In view of the nature of the displacement convexity condition, such well-posedness is also true for the degenerated case. Our analysis on the $N$-particle system also induces an Lipschitz approximator to the optimal feedback function in generalized MFC/potential MFGC where an algebraic convergence rate is obtained. Furthermore, an alternative approximate Nash equilibrium is proposed based on the $N$-particle system, where the approximation error is quantified thanks to the aforementioned uniform estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
A Minkowski normed space is the Euclidean space equipped with a (possibly asymmetric) uniformly convex and smooth norm, forming a particular class of Finsler manifolds.
  We construct a stochastic process with one-dimensional time marginal densities given by the fundamental solution to the nonlinear Finsler heat equation in Minkowski normed spaces.
  This process is constructed as a solution to a singular McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and constitutes a nonlinear Markov process in the sense of McKean.
  We show that solutions to this stochastic differential equation are pathwise unique, and, thus, probabilistically strong solutions, though the equation has singular coefficients beyond the subcritical regime.
  Since our construction is a natural extension of the construction of standard Brownian motion from the standard heat kernel, we call this process \emph{Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces.}
  Furthermore, we obtain a universality property, namely that whichever Minkowski norm is chosen, the radial part of this process is the standard Bessel process.
  To the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of stochastic processes associated with nonlinear heat equation in Finslerian spaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $γ$-Valued Stein--Tomas Restriction for Schatten Classes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $Σ\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact $C^2$ hypersurface with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We prove the sharp matrix-dimension-independent Schatten-valued Stein--Tomas range \[ R_Σ:L^p(\mathbb R^3;S^a)\longrightarrowγ(L^2(Σ),S^a), \qquad 1<a<\infty,\quad 1\le p\le\min\{a,4/3\}. \] The core endpoint is $E_Σ:γ(L^2(Σ),S^4)\to L^4(\mathbb R^3;S^4)$. After squaring the quartic norm, multiplication lands in the Hilbert--Schmidt class. A local coarea argument splits resonant quartets according to the shorter adjacent frequency chord, producing a dimension-free row/column estimate for elliptic and hyperbolic curvature. We also show that Gaussian type $4/3$ alone does not characterize the corresponding endpoint for arbitrary Banach spaces. Applications include matrix Herglotz waves, a two-dimensional Schrödinger $L^4$ estimate, and free spectral-measure bounds.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Exact Traces for Vector-Valued Morrey Spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish an exact trace theorem for vector-valued time-Morrey spaces and complementary continuity theorems for time-BMO evolution classes. For a Banach couple $X_1\hookrightarrow X_0$, $1<p<\infty$ and $0<λ<1$, we prove that the trace of the class $u\in\mathcal M^{p,λ}(X_1)$, $u_t\in\mathcal M^{p,λ}(X_0)$ is exactly $(X_0,X_1)_{θ,\infty}$, where $θ=1-(1-λ)/p$. A constructive extension realizes every admissible trace, and counterexamples establish optimality of both the smoothness exponent and the weak fine index. Time-BMO control yields continuous finite-index interpolation traces and, under a mixed boundedness hypothesis, a logarithmic time modulus whose base-space logarithm is necessary. For the quadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation on the torus, we characterize the bounded initial data generating Morrey-regular solutions by the exact Besov condition $u_0\in B_{2,\infty}^{2θ}$. The proof uses Hopf--Cole linearization and a direct composition argument, and requires no smallness assumption. Lacunary nonlinear solutions realize the sharp trace threshold. A forced Hamilton--Jacobi example exhibits genuinely logarithmic time regularity, and a forward--backward mean-field-game system illustrates initial and terminal trace compatibility. \par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} Morrey spaces; trace spaces; real interpolation; Hamilton--Jacobi equations; bounded mean oscillation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth in a biological membrane exposed to a periodic electric potential, where the growth term is modified through the first moment of the solution $n_1(t)$. We show that for initial data $f_0$ with noncompact support it holds $n_1(t) \rightarrow \infty$ , whereas for $f_0$ with compact support the limit of $n_1$ depends sensitively on the data. For a broad class of initial data we additionally obtain $n_1 \sim t^{\frac{1}{2}}$. In the case of a constant external potential we further prove that solutions converge to the self-similar solution having the same tail behaviour as $f_0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local boundedness for solutions to parabolic double phase problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate the local boundedness of weak solutions to parabolic double phase equations of type $$u_t-\mathrm{div}(|Du|^{p-2}Du+a(x,t)|Du|^{q-2}Du)=0\quad\text{in }Ω_T:=Ω\times(0,T),$$ where $0\leq a(\cdot)\in L^\infty(Ω_T)$ and $\frac{2n}{n+2}<p<q<p\left(\frac{n+2}{n}\right)$, so that both the degenerate range $p\geq 2$ and the singular range $p<2$ are covered. To this end, we derive the Caccioppoli inequality and recall a parabolic embedding theorem, which are then utilized in an iteration method.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Liouville theorem for plurisubharmonic functions with periodic complex Monge-Ampère measure
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study entire continuous plurisubharmonic solutions of the complex Monge-Ampère equation $(i\partial\bar\partial u)^n=2^n n!μ$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$, in the Bedford-Taylor sense, where $μ\not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite Borel measure periodic with respect to a lattice of full real rank. We assume that $μ$ is locally dominated by complex Monge-Ampère measures of Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic functions, a condition under which the existence theorem of Demailly et al. yields Hölder continuous periodic correctors. Under this assumption, we prove that every such solution with positive two-sided quadratic growth can be written uniquely, up to an additive constant, as the sum of a real quadratic polynomial and a Hölder continuous periodic function.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Linear stability analysis for 2D shear flows near Couette in the isentropic Compressible Euler equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate linear stability properties of the 2D isentropic compressible Euler equations linearized around a shear flow given by a monotone profile, close to the Couette flow, with constant density, in the domain $\mathbb{T}\times \mathbb{R}$. We begin by directly investigating the Couette shear flow, where we characterize the linear growth of the compressible part of the fluid while proving time decay for the incompressible part (inviscid damping with slower rates). Then we extend the analysis to monotone shear flows near Couette, where we are able to give an upper bound, superlinear in time, for the compressible part of the fluid. The incompressible part enjoys an inviscid damping property, analogous to the Couette case. In the pure Couette case, we exploit the presence of an additional conservation law (which connects the vorticity and the density on the moving frame) in order to reduce the number of degrees of freedom of the system. The result then follows by using weighted energy estimates. In the general case, unfortunately, this conservation law no longer holds. Therefore we define a suitable weighted energy functional for the whole system, which can be used to estimate the irrotational component of the velocity but does not provide sharp bounds on the solenoidal component. However, even in the absence of the aforementioned additional conservation law, we are still able to show the existence of a functional relation which allows us to recover somehow the vorticity from the density, on the moving frame. By combining the weighted energy estimates with the functional relation we also recover the inviscid damping for the solenoidal component of the velocity.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Withdrawn due to an error in the analysis of shear flows near Couette: the weight v defined in (5.19) was incorrectly treated as self-adjoint in the energy identities. The results for the exact Couette flow are unaffected and were subsequently included, improved and extended in arXiv:2101.01696

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Hénon equation beyond the critical Sobolev exponent
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the Dirichlet problem $-Δu=|x|^αu^p$, $u>0$ in $Ω$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, where $Ω\subset R^N$, $N\ge 3$, is a bounded domain containing the origin and $α>0$. We prove that a solution exists for every exponent $1<p<p_α=\frac{N+2+2α}{N-2}$, in particular in the whole Sobolev-supercritical range $\frac{N+2}{N-2}\le p<p_α$, provided $Ω$ is invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and satisfies an angular monotonicity condition. This class contains the balls, the oblate ellipsoids of revolution, lens-shaped domains, and non-convex, non-smooth and non star-shaped domains. The solution is obtained by minimizing the Rayleigh quotient on a suitable closed convex cone.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplacian with Morrey data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We obtain sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplace equation with a right-hand side belonging to a Morrey space. We derive local $C^{σ+λ-n}-$regularity of solutions when $σ+λ-n\neq1$, where $σ\in(0,2)$ is the order of the operator and $λ\in(n-σ,n)$ is the Morrey decay rate of the right-hand side. In the case $σ+λ-n=1$, we show that solutions are locally in the Zygmund class, and hence are Log-Lipschitz continuous. Explicit examples attest to the sharpness of the conditions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Variational characterization of principal eigenvalues for a general class of linear weighted BVP's under mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
The main goal of this paper is to characterize the existence of principal eigenvalues of $$
  \left \{ \begin{array}{ll}
  -\mathrm{div}\left(A\nabla u\right) +qu=λm u \quad & \hbox{in} \;\; Ω,\\[1ex]
  \mathscr{B} u = 0 \quad & \hbox{on} \;\; \partial Ω, \end{array} \right. $$ where $m\in L^\infty(Ω)$ satisfies some of the conditions (A1)-(A3) below, as well as to deliver their variational characterizations whenever they exist. As we are dealing with general boundary operators of mixed non-classical type, in the general setting of this paper our results are far more general than all existing results. The case when $m$ satisfies (A2) has not been previously explored in the literature.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate a matrix Riemann--Hilbert problem whose solution provides a reconstruction formula for the solution of the original Cauchy problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On decay of solutions to the anisotropic Boussinesq equations near the hydrostatic balance in half space $\mathbb{R}_+^3$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The system of the Boussinesq equations is one of the most important models for geophysical fluids. This paper focuses on the initial-boundary problem of the 3D incompressible anisotropic Boussinesq system with horizontal dissipation. The goal here is to assess the stability property and large-time behavior of perturbations near the hydrostatic balance. By utilizing the structure of the system, the energy methods and the means of bootstrapping argument, we prove the global stability property in the Sobolev space $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3_+)$. After taking a Fourier transform in $x_h = (x_1, x_2)$ and Fourier cosine and sine transforms in $x_3$ for the system, we obtain the decay rates for the global solution itself as well as its derivatives.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A class of port-Hamiltonian systems with general time delays
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We define a class of infinite dimensional linear port-Hamiltonian delay systems, give a characterization for such systems, and provide an easily verifiable sufficient condition to belong to this class, thereby extending the study by Breiten, Hinsen and Unger in [IEEE Trans. Autom. Control vol. 69, no. 12 (2024), pp. 8924-8930, doi: 10.1109/TAC.2024.3464332]. The results rely on the operator semigroup theoretic treatment of linear delay PDEs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Semigroup-Aware Kernel Neural Operator with Latent Exponential Integration for Forced PDEs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We propose a semigroup-aware structured kernel neural operator for source-driven evolution PDEs. Unlike generic time-conditioned kernel models, the proposed formulation represents temporal dependence through a latent exponential propagator \(e^{tA_θ}\), where \(A_θ\) is a learned latent generator. This provides a structured transition from a non-ODE kernel representation to an ODE-inspired kernel operator whose latent temporal evolution satisfies the composition principle of evolution semigroups. For time-dependent forcing terms, a direct kernel-based evaluation requires repeated quadrature over delayed kernel evaluations. To address this computational bottleneck, we derive a latent-first reformulation of the source term: the forcing field is projected onto the kernel-induced latent space, where its accumulated effect is represented as the solution of a forced linear latent dynamical system. For a fixed learned kernel, this reformulation is exact. The resulting system can then be integrated using a \(φ_1\)-based exponential integrator, yielding a source-evaluation path that is structurally aligned with the learned latent propagator. The resulting framework combines geometry- and physics-conditioned low-rank kernel factorization with alternative source-evaluation paths based on either explicit Duhamel quadrature or latent exponential integration. Dissipativity constraints on the latent generator and identity-preserving corrections near the initial time are optional architectural components. Numerical experiments on advection-iffusion-reaction (ADR) problems compare the non-ODE and semigroup-aware formulations, evaluate the quadrature and \(φ_1\) source paths, and assess predictive accuracy and computational cost.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Noether symmetries and conservation laws of a class of time-dependent multidimensional nonlinear wave equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Conservation laws of a class of time-dependent damped nonlinear multidimensional wave equations are derived by Noether's theorem. For arbitrary nonzero damping coefficient and nonlinear interaction term, its infinitesimal variational symmetries span a Euclidean algebra $\euclid(n)$ of space translations and rotations. They produce conservation of linear and angular momentums. For some specific forms of these two terms symmetry algebra is enlarged to a subalgebra of the conformal algebra $\conf(1,n)$ and in this case more interesting conservation laws are found.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Instability theory of stationary solutions for nonlinear Schrödinger equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the orbital instability of algebraically decaying stationary solutions of nonlinear Schrödinger equations in dimensions $d\ge2$, taking competing double-power nonlinearities as a canonical model. At zero frequency, the essential spectrum of the linearized operator touches zero, and the usual $H^1$ coercivity is lost. We construct the zero-frequency limit $η_0$ of the frequency derivatives $\partial_ωφ_ω$ of standing-wave profiles and determine its sharp asymptotic behavior. For a stationary ground state $φ_0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, we prove instability if $\langle x\rangle\,φ_0\notin L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ or, when $\langle x\rangle\,φ_0\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, if the duality pairing $\langleη_0,φ_0\rangle$ is negative. This criterion is a zero-frequency counterpart of the negative slope condition in the Grillakis--Shatah--Strauss theory. The proof combines variation of parameters for the linearized ODE with a shooting analysis that determines the global behavior of the homogeneous solution regular at the origin. We then localize $η_0$ to construct an unstable direction and establish instability through a Lyapunov functional argument based on the variational characterization of ground states. The results extend with essentially the same proofs to a class of multiple-power nonlinearities.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Klein-Gordon-Born-Infeld equations driven by mixed local-nonlocal operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we study a class of Klein-Gordon-Born-Infeld systems in which the classical Laplacian appearing in the matter equation is replaced by a mixed local-nonlocal operator, whose nonlocal part is allowed to be nonpositive definite according to a real parameter. Both the approximate and the exact Born-Infeld field equations are considered in parallel. After making the functional framework explicit, we identify a range of real parameters for which infinitely many radially symmetric standing waves exist, obtained as Mountain Pass critical points of the associated reduced energy functionals. The mixed local-nonlocal operator reduces to the classical Laplacian as the nonlocal weight vanishes, and is motivated, in the spirit of effective field theories, by nonlocal corrections to the matter dispersion relation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform $L^2$-bounds for the $n$-th Calderón commutator on Lipschitz graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that, for every real Lipschitz function $A$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\|T_{A,n}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C\,\|A'\|_\infty^n$, where $T_{A,n}$ is the $n$-th Calderón commutator and $C$ is an absolute constant.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Euler--Lagrange Flow Monotonicity for the Radon Transform
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We present a new gradient-like flow that targets critical points of the inequality for the planar Radon transform $\mathcal{R}$ proven by Oberlin and Stein, partially answering a question of Christ, who gave a complete characterisation of the extremisers of the inequality via rearrangement methods. We show that for non-negative radial initial data near the extremiser manifold, solutions to the flow exist globally and there exists a rescaled subsequence of the flow that converges to a critical point of the Radon functional $\|\mathcal{R} f\|_3/\|f\|_{3/2}$ locally in $L^{3/2}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We also obtain a quantitative result for the rate of decay of critical points, which complements a result of Christ arXiv:1106.0719 in the special case of radial functions. We prove a novel localised smoothing estimate for the operator $\mathcal{R}^*[(\mathcal{R}\cdot)^2]$ restricted to radial functions. This approach is complementary to that of Christ and provides a robust framework for studying extremal problems associated to Radon-like operators.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Centro-Affine Differential Geometry and the Log-Minkowski Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We interpret the log-Brunn-Minkowski conjecture of Böröczky-Lutwak-Yang-Zhang as a spectral problem in centro-affine differential geometry. In particular, we show that the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator coincides with the centro-affine Laplacian, thus obtaining a new avenue for tackling the conjecture using insights from affine differential geometry. As every strongly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a centro-affine unit-sphere, it has constant centro-affine Ricci curvature equal to $n-2$, in stark contrast to the standard weighted Ricci curvature of the associated metric-measure space, which will in general be negative. In particular, we may use the classical argument of Lichnerowicz and a centro-affine Bochner formula to give a new proof of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality. For origin-symmetric convex bodies enjoying fairly generous curvature pinching bounds (improving with dimension), we are able to show global uniqueness in the $L^p$- and log-Minkowski problems, as well as the corresponding global $L^p$- and log-Minkowski conjectured inequalities. As a consequence, we resolve the isomorphic version of the log-Minkowski problem: for any origin-symmetric convex body $\bar K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, there exists an origin-symmetric convex body $K$ with $\bar K \subset K \subset 8 \bar K$, so that $K$ satisfies the log-Minkowski conjectured inequality, and so that $K$ is uniquely determined by its cone-volume measure $V_K$. If $\bar K$ is not extremely far from a Euclidean ball to begin with, an analogous isometric result, where $8$ is replaced by $1+ε$, is obtained as well.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Appended an erratum at the end of the published version. We replace the widthdrawn Theorem 6.4 with a corrected lemma, stressing that this does not change the validity of any of the other results in the paper. In particular, we give corrected proofs of Theorems 1.2, 1.5 and 1.7, with their original statements and constants unchanged

Analysis of PDEs.title: Invariant Densities on Cylinders with an Interface: Existence, Uniqueness, and Exponential Asymptotics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the stationary double-divergence equation on the infinite cylinder $\mathbb R\times\mathbb T^{d-1}$, whose coefficients coincide with two possibly different periodic media outside a bounded interface layer. Under the centering conditions for the two periodic media, we construct a positive invariant density that converges exponentially in $C^1$ at each end to a positive multiple of the corresponding periodic invariant density. Every bounded distributional solution is a scalar multiple of this density. The two asymptotic amplitudes are determined by the full interface problem, up to a common normalization. Motivated by the invariant-measure analysis of Hairer and Manson [Ann. Probab. 39(2011) 648-682], our proof uses only PDE methods: a transformation based on the periodic invariant densities, adjoint Neumann problems on finite cylinders, and energy estimates.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Substantially revised version. The assumption $b_1=0$ has been removed, and the homogenization applications have been omitted. The title has been changed to reflect the focus on existence, uniqueness, and exponential asymptotics for stationary double-divergence equations on cylinders with an interface

Analysis of PDEs.title: Arbitrary Dirichlet Eigenvalue Multiplicities on Smooth Star-Shaped Euclidean Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In every fixed dimension \(N\ge3\), for any finite list of positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\), we construct smooth strictly star-shaped Euclidean domains whose first \(\ell+1\) distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues can have multiplicities \(1,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\) respectively. The condition "star-shaped" is almost optimal in the sense that this statement can not hold for bounded convex domains. In fact, we show that the second Dirichlet eigenvalue of any bounded convex domain has multiplicity at most $N$, and this bound is sharp.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Wulff Rigidity for Overdetermined Anisotropic $k$-Hessian Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish Wulff rigidity for overdetermined anisotropic $k$-Hessian equations associated with a smooth and strongly convex Finsler gauge. The solutions are subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary and a prescribed anisotropic gradient condition on a smooth domain. We prove that the domain must be a Wulff shape. The same rigidity holds under a prescribed positive weighted Neumann-type condition. These results extend the Wulff rigidity for the endpoint cases $k=1$ (Cianchi--Salani, \emph{Math. Ann.}, 2009; Wang--Xia \emph{Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal.}, 2011) and $k=n$ ( Cianchi--Salani, \emph{J. Funct. Anal.}, 2023) to the intermediate cases $2\le k<n$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Transfer Principle for Elliptic Carleman Estimates: Application to Discrete Calderón Stability
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop a transfer principle that lifts continuous elliptic Carleman estimates to mesh-uniform estimates for conforming Galerkin discretizations. The main difficulties are twofold: discrete states generally lack the \(H^2\)-regularity required by the continuous estimate, and the Carleman parameter \(s\) must be controlled relative to the mesh size \(h\). We overcome both by introducing a shifted continuous problem whose Galerkin solution is exactly the conforming reconstruction of a prescribed discrete state. Weighted approximation then transfers the inequality back to the original discrete operator without adding stabilization, and yields the range \(s\le ch^{-4/5}\) for radial weights. We verify the framework for piecewise affine finite elements with consistent or lumped mass on fitted, uniformly shape-regular meshes, and for standard Cartesian finite differences through their finite-element realization. As an application, we study the discrete Calderón problem for bounded complex Schrödinger potentials in dimension \(d\ge3\). Assuming agreement in a fixed connected boundary neighborhood and uniform stability of the discrete Dirichlet problems, we obtain stability from Dirichlet inputs and variational flux observations on independently prescribed, possibly disjoint boundary patches. The resulting estimate in \(H^{-r}\), \(r>d/2\), retains the single logarithmic data term and the \(O(h^{1/2})\) mesh remainder of the full-data estimate.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Optimality of the BCC lattice among 3D lattice quantizers
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the problem of the best approximation (w.r.t. the optimal transport metric $W_p$, $p \in [1,\infty)$) of the three-dimensional Lebesgue measure on a domain of volume 1 by a discrete probability measure supported on a Bravais lattice. This problem is known as the quantization problem and it arises in numerical integration, electrical engineering, discrete geometry and materials science. As the lattice size tends to zero and the cardinality of the support of the discrete measure tends to infinity, this reduces to the following geometric optimization problem: Amongst three-dimensional Bravais lattices with determinant $1$, which lattice minimises the $p$-th moment of the lattice Voronoi cell? Barnes and Sloane (1983) proved that the BCC lattice is optimal for the case $p=2$, which is known as the vector quantization problem in the signal compression literature. Bambah (1954) proved that the BCC lattice is optimal for the limiting case $p=\infty$, which is the sphere covering problem. Based on these results, Graf and Luschgy (2000) conjectured that the BCC lattice is optimal for all $p \in [1,\infty)$. Three dimensions is the critical dimension in the sense that in two dimensions the optimal lattice is independent of $p$, whereas in four dimensions it varies with $p$. In this paper we give support in favour of Graf and Luschgy's conjecture by proving that the BCC lattice is a local minimiser for all $p \in [1,\infty)$ and a global minimiser for $p$ near 2. While the conjecture asserts that the global minimiser is independent of $p$, we prove a bifurcation theorem which shows that the set of critical points depends on $p$ and that $p=2$ is a distinguished case. Our proofs combine results from discrete geometry by Barnes and Sloane (1983) and Conway and Sloane (1992) with optimal transport theory, the calculus of variations, bifurcation theory, and some delicate positivity estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Unified transform method for nonautonomous linear evolution equations: rigorous analysis and qualitative theory
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Established herein is the rigorous extension of the celebrated Fokas unified transform method for linear evolution PDE with time-dependent coefficients. As illustrative examples, considered below and rigorously analysed in detail are non-homogeneous initial-boundary-value problems, formulated on the half-line, for the heat equation and the modified heat (also widely known as Barenblatt's pseudo-parabolic) equation with reaction terms and temporally varying coefficients. Solution formulae are derived formally via suitable implementation of the UTM, and rigorously verified a posteriori, in the classical sense. The latter task relies on complex-analytic tools and careful interpretation of the obtained integral representations. The explicit solutions established here are then used for investigating qualitative properties. These include regularity, boundary behavior near the axes of the domain as well as long-range and eventual periodicity asymptotics. Notably, smoothness of the solution up to the boundaries depends on compatibility conditions between initial, boundary and forcing data, into which interjected now are initial values of the coefficients. Further results pertaining to solution uniqueness, analyticity and controllability of the addressed problems are thence deduced in light of the preceding qualitative theory.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The fundamental solution of a family of anisotropic fourth-order parabolic equations: small-time asymptotics and related Gaussian estimates
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the fundamental solutions of a class of uniformly elliptic fourth-order parabolic equations in two dimensions, whose principal symbols are not necessarily strongly convex. For constant-coefficient operators, we derive precise small-time asymptotic formulas along certain special directions. These formulas are obtained by the method of steepest descent and reveal the dependence of the asymptotic behavior on the coefficients of the symbol. We subsequently consider operators with bounded measurable coefficients, subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions, and establish Gaussian bounds for their fundamental solutions by means of Davies' exponential perturbation method. The exponential constant in these bounds is shown to be sharp, as a consequence of the constant-coefficient asymptotics.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A sharp lower bound for torsional rigidity of convex domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, we establish the following sharp inequality for torsional rigidity $$T(Ω)\ge\frac{2(d+1)}{d}\int\limits_Ω\operatorname{dist}(x,\partialΩ)^2\dd x,$$ where $T(Ω)=4\int\limits_Ωu\dd x$ and $-Δu=1$ in $Ω$, $u\in H^1_0(Ω)$. Equality holds for balls.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A new sharp Sobolev inequality between the $Q$-curvature and the scalar curvature on Euclidean space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a sharp Sobolev-type inequality on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 5$, that interpolates between the second-order energy and a weighted first-order term. Specifically, we determine the sharp constant $S_{4,2}$ in the inequality \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^n} (Δu)^2\,dx \ge S_{4,2} \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\nabla u|^{2}|u|^{\frac{4}{n-4}}\,dx\right)^{\frac{n-4}{n-2}}, \end{equation*} for any $u\in\dot H^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and we classify the cases of equality. This solves the problem of minimizing the total $Q$-curvature of among metrics on the sphere, conformal to the standard metric, with fixed total scalar curvature.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Symmetry and uniqueness of degree $-1$ minimizers of a chiral magnetic energy
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the two-dimensional energy of a chiral magnet, consisting of the exchange energy, a bulk Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction with constant $κ\ne0$, and the Zeeman energy in an applied field $h>0$. We prove that the minimizers of this energy among maps of degree $-1$ are exactly the translates of one axially symmetric Bloch skyrmion, whose helicity is determined by the sign of $κ$. This holds for $h \geq c κ^2$, where $c \in(π^2 / 16,1)$ is determined by the slope of the radial profile at the origin; in particular, it holds in the whole range $h\geκ^2$, which answers a question raised by Melcher and by Döring and Melcher. The proof is a calibration argument. Using the profile of the skyrmion, we write the energy density of an arbitrary map as a weighted topological density, plus a divergence, plus a nonnegative remainder, and we show that this identity can be integrated for every map of finite energy. The method also gives the uniqueness of the monotone solution of the profile equation for $h\geκ^2/2$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quasi-crystalline phase separation in one dimension
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate a Modica-Mortola energy in heterogeneous materials with a quasi-crystalline microstructure, described by a suitable notion of almost periodicity. In the regime where phase separation occurs at a finer scale than homogenization, we establish compactness and $Γ$-convergence results in one dimension for vector-valued phases. The main novelty lies in the explicit characterization of the effective surface energy, which reveals the interplay between phase separation and homogenization. In particular, we prove that heterogeneities can promote the splitting of a phase separation into several energetically favorable microscopic transitions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and spectral instability of steady rolls in the Nikolaevskiy equation: a computer-assisted study
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The Nikolaevskiy equation is a model of short-wave pattern formation coupled to a neutral long-wave mode, and it is believed that all of its spatially periodic steady states are unstable. Existing results are formal, numerical, or restricted to a small neighbourhood of onset. We give computer-assisted proofs of three results. First, for every wavenumber q in [0.9, 1.1] and every control parameter r between the onset value (1-q^2)^2 and 4, the equation has a nontrivial, real-analytic, odd steady roll; these rolls form a single continuous two-parameter family that bifurcates from the trivial state at onset, with an explicit amplitude bound proportional to the square root of the distance to onset. Second, every roll of this family with r in [0.25, 4] is spectrally unstable on the real line: its linearisation has a Bloch eigenvalue with real part at least 6.7e-4, and at least 0.13 for r >= 0.575. Third, at nine sample points we enclose, at a small Bloch number, the eigenvalue numerically identified with the long-wave (Matthews-Cox) branch; its real part is positive at seven points and negative at two, while strongly unstable eigenvalues exist at all nine. The proofs combine a parametrised Newton-Kantorovich theorem, a desingularisation near onset, Taylor-model bounds on parameter boxes, and a Weyl-sequence argument for the Bloch spectrum; all estimates are evaluated in rigorous interval arithmetic.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 16 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to SIAM J. Appl. Dyn. Syst. (2026)

Analysis of PDEs.title: Spectral Characterization, Local Rigidity and Morse Index of Bubble Solutions to the CR Fractional Yamabe Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study bubble solutions to the critical CR fractional Yamabe equation on the Heisenberg group for the full range \(0<γ<\frac{Q}{2}\), including the admissible integer-order cases. The CR fractional operator is genuinely nonlocal and is described by Gamma-function spectral multipliers. Its structure differs from that of the Euclidean fractional Laplacian, so the linearized analysis cannot be obtained by a direct extension of integer-order arguments. We develop a direct spectral approach based on the Cayley intertwining relation and the complex spherical-harmonic decomposition, which characterizes the kernel of the linearized operator in terms of infinitesimal translation and dilation modes without reducing the equation to an integral equation or requiring a separate decay analysis. As a byproduct, we obtain the exact normalization constant of the standard bubble throughout the admissible range. We then prove three main results: $(i)$ the non-degeneracy of the bubble manifold; $(ii)$ the local rigidity of the bubble manifold, via a uniform invertibility estimate on the orthogonal complement of the tangent space, with an explicit optimal constant; $(iii)$ the Morse index of every positive bubble is exactly one. The results provide a unified spectral and variational framework for the CR Yamabe problem on the Heisenberg group, covering both integer and noninteger orders.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop a perturbative theory for minimal submanifolds with only (strongly) isolated singularities, with respect to varying background Riemannian metrics. As an application, we obtain a general "sporadic persistence" criterion, thus naturally complementing the non-persistence theorem by the authors. In particular, such a criterion is satisfied by the spherical suspension in $\mathbb{S}^{3m+2}$ of the Veronese embedding of $\mathbb{K}\mathbb{P}^2$ for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ (the normed division algebras) in the round spheres of dimension $3m+1=4,7,13,25$ respectively, thereby providing families of continuously varying $(2m+1)$-dimensional stationary varifolds with isolated singularities that are observable on an open set of metrics. By our previous results, these phenomena cannot possibly occur in the codimension one scenario.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: v2: added one item to the bibliography

Analysis of PDEs.title: The mean-field limit of non-exchangeable particle systems with non-conservative dynamics and adaptive weights
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In the paper we introduce vector-valued dynamic extended graphons in order to obtain the mean-filed limit for certain class of problems with adaptive weights. We impose fairly general assumptions on the matrix of initial connections, which allows us to cover the case of sparse graphs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A note on application of mean-field limit to non-exchangeable non-conservative systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we apply the newly developed theory of extended graphons to a certain class of non-exchangeable, non-conservative problems. We establish the mean-field limit by proving the convergence of the associated generalized weighted empirical measures.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Approximation of the relaxed Euler system at the level of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the global well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$, for the relaxed compressible Euler system with a Maxwell-type constitutive law for the stress tensor. We show that the corresponding compressible Navier-Stokes solutions serve as both relaxation limits and large-time asymptotic profiles of the global relaxed Euler solutions constructed here. Given a Navier-Stokes background satisfying suitable boundedness and decay assumptions, we construct global smooth relaxed Euler solutions for each fixed $α\in(0,1]$ and sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. Here, the background need not be small. After subtracting the stress initial layer, the approximation error is $O(\varepsilon^α)$ uniformly in time. Under suitable additional conditions on the initial perturbations, this error decays in $L^2$ faster than the decay of standard Navier-Stokes background, uniformly in $\varepsilon$, identifying the background solution as a large-time asymptotic profile. As an application, we obtain the corresponding small-data results using classical Navier-Stokes theory to verify the background assumptions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On general Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg type inequalities involving non-doubling weights in the case of $p=1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg type inequalities in the case of $p=1$ and generalize them adopting weight functions
  $w(|x|)$ on $R^n$ with $w(t)$ in ${W}(R_+)$. Here ${W}(R_+)$ is a general class of weight functions on $R_+$ including non-doubling weights like $e^{1/t}$ and $e^{-1/t}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability of the $L^p$ Poisson-Neumann problem under small perturbations of the coefficients and the domain
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this article, we obtain three stability results for the Poisson-Neumann problem: (1) the stability of the $L^p$ Poisson-Neumann problem under small Carleson perturbations of the coefficients, (2) the preservation of the $L^p$ Poisson-Neumann problem when transitioning from the Laplacian to operators in a special form with oscillations satisfying a small Carleson condition (''small special DKP operators''), and (3) the stability of the $L^p$ Poisson-Neumann problem under small bi-Lipschitz transformations of domains.
  In contrast to the Neumann problem, the Poisson-Neumann problem is notably more self-contained, as results pertaining to it do not require assumptions regarding the $L^{p'}$ Dirichlet problem, making it a more suitable object for a perturbation theory.
  As intermediate steps, we establish estimates on the square functional for solutions to the Poisson problem and their gradients on chord arc domains, which are of independent interest for specialists.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Propagation of Sobolev Regularity for Integral-Invariant Weak Solutions of the Linear Transport Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Previous work strengthened the time integrability of integral-invariant weak solutions from L^1 to L^\infty within a spatial L^2 framework.This paper studies the propagation of Sobolev regularity for integral-invariant weak solutions of the conservative linear scalar transport equation.We first derive a representation formula along the flow and a distributional equation from integral identities against adjoint-transported test functions on domains moving with the same characteristic flow,and relate the weak formulation in time, including an endpoint term for the initial data, to representatives satisfying the pointwise-in-time integral definition.We then give a unified proof for k=1,2:under u_0\in H^k(Ω_0)and Assumption \mathsf A_{k+1},the pullback of the solution belongs to C^1([0,T];H^k(Ω_0)),the material derivative has spatial $H^k$ regularity,and the Eulerian time derivative has spatial H^{k-1} regularity.The corresponding time continuity is understood after pullback to the fixed domain by the flow.In both cases, U\in H^1(Q);when k=2, we further obtain \nabla_xU\in H^1(Q;\R^d).The pullback differentiability and the spatial estimates for the material derivativeprovide information beyond first-order space-time Sobolev regularity alone.The proof combines estimates for the characteristic flow with Sobolev product and composition rules.Under the additional assumption that the zero extension of the initial data belongs to H^2(\R^d),we also establish $H^1(0,T;H^1(\R^d))$ regularity in the fixed ambient space.Counterexamples show that these results concern regularity propagation under additional assumptions: general L^2 initial data do not automatically yield spatial smoothing,and spatial regularity of the material derivative cannot replace the corresponding regularity of the Eulerian time derivative.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Godin (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface and edge waves, possibly carried by currents. Using the short-wavelength instability method for compressible flows, we show that these waves are linearly unstable above a critical steepness. The stability of each fluid level reduces to a Floquet problem depending on two parameters: the steepness $\mathfrak{e}=e^{ka_2}$ and $ν^2=(1-\mathfrak{e}^2)ν_0^2$, where $ν_0^2=\cos^2α\,N_0^2/Ω^2$, $N_0$ is the buoyancy frequency of the hydrostatic reference state, $α$ the inclination of the plane of motion and $Ω=(gk\cosα)^{1/2}$ the intrinsic orbital frequency. In an isentropic fluid, a level is unstable if $\mathfrak{e}>1/3$, recovering Leblanc's threshold for Gerstner waves (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 506, 2004, pp. 245--254) and extending it to compressible surface and edge waves; weak stable stratification lowers the threshold to $\frac13-\frac{32}{81}ν_0^2+O(ν_0^4)$. In an isothermal atmosphere, $ν_0^2=κ\cosα/(kH)$, where $H$ is the pressure scale height. For horizontal wavelengths near $5.5\,H/\cosα$, principal subharmonic resonance makes the critical steepness vanish. For the fast airglow wave observed by Hecht et al. (\textit{J. Geophys. Res.}, vol. 107, 2002, D20, 4444), which Godin interpreted with his solution, the lidar temperature places the layer in which this interpretation is consistent on this resonance, where the critical steepness is typically 0.1 instead of $1/3$. Instability is confined to a layer beneath the free surface of surface waves and to a wedge at the shoreline of edge waves.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundedness in a chemotaxis system with nonlinear diffusion and singular sensitivity
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This paper studies the following chemotaxis system with nonlinear diffusion and singular sensitivity \[ \begin{cases}
  u_t = \nabla \cdot \left( (u+a)^{m-1} \nabla u \right)
  - χ\nabla \cdot \left( u \dfrac{\nabla v}{v^k} \right), \\[4pt]
  v_t = Δv - v + u, \end{cases} \] in a smoothly bounded domain \(Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n\), \(n \geq 2\), subject to no-flux boundary conditions, where \(χ,k,a,m>0\). For suitably regular initial data, we prove global existence and uniform-in-time boundedness of classical solutions if one of the following conditions holds: \[ \begin{aligned} & n=2,\quad k\in(0,\infty),\quad m>1;\\ & n\ge 3,\quad k\in\left(0,\tfrac12\right),\quad
  m>1+\frac{(1-k)(n-2)}{n};\\ & n\ge 3,\quad k\in\left[\tfrac12,1\right),\quad
  m>\frac{3n-2}{2n};\\ & n\ge 3,\quad k\in[1,\infty),\quad
  m>\max\left\{1,\frac{3n-2}{2n+2}\right\}. \end{aligned} \] The main contribution is the physically relevant three-dimensional case. In particular, for every \(χ>0\), \(a>0\), \(m>1\) and \(k\ge 1\), the system admits a global bounded classical solution. Thus, in dimension three, nonlinear diffusion of porous-medium type removes the smallness restriction on the chemotactic sensitivity $χ$ that earlier results require in the case \(m=1\) and \(k\geq 1\).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp observation time for wave equations with an inverse-square boundary potential
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We determine the sharp observation-time threshold for the autonomous, pure-potential wave equation with an inverse-square boundary singularity on the unit ball. For every fixed $κ<0$, full-boundary observability holds on $(-T,T)$ whenever $T>1$ and fails when $T<1$. This resolves, for this model, the optimal-time question raised by Enciso, Shao, and Vergara [J. Eur. Math. Soc. 23 (2021), 3459--3495] and extends their parameter range $-\frac12<κ<0$ to all $κ<0$, including the limit-point regime $κ\leq-\frac12$.
  Our approach is based on the Ingham--Beurling theory of nonharmonic Fourier series. Spherical harmonic decomposition reduces the problem to one-dimensional singular operators, for which we establish frequency separation, local counting estimates, and lower bounds for the boundary norming constants, uniformly in the angular parameter. A quantitative Ingham--Beurling inequality then yields the sharp-time observability estimate.
  As a by-product, this spectral approach provides an independent proof of boundary observability and an explicit functional characterization of its maximal $L^2$ observation domain. The latter is described by a weighted $\ell^2$ condition on the spectral coefficients and consists precisely of energy solutions whose distributional Neumann trace belongs to $L^2$. It contains the boundary-admissible energy solutions considered in Enciso--Shao--Vergara's original work.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Singularity removal in nonlocal operator inequalities on domains and applications
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that certain classes of nonlocal integral estimates on domains, involving operators, may be reduced to the local analogues without the singular weight on cubes. The theory applies to two-sided inverse doubling and quasi-monotone kernels with some moment conditions, and with a left-hand-side operator with average domain-bi-Lipschitz properties. Direct applications to fractional semi-norm inequalities in Peridynamics, such as fractional Korn's inequalities and Geometric Rigidity Estimates are presented.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Effective interface laws for Darcy--Boussinesq convection across a vanishing low-permeability layer
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study Darcy--Boussinesq convection in a layered porous medium containing a thin layer whose thickness $h_0$ and permeability $K_0$ vanish simultaneously. The competition between these two small parameters is measured by the effective hydraulic conductance $α= \lim \frac{K_0}{h_0} \in [0,\infty]$. We show that the collapsing layer is replaced by an effective interface whose transmission law depends qualitatively on this ratio. When $α= 0$, the limiting interface is impermeable; when $ 0 <α<\infty$, the normal Darcy flux is proportional to the pressure jump, yielding a finite-resistance transmission law; and when $α=\infty$, the pressure is continuous and the interface becomes hydraulically transparent. We establish estimates uniform in the layer thickness and permeability, quantitative convergence of solutions on every finite time interval, and upper semicontinuity of the associated global attractors. The analysis has to accommodate both a degenerating geometry and a loss of coercivity in the pressure equation. In particular, we use a generalized Poincaré inequality for piecewise $H^1$ pressures, a pressure extension across the collapsing layer, and uniform thin-strip estimates. The results provide a rigorous finite- and long-time validation of effective interface models for convection through thin low-permeability interphases.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Strictly stable solutions in uniformly convex planar domains may have nonconvex superlevel sets
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct smooth, uniformly convex planar domains that admit minimal, strictly stable solutions of a semilinear Dirichlet problem whose superlevel sets are nonetheless nonconvex. The class of admissible nonlinearities includes, in particular, two prototypical cases: the Gelfand-type nonlinearity $e^u$ and the family of shifted power-type nonlinearities $(a+u)^p$, where $a>0$ and $p>1$.
