Functional Analysis.summary: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp derivative inequalities for maximal functions
Functional Analysis.summary: We determine the optimal constant in the $L^p$-derivative inequality for the uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on the real line for every $1<p<\infty$. It is the unique number $γ_p\in [0,1]$ satisfying $(2p-1)γ_p+(p-1)γ_p^{(2p-1)/(p-1)}=p$. As $p$ goes from $1$ to $+\infty$, $γ_p$ decreases from $1$ to $\sqrt2-1$, and at the endpoints the limiting arguments recover the classical total-variation and Lipschitz inequalities, with the qualitative regularity ingredient at the $BV$ endpoint supplied by Aldaz and Pérez Lázaro.

Functional Analysis.title: Locally unital $C^*$-algebras and limitations of seminorm criteria for compact operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the problem of geometric characterization of Banach-compact and $\mathcal A$-compact operators on Hilbert $C^*$-modules in terms of uniform structures generated by seminorms. Previously, such a criterion for $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators was obtained by Troitsky for countably generated range modules with a suitable system of seminorms. Using locally unital $C^*$-algebras as modules over themselves, we establish fundamental limitations of such characterizations. Namely, we show that for nonunital locally unital $C^*$-algebras not only does Troitsky's criterion fail to extend, but, more generally, no system of seminorms can characterize $\mathcal A$-precompactness by total boundedness, nor Banach-compactness of bounded operators or $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators by total boundedness of the images of the unit ball. Moreover, the same statement holds for Hilbert $C^*$-modules $\mathcal N$ whenever the algebra $\mathbf K(\mathcal N)$ of $\mathcal A$-compact operators is locally unital and nonunital. We also study Troitsky-type systems of seminorms and their relation to $\mathcal A$-precompactness. We prove that every $\mathcal A$-precompact subset is totally bounded with respect to the strongest of such structures. Consequently, for Hilbert $C^*$-modules admitting a standard frame, all the corresponding notions of total boundedness coincide.

Functional Analysis.title: Convergence of Levenberg--Marquardt method in Banach spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the Levenberg--Marquardt method for nonlinear inverse problems in Banach spaces under a Hölder stability estimate. Under suitable assumptions on the geometry of the Banach space and the Fréchet derivative of the measurement operator, we establish the well-definedness of the method, local convergence and convergence rates for exact data, and the monotonic decrease of the Bregman distance up to the stopping index for noisy data. These results extend the corresponding Hilbert space theory to the Banach space setting.

Functional Analysis.title: Embeddings of variable Sobolev, Besov, and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces on metric measure spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Sobolev-type embeddings on metric measure spaces encode a subtle interaction between the analytic regularity of functions and the geometry of the underlying domain space. In this paper we develop an embedding theory for variable Hajłasz-type smoothness spaces on metric measure spaces whose ``dimension'' is allowed to vary pointwise through a bounded exponent $Q(\cdot)$ that governs a lower Ahlfors growth condition on the measure. We introduce variable exponent Hajłasz-Sobolev spaces $M^{s(\cdot),p(\cdot)}$, Hajłasz-Triebel-Lizorkin spaces $M^{s(\cdot)}_{p(\cdot),q(\cdot)}$, and Hajłasz-Besov spaces $N^{s(\cdot)}_{p(\cdot),q(\cdot)}$, and establish Sobolev, Morrey, and Moser-Trudinger type embeddings into variable exponent Lebesgue and Hölder spaces. These embeddings are proved both locally (on balls) under a lower Ahlfors $Q(\cdot)$-regularity condition on the measure and regularity assumptions on the exponents (notably log-Hölder continuity), and globally under additional geometric hypotheses such as geometric doubling and mild uniform bounds on the measure of unit balls. We also identify geometric conditions that are not only sufficient but, in appropriate forms, necessary for the validity of these embeddings, showing in particular that such inequalities force a lower growth bound on the measure of order $r^{Q(x)}$.

Functional Analysis.title: Additive preservers of mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with $\dim H\ge2$. We show that the additive surjections on $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and on its self-adjoint part $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$ that preserve mutual strong numerical-radius orthogonality in one direction are precisely the maps of the form $A\mapsto cUAU^*$, where $U$ is a unitary or antiunitary operator on $H$ and $c$ is a nonzero complex or real scalar, respectively.

Functional Analysis.title: Bounds on non-hermite Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information
Functional Analysis.summary: We obtain the relation between non-hermite skew information $NI_{ρ,α}(A)$, $NU_{ρ,α}(A)$, variance $NV_ρ(A)$ and $NJ_{ρ,α}(A)$ by using the maximal eigenvalue and the minimal eigenvalue of density $ρ$. And also we obtain their refinements.

Functional Analysis.title: Linear Rank Nonincreasing and Preserving Maps between Matrix Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We classify linear maps $φ$ between possibly different rectangular matrix spaces over a field $\mathbb F$ with $|\mathbb F|\ge5$ such that $\operatorname{rank} φ(A)\le2$ whenever $\operatorname{rank} A\le2$. Every such map has one of six forms. If its image contains a matrix of rank greater than two, then $φ(A)=MAN$ or $φ(A)=MA^{\top}N$ for fixed matrices $M,N$. The remaining forms have images consisting entirely of matrices of rank at most two, including an exceptional form arising from $3\times3$ alternating matrices. As a consequence, we characterize linear maps preserving rank exactly two. We also prove that rank-$k$ preservation implies rank-$k$ nonincrease when $|\mathbb F|>k+2$, and that rank-$k$ nonincrease implies rank-$\ell$ nonincrease for every admissible $\ell\ge k$ when $|\mathbb F|>k+1$. The classification uses the fact that the Chow rank of the generic $3\times3$ determinant is five, connecting the rank preserver problem with product decompositions of polynomials.

Functional Analysis.title: Non-Asymptotic Stability and Consistency Guarantees for Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coercive Operator Analysis
Functional Analysis.summary: We present a unified theoretical framework for analyzing the stability and consistency of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), grounded in operator coercivity, variational formulations, and non-asymptotic perturbation theory. PINNs approximate solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs) by minimizing residual losses over sampled collocation and boundary points. We formalize both operator-level and variational notions of consistency, proving that residual minimization in Sobolev norms leads to convergence in energy and uniform norms under mild regularity. Deterministic stability bounds quantify how bounded perturbations to the network outputs propagate through the full composite loss, while probabilistic concentration results via McDiarmid's inequality yield sample complexity guarantees for residual-based generalization. A unified generalization bound links residual consistency, projection error, and perturbation sensitivity. Empirical results on elliptic, parabolic, and nonlinear PDEs confirm the predictive accuracy of our theoretical bounds across regimes. The framework identifies key structural principles, such as operator coercivity, activation smoothness, and sampling admissibility, that underlie robust and generalizable PINN training, offering principled guidance for the design and analysis of PDE-informed learning systems.
Functional Analysis.comment: arXiv admin note: This submission has been withdrawn because it does not meet arXiv's research content quality standards

Functional Analysis.title: Simple proofs of a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality and their extensions
Functional Analysis.summary: We revisit the one-dimensional Gagliardo-Nirenberg interpolation inequality $$\|u'\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R})}\leq C\|u\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R})}^{1-a}\|u''\|_{L^r(\mathbb{R})}^{a},\qquad u\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}),\quad \tfrac12\leq a\leq 1,$$ and recall how its general form follows from the case $a=\frac12$ by interpolation with an endpoint estimate. For $a=\frac12$ and $p=q=r$, we give four alternative proofs, based on integration by parts (two proofs), on an ODE, and on the $L^p$ theory of singular integrals. The two proofs by integration by parts also cover most of the other admissible exponents. In $\mathbb{R}^N$, the integration by parts arguments give the inequality with explicit constants and, for $p\leq 2$, with the Laplacian in place of the Hessian and a constant independent of the dimension. For weighted measures $w(x)\,dx$, a pointwise version of the ODE argument gives the pointwise inequality $|\nabla u|^2\leq C_N\,Mu\,M(Δu)$, where $M$ is the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function, and hence the inequality for Muckenhoupt weights, with the Laplacian and an explicit constant. The integration by parts arguments give it for homogeneous weights of large degree and for superharmonic weights. These results apply, in particular, to power weights and to monomial weights.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp convex body sparse bounds and quantitative matrix weighted estimates for Hilbert transforms along curves
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove convex body sparse bounds for coordinatewise Hilbert transforms along monomial curves and local $C^d$ curves with uniformly nonvanishing torsion on the closed integration interval. Adapting the scalar estimates of Cladek--Ou \cite{CladekOu2018} and the lifting method of Laukkarinen--Lorist \cite{LaukkarinenLorist2026} to the anisotropic geometry, we obtain one sparse family of genuine curve-adapted boxes and quantitative $L^p(W)$ bounds for matrix weights. The convex body sparse exponent range is sharp up to its boundary: estimates hold in the interior of $Ω_d$, while any fixed finite number of sparse families fails outside $\overline{Ω_d}$ when $1/r+1/s>1$. We also establish an explicit endpoint-contact obstruction. For every interior planar exponent pair, a polynomial curve with positive torsion on the open integration interval violates the full-interval sparse estimate.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Optimal Decay Exponents for Fractional Burgers Rarefaction Waves
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish decay estimates toward rarefaction waves for the one-dimensional fractional Burgers equation when the order of dissipation lies between one and two. The initial data are bounded, and their perturbation from the Riemann step belongs to the critical weak-Lorentz space determined by scaling; the perturbation need not be small or integrable. We obtain optimal algebraic decay exponents, improving the known decay rates, and extending convergence to every Lebesgue space above the critical exponent, including the supremum norm. We prove optimality by constructing a single solution with Riemann step initial data whose lower decay estimates have exactly the same algebraic exponents as our upper estimates. These lower bounds establish that neither the algebraic decay exponents nor the range of convergence can be improved under the stated assumptions. The upper estimates contain a logarithmic factor whose necessity remains open. The proof combines convex truncation estimates, fractional interpolation, and a one-sided slope estimate for the supremum norm.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
The thin-film equation describes the evolution of a thin liquid film driven by capillarity and limited by viscosity. For sufficiently small film heights, thermal fluctuations may not be neglected. Since the thin-film equation as an overdamped evolution equation has a gradient flow structure, the informal implementation of the fluctuation-dissipation principle is straightforward. In this paper, we work out that the concept of Dirichlet forms and the related construction of Markov processes are tailor-made for this type of overdamped continuum evolution with thermal noise. However, the concept of Dirichlet forms relies on the availability of a Gibbsian equilibrium measure, which, in case of the thin-film equation, limits the treatment to the $(1+1)$-dimensional case.
  By means of Dirichlet form theory, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of the evolution of laws on configuration space. We show that the regularity of the realizations of this Markov process matches the heuristics. In a simplified situation with a Gaussian reference measure and a non-degenerate mobility function, we characterize it as what is called an energy solution. The latter provides a pathwise decomposition of the driving forces into a deterministic and a thermal one, which was the starting point.
  Applying the same techniques in the spatially discretized setting proposed in [Math. Comp. 92 (2023), 1931--1976], we obtain the same results uniformly in the discretization parameter. In particular, Galerkin as well as spectral approximations of the stochastic thin-film equation are shown to be uniformly tight in optimal topologies. In the simplified setting, we also prove Mosco convergence of the associated Dirichlet forms and thereby obtain convergence of these approximations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Lane-Emden equation for the superposition of a local and nonlocal operator with the "wrong sign"
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the Lane-Emden equation associated with the operator $-Δ- γ\, (-Δ)^s$ (for positive $γ$). First we consider the equation in the entire space and we prove that no Serrin-type critical exponent arises in the $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$ framework. Secondly we consider the problem settled in an open, bounded and connected set and we prove the existence of a positive solution for sufficiently small $s$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large-Time Upper Decay Estimates for Weakly Coupled Time-Fractional Diffusion Systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove conjectured-optimal large-time upper decay estimates for solutions of weakly coupled systems of $m\ge2$ time-fractional diffusion equations. Our result establishes the upper-bound assertion in the conjecture of Li, Liu, and Wada~\cite{LLW26}. The sharpness of these upper exponents for $m\ge3$ remains open in general; see Section~\ref{sec:discussion}.
  Assume that the diffusion matrices are uniformly elliptic, the coupling coefficients are bounded and may depend on time, and the matrix of $L^\infty$-norms of the coupling coefficients satisfies a spectral-radius stability condition. Let $α^*$ denote the smallest fractional order among the components with nonzero initial data. Then the $L^2(Ω)^m$-norm of the solution is $O(t^{-α^*})$ as $t\to\infty$ if $α^*<1$, whereas it is $O(t^{-(1+α_m)})$ if $α^*=1$, where $α_m$ is the smallest fractional order occurring in the system. For $m=2$, the result yields the same upper decay exponents as \cite[Theorem~1.1]{LLW26}; in the absence of self-coupling, the matrix stability condition is weaker than the corresponding small-coupling condition in that work. The case $m\ge3$ is new.
  Our proof uses a large-time weighted Volterra framework. If $α^*<1$, the weight is a regularly varying power weight; if $α^*=1$, it is constructed by convolution with the resolvent kernel associated with the smallest fractional order. These weights yield the required large-time bounds for all resolvent kernels in the system. In particular, the argument avoids the Laplace-transform and residue-calculus methods used in \cite{LLW26}, which become difficult to implement for systems with three or more components.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Traveling waves near shear flows for the inhomogeneous Euler equations with non-constant density
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the existence and nonexistence of traveling wave solutions near monotonic shear flows with non-constant background density for the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Euler equations in a finite channel. For any small $τ>0$, first, we construct nontrivial traveling waves with velocity and density in $H^{5/2-τ}$ and $H^{3/2-τ}$, respectively, showing that inviscid damping fails at these regularities. Second, when the distorted Rayleigh operator has no eigenvalues, we prove that such traveling wave solutions cannot exist in higher regularity spaces ($H^{5/2+τ}$ for velocity and $H^{3/2+τ}$ for density).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Inverse source problem for the stochastic fractional Helmholtz equation in inhomogeneous media
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is concerned with an inverse source problem for the stochastic fractional Helmholtz equation in a three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is modeled as real Gaussian spatial white noise with an unknown nonnegative strength function. For admissible frequencies, we establish well-posedness of the radiating solution in the distributional sense and show that it has a smooth representation outside the source region. For the inverse problem, by using two-point correlations of the field measured in an exterior open set at a single frequency, we prove a logarithmic stability estimate for recovering the source strength under an a priori Sobolev bound. As a uniform Hölder stability estimate is unavailable for the general admissible class, by assuming the difference between two source strengths has a fixed sign, we improve the stability to Hölder continuity with an optimal Hölder exponent. The analysis combines scattering theory and quantitative continuation for the fractional Laplacian using the Caffarelli-Silvestre extension.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and uniqueness of the dual solution for obstacle problems in the space BV
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the variational problem of minimizing the multiple integral $\int_Ωf(\nabla u) \, dx$ with a convex density $f$ being of linear growth among functions $u$: $Ω\to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the Dirichlet boundary condition $u = u_0$ on $\partialΩ$ and for which $u \ge Ψ$ holds throughout the domain $Ω$. We prove that the dual problem has a unique solution. This result is extended to the case of interior obstacle problems, where the validity of $u \ge Ψ$ is only required on a subset $E$ of $Ω$. Moreover, we discuss the vectorial setting, i.e. the case of functions $u$: $Ω\to \mathbb{R}^N$, $N > 1$, combined with the additional condition $u(Ω) \subset A$ for a closed convex set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^N$, again showing the existence and the uniqueness of the associated dual solution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fractional Differential Equations in Chemical Modeling: From Memory and Anomalous Transport to Mathematically Justified Models
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Fractional differential equations are increasingly used to model memory and anomalous transport in chemistry and related fields. However, the formal replacement of an integer-order derivative by a fractional one does not by itself justify fractional dynamics. The essential issue is whether nonlocality can be derived from a physical, stochastic, geometric, or reduction mechanism and whether it leads to experimentally testable consequences.
  This review, written primarily for mathematicians and specialists in fractional analysis, discusses representative applications in electrochemistry, adsorption and sorption, reaction--subdiffusion, chemical and enzyme kinetics, polymer relaxation, and atmospheric chemistry. Particular attention is paid to distinguishing mechanism-based fractional models from phenomenological fractionalizations.
  Mathematical questions of well-posedness, nonnegativity, conservation laws, dimensional consistency, parameter identifiability, and numerical convergence are emphasized. Experimental electrochemical examples illustrate the need to distinguish genuine fractional effects from model mismatch or non-identifiability. Several open problems connecting fractional analysis with experimentally grounded chemical modeling are formulated.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical curl extremals and the hyperbolic plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the critical Sobolev-curl quotient on $\mathbb{R}^3$ at the conformally invariant exponent $p=3/2$. Its sharp constant and optimizers were posed as open problems in the literature. We identify the toroidal and poloidal extremals. Two structural facts are used. First, the critical curl--curl equation is self-dual: the map $u\mapsto|\nabla\times u|^{-1/2}\nabla\times u$ is an involution on finite-energy solutions. It is the self-dual case of a duality between the exponents $p$ and $3p/(4p-3)$, which exchanges toroidal and poloidal fields and relates the sharp constants. Second, the toroidal minimization problem reduces exactly to a subcritical $3/2$-Laplace problem on the hyperbolic plane. Combined with symmetry and shooting results, these facts show that the two restricted sharp constants coincide. They also classify the gauge-minimal extremals: these are unique up to scaling and the Euclidean transformations realizing hyperbolic isometries, semi-explicit, and dual to each other. For nonzero one-signed profiles radial about a fixed hyperbolic centre, a gauge-canonical inverse of the duality yields an iteration by one-dimensional quadratures: the quotients are nonincreasing and converge to the restricted sharp constant, while the normalized iterates converge to the extremal pair. The first step from an explicit competitor gives the new upper bound $96\sqrt{15}π/(5\sqrt{4455π-13568})\approx11.2948$ for the restricted constants. The unrestricted sharp constant remains open. As an application, bounded axisymmetric poloidal potentials admit no $L^2$ zero mode of the Weyl-Dirac operator. An explicit conformal transformation extends this exclusion to both extremals at every real coupling.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Morse theory and topological degree for resonant mean field equations on Riemann surfaces with boundary
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we establish Morse theory for the Neumann mean field equation on a compact Riemann surface at $ρ=4πm$, $m\in\mathbb N$. To address the loss of compactness associated with bubbling, we use Bahri's theory of critical points at infinity. Assume that the reduced functionals are Morse and that the leading scale coefficient does not vanish at their critical points. We classify the critical points at infinity arising from interior, boundary, and mixed concentration, compute their Morse indices and local relative homology, and establish deformation lemmas at resonance. We prove that, for $m\geq 2$, every sufficiently negative sublevel is homotopy equivalent to the boundary-weighted barycenter space of order $m-1$. The Euler--Poincaré identity gives the Leray--Schauder degree at resonance without assuming nondegeneracy of the solutions. If all solutions are nondegenerate, we further obtain strong Morse inequalities with explicit Betti numbers over $\mathbb Z_2$. As a consequence, we obtain existence and multiplicity results, as well as criteria for solutions with prescribed Morse index.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Effective threshold dynamics for the cubic nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in three dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the focussing cubic Klein-Gordon equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$ in the radial setting. Foundational work by Nakanishi-Schlag gives a complete qualitative characterisation of the dynamics near the ground state $Q$, in particular revealing a threshold phenomenon, whereby a co-dimension one Lipschitz manifold separates finite time blow up from scattering solutions in forward time. Our aim in this paper is to derive an effective bound for the scattering norm $\|u\|_{L_t^3([0,\infty);L_x^6(\mathbb{R}^3))}$, for scattering energy class solutions $u$ with data sufficiently near $Q$ and close to the threshold manifold. This requires the development of an induction on energy strategy in a setting where an alternative to the usual Morawetz approach appears necessary.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Preconditioned Quantum Linear Solver for Periodic Two-Phase Heat Conduction with Mesh-Independent Condition Number
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We consider here computational homogenization of a periodic two-phase conduction problem. Quantum linear-system algorithms for its finite element discretization are limited by the condition number of the stiffness matrix. This condition number grows quadratically with the number of elements per side. Classically, preconditioning by the homogeneous (single-phase) operator bounds the condition number by the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size. On a quantum computer, however, a preconditioner encoded as a separate factor multiplies the subnormalizations, and the quadratic dependency returns.
  In this paper, we absorb the closed-form inverse square root of the homogeneous operator into the finite element factors. The preconditioned operator then becomes the product of a norm-preserving gradient operator $\mat{V}$, a diagonal matrix of scaled conductivities, and $\mat{V}^T$. Each factor has norm at most one. The block encoding therefore has subnormalization one, and its condition number is bounded by just the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size and in every dimension. The operator $\mat{V}$ is applied as a quantum Fourier transform, a small rotation at each wavenumber, and an inverse transform. Quantum singular value transformation then block-encodes the inverse of the preconditioned operator.
  We test the method numerically on three periodic cells with up to $10^6$ unknowns. The results confirm that the condition number does not depend on the mesh, and the energy-norm error of the inverse is below the polynomial tolerance at every mesh. On meshes of $4 \times 4$ and $8 \times 8$ elements, we also build the entire inverse as one Qiskit circuit and simulate it by state vector, with the rotation at each wavenumber built from uniformly controlled rotations. The output state agrees with the finite element solution to within the polynomial tolerance.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Inviscid limit for the hyperbolic Keller--Segel equations in $B_{\infty,1}^{1}$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the inviscid limit for the hyperbolic Keller--Segel equations with logistic sensitivity $1-u$. We establish a common existence time and a priori estimates uniform with respect to the diffusion coefficient in the critical Besov spaces $B_{p,1}^{1+d/p}(R^d)$ with $1\le p\le\infty$. For $1<p<\infty$, we obtain explicit convergence rates in $B_{p,1}^{0}$, and we also give estimates for the case $p=1$. For initial data in $B_{\infty,1}^{1}$, we prove convergence at rate $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ in $L^\infty$, a bound of order $O(\varepsilon^{1/2}\log(e/\varepsilon))$ in $B_{\infty,1}^{0}$, and strong convergence in $L^\infty(0,T;B_{\infty,1}^{1})$. Additional regularity of the initial data yields improved convergence rates. We construct a fixed initial datum showing that the exponent $1/2$ in $L^\infty$ is optimal.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Mean First-Reaction Time on a Thin Filament in a 3-D Domain
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the mean first-reaction time (MFRT) of a Brownian particle in a bounded three-dimensional domain $Ω$ with a reflecting boundary $\partialΩ$, that contains a thin reactive filament. The filament is a tube of cross-sectional diameter $\varepsilon\ll 1$ around a smooth closed curve $Γ$, and its surface is partially reactive with reactivity $b$. As $\varepsilon\to 0$ the filament reduces to a line source in the outer problem. Its cross-section enters only through a logarithmic reactive capacitance $d_c(b)$, so that the MFRT is O$(-\log[\varepsilon d_c])$. This contrasts with the $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ scaling for spatially localized traps of radius $\varepsilon$. Using matched asymptotic expansions, we derive a Fredholm integral equation on $Γ$ for the line density of the reactive flux. It sums all powers of $ν\equiv -1/\log[\varepsilon d_c]$ and involves two geometric quantities: the regular part $R$ of the Neumann Green's function, which encodes the interaction of $Γ$ with $\partialΩ$, and an intrinsic self-energy of $Γ$ that depends only on its shape. The framework extends to multiple filaments, splitting probabilities, a spatially heterogeneous diffusivity, and the principal eigenvalue of the Laplacian. For the unit sphere we solve the integral equation with a simple trapezoidal Nyström scheme, and we validate the predictions for rings, linked rings and torus knots against full 3-D finite-element solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Spectral theory for transmission problems and resonances for transparent balls
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct generalized eigenfunctions and a spectral calculus for the transmission problem on Lipschitz domains. Then, focusing on the specific example of the ball, we prove a high-frequency resonance dichotomy for Maxwell's equations for a ball with positive, piecewise constant permittivity and permeability. If the product of these coefficients is no larger inside the ball than outside, the cutoff resolvent extends holomorphically to a strip of fixed width below the real axis, including the case of equal products. If the interior product is larger, we construct whispering-gallery resonances exponentially close to the real axis. The proofs use estimates for the transverse electric and transverse magnetic determinants that are uniform in angular momentum and complex frequency, together with a quasimode construction and Rouché's theorem. Explicit generalized eigenfunctions identify these determinants with the scattering poles and give the spectral resolution and the normalization relating the scattering amplitude to the Mie T-matrix.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global existence and uniqueness of Lions' weak solutions for the 2D inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations in bounded domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The global well-posedness for Lions' weak solutions to the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in two-dimensional bounded domains is concerned. When the initial density $0\leq ρ_0\in L^\infty(\Om)$ (allowing for vacuum) and initial velocity $u_0\in L^2_σ(Ω)$, the global existence, regularity, and exponential decay-in-time rates of weak solutions are established via a priori estimates, which rely crucially on the duality of BMO and Hardy space for the pressure term, and the classical Sobolev extension theorem. In particular, for the non-vacuous case where $0< ρ_0\in L^\infty(\Om)$ is bounded away from zero, we further prove the uniqueness of weak solutions in the sense of approximation by strong solutions, based on the key estimate \(t^{1/2}\nabla u\in L^2(0,T;L^\infty(Ω))\), which essentially follows from a delicate localized point-wise bound for \(\nabla u\) near the boundary. The latter bound is derived by the Green functions estimate for the nonhomogeneous Dirichlet Stokes problem, and the uniform \(C^1\) boundary estimate on the remaining homogeneous Stokes problem, through a Stokes decomposition on suitably constructed local \(C^2\) domains.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary stabilization of a moving interface in a 2 x 2 weakly hyperbolic system of balance laws: application to continuous sedimentation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We design a boundary feedback for the level of the sediment bed of a continuous settler and prove that it exponentially stabilizes the linearized closed loop under a small-gain condition. The unit is modeled by a 2 x 2 system of balance laws in which the bed surface, the interface, is not a smooth part of the solution but a moving shock between a weakly hyperbolic free-settling zone and a strictly hyperbolic compression zone. We describe it by the Rankine-Hugoniot relations and map the problem onto a fixed domain. Moreover, we prove local well-posedness with a continuation criterion given by a single margin function. Then we linearize the system near an equilibrium. The linearization couples a dissipative distributed layer to one scalar, the interface position, whose equation does not contain the control. We solve this by infinitedimensional forwarding: a Sylvester kernel cancels the interface trace and isolates the interface pole, and a proportional feedback then sets its decay rate. Every hypothesis is verified on an illustrative example, a laboratory-scale continuous settler containing a bed of compact polystyrene beads.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(β+1)}/β}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $β^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\logβ$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $β$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale flocking dynamics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Flocking refers to a phenomenon in collective motion where particles align their velocities with each other, commonly modelled using Cucker-Smale dynamics. In this work, we introduce and analyse two general reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale particle dynamics that encompass environmental and i.i.d.-type noises. Our models are computationally cheaper alternatives to the underlying particle system and preserve the flocking behaviour. To derive our reduced models, we consider suitable empirical particle densities which depend on position and time, but feature velocity dependency in a multiplicative fashion: this setup crucially allows for a very intuitive and convenient notion of flocking at the SPDE level. In $d=1$ we prove flocking of the reduced SPDE models, and, for the environmental noise, we also quantify the discrepancy between the reduced SPDE and mollified particle system. We also discuss the technical modifications required to extend the results to higher dimensions. We then provide extensive numerical experiments to verify our theoretical results in $d=1$ and to explore the behaviour of our models in $d=2$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The virial--Kato method and the asymptotic stability of solitons of the generalized Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We apply to the generalized pure power Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation our method of combining high energy virial estimates with Kato smoothing, which closes the virial estimates in a natural way and allows us to prove a result of asymptotic stability for all the stable solitons with $c>1$ for all the exponents $p>1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Blow-up suppression for the 2D parabolic-parabolic Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Chemotactic aggregation can overcome diffusion and lead to finite-time blow-up in Patlak-Keller-Segel models. Mixing induced by suitable fluid flows can counteract this aggregation through enhanced dissipation. Earlier results of Zeng-Zhang-Zi (J. Funct. Anal., 2021) for the coupled system impose additional smallness assumptions on the initial chemical gradient. A natural question is whether this restriction can be removed for the coupled system near a stationary Couette flow. We give a positive answer to this question for the two-dimensional parabolic-parabolic Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system near the Couette flow $(Ay,0)$ in $\mathbb T\times\mathbb R$. It is proved that, when the Couette flow is strong enough ($A$ is large enough), the system admits a global solution that remains uniformly bounded in time for arbitrary fixed initial data. The main difficulties are the transient growth of the chemical gradient and the nonlinear coupling among the density, chemical field and fluid. We develop a two-stage energy method combining short-time estimates in Kelvin coordinates with long-time estimates in physical coordinates. The key is to split the nonzero chemical modes into two parts while accounting for the nonlinear transport. One part carries the initial data, and the other is a forced component with zero initial data. A weighted coupled energy controls the former through a time-integrable Gronwall coefficient and absorbs the feedback from the latter without increasing the initial energy. Enhanced dissipation then provides the bounds needed to enter the long-time regime, while one-dimensional zero-mode estimates and Moser iteration complete the argument without a mass restriction.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An Onsager-type theorem for the compressible Euler equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
For any $0\leqγ_m<\frac13$ and $0\leqγ_ρ<\frac23$,, we use convex integration to construct a nontrivial weak solution $(ρ,m)$ to the three-dimensional isentropic compressible Euler equations such that $ρ-ρ^*\in C^{γ_ρ}(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}^3)$ and $m\in C^{γ_m}(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}^3)$. Here $ρ^*>0$ is a constant, and the density stays bounded away from vacuum. Both $ρ-ρ^*$ and $m$ have compact support in time. The construction applies to smooth pressure laws with positive derivative throughout the density range. This yields nonuniqueness for the constant initial data $(ρ^*,0)$.
  Each stage of the convex integration scheme consists of finitely many Newton steps followed by a Nash step. Kirchhoff's formula in Lagrangian coordinates and the Piola transform yield coupled density and momentum corrections that treat the acoustic part of the linearized system while preserving the continuity equation exactly. In the Newton step, we combine these corrections with an incompressible correction adapted from Giri--Radu (2024) to reduce the error. In the Nash step, a divergence-free perturbation built from spatially separated Mikado flows treats the gluing stresses on disjoint time intervals without changing the density.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Integrate-and-Fire model with superlinear drift
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The Nonlinear Integrate-and-Fire equation is a fundamental model for neural assemblies, describing the dynamics of the density of neurons with a given potential. Its standard formulation uses a given firing potential, and is known to undergo finite-time blow-up for excitatory connections. To fit experimental observations, it has been advocated to use superlinear drifts. We show how, in this situation, it makes sense to set the equation on the whole line. The main question we address is whether in these circumstances the solution still exhibits finite-time blow-up. We study the construction of solutions by a fixed point and, using the framework of \cite{carrilloQualitativePropertiesSolutions2015}, we develop novel a priori estimates which use specifically the superlinearity of the drift at $+\infty$. In particular, we obtain Ces{à}ro-mean bounds on the activity, as well as exponential convergence towards the unique steady state in the weakly connected regime. Several critical steps rely on controls depending solely on the $L^1$ norm of the solution or coefficients.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantum Velocity Averaging (or Not...) in the Semiclassical Regime
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper discusses the possibility of applying the velocity averaging theorems in [F. Golse, P.-L. Lions, B. Perthame, R. Sentis: J. Funct. Anal. 76(1):110--125, 1988] to the Wigner equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of quantum density operators. Our first main results address the case of the Wigner function of a special class of density operators associated to mixed states, whose Hilbert-Schmidt norm is of order $\hbar^{d/2}$, where $d$ is the space dimension and $\hbar$ the reduced Planck constant. In space dimension $d=1$, we prove that the density function belongs to the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb R)$ for some $s>0$. In the case of pure states, we first obtain a characterization of the Wigner transform of rank-one quantum density operators, and apply this characterization (1) to analyze a rather general setting in which velocity averaging cannot apply to the Wigner functions of a family of rank-one density operators whose evolution is governed by the von Neumann equation, and (2) to obtain a quick derivation of Madelung's system of quantum hydrodynamic equations. This derivation provides a physical explanation of one key assumption used in the proof of the negative result (1) described above.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A lower bound for the stability constant in the Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality
Finite-energy travelling waves for the easy-plane Landau-Lifshitz equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every integer $d\ge2$ and every subsonic speed $c\in(0,1)$, we construct a nonconstant finite-energy travelling wave for the easy-plane Landau-Lifshitz equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$. This addresses the existence problem raised in the numerical work of Papanicolaou and Spathis. The profiles satisfy the travelling-wave equation in the sense of distributions and are smooth in dimension two.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Structural identifiability of partially-observed stochastic processes: from single-particle trajectories to total particle density data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The increasing availability of experimental data has intensified interest in calibrating stochastic models, raising fundamental questions about parameter identifiability. Structural identifiability determines whether parameters can be uniquely recovered from idealised data, a prerequisite to allow for parameter estimation in real-world scenarios. However, there is a lack of methodologies generally applicable to analyse the structural identifiability of such stochastic processes. Therefore, we develop a methodology for a class of spatio-temporal stochastic processes. We investigate how structural identifiability depends on the type of available data, distinguishing between single-particle trajectories and total particle density measurements. For trajectory data, we use a particle-based description that explicitly represents single-particle dynamics. For population-level data, we derive a partial differential equation representation, that describes the evolution of total particle density, and apply a differential algebra approach, common to ordinary differential equation analysis. We further introduce Taylor-series-expansion and Fourier-transform approaches to study the initial condition. We apply our methodology to an example model with a specified class of initial conditions. We show that the model is globally structurally identifiable given infinitely many, infinitely long single-particle trajectories, but only locally structurally identifiable from total particle density data, demonstrating that parameter identifiability depends on the type of data available.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Main: 34 pages, 3 figures. Supplementary Information: 17 pages, 5 figures

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Sharp Sobolev Inequality on Compact CR Manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
For any \(n\geq 1\), let \((M,θ)\) be a compact strictly pseudoconvex hypersurface type CR manifold with dimension \(2n+1\), \(Q=2n+2\) be its homogeneous dimension. We prove the sharp Folland--Stein Sobolev inequality on \(M\): if \(Q^*=2Q/(Q-2)\), then there exists a constant \(A>0\), depending only on \((M,θ)\), such that
  \[
  \|u\|_{L^{Q^*}(M)}^2 \le K(n)^2\|\nabla_b u\|_{L^2(M)}^2 + A\|u\|_{L^2(M)}^2, \qquad u\in S^{1,2}(M).
  \]
  Here \(K(n)\) is the sharp constant in the Folland--Stein Sobolev inequality on the Heisenberg group \(\mathbb H^n\).

Analysis of PDEs.title: On Nonlocal Equations under Symmetries
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we establishes results of existence and regularity for solutions to nonlocal equations of the form $f(Δ)u = U(x,u(x)) ~\text{and}~f(Δ_{g})u=U(x,u(x))$ in the Euclidean context and Riemannian context respectively. We extend the results of \cite{Gorka 6} for the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ under cylindrically symmetry and compact Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ under action of a closed Lie subgroup $G \leq \text{Isom}_{g}(M)$. Our approach combines spectral theory, complex interpolation and fixed-point methods.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Eigenvalue bounds for quantum dot Dirac operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We exploit the connection between quantum dot Dirac operators and $\overline\partial$-Robin Laplacians. First, we find a graphical relation between their smallest positive eigenvalues, which allows us to deduce a recipe for translating bounds (from above and below) from one to the other. As an application, we provide new upper and lower bounds for the eigenvalues of the quantum dot Dirac operators, which depend only on geometric quantities of the underlying domain. In particular, we obtain some Faber-Krahn type inequalities for convex thin domains.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 20 pages, 3 figures. v2: added a Note before Section 1.1 discussing a proof of Dirac-Faber-Krahn that appeared during the peer review process of this work

Analysis of PDEs.title: Integral Harnack-type estimates and the rate of extinction for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish local boundedness and integral Harnack-type inequalities for locally nonnegative weak solutions to nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations in the fast diffusion range by combining refined energy estimates with a careful treatment of the nonlocal terms. As an application, quantitative decay estimates for both the local mass and the local supremum of weak solutions are derived near the extinction time. Furthermore, we study the extinction phenomenon for bounded nonnegative weak solutions to the Cauchy--Dirichlet problem and obtain quantitative upper bounds for the extinction time.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Exponential stability of port-Hamiltonian systems with unstructured, measurable Hamiltonian densities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For first-order port-Hamiltonian systems in the dissipative setting considered here, we characterise exponential stability without any further regularity or block-structure assumption on the Hamiltonian density, thus closing a gap persisting in the literature. The proof requires revisiting the computation of the adjoint generator of the port-Hamiltonian semigroup. Finally, we provide both examples and non-examples showcasing the inconclusiveness of known conditions on the Hamiltonian densities necessary for the application of characterisation results in the literature.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence, Equivalence, and Convergence of Unbalanced Optimal Transport
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study an unbalanced optimal transport problem with a spatially independent signed source. The target density is continuous on a bounded domain or continuous and integrable on $\mathbb R^n$. We establish sequential weak lower semicontinuity at the critical Sobolev regularity $W^{1,n}$ and existence of minimizers under prescribed distortion and Jacobian mass bounds, provided a finite-energy admissible pair exists. For domain-preserving, uniformly bi-Lipschitz affine flows, we prove an energy-preserving static-dynamic correspondence and stability of the reconstruction. Within this class, sequential $Γ$-convergence identifies the strong source-penalty limit as transport minimization among pairs of minimum source cost. This yields optimal-cost asymptotics and subsequential convergence of minimizers and their reconstructed paths. When a constant source is admissible, optimal sources converge strongly in $L^2$ to the constant determined by the endpoint mass difference. We establish local constant-source feasibility for Hölder endpoint densities near a fixed reference pair and give a quantitative obstruction showing that constant-source feasibility may fail even when admissible pairs exist.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Wave Selection at an $O(2)$-Hopf Bifurcation in Conservative Two-Component PDE Systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: At an $O(2)$-equivariant Hopf bifurcation a spatially periodic system selects between traveling waves and standing waves, and which branch appears and whether it is stable is decided by two cubic normal form coefficients. Obtaining these coefficients for a given PDE has required a derivation carried out afresh for each model. We remove that step for two-component systems with conservative polynomial differential nonlinearities on a one-dimensional periodic domain, deriving closed form formulas for both coefficients. They are expressed directly in terms of the array of nonlinear PDE coefficients and the spectral data of the linearization, its critical eigenvectors, adjoint eigenvectors, and non-critical resolvents. We give verifiable conditions under which the underlying center manifold reduction is valid. A structural condition on the principal part of the linearization, together with sign conditions on the trace and determinant of its Fourier symbol, yields the resolvent estimate and the spectral gap that the reduction requires. A companion implementation evaluates the two normal form coefficients from the coefficient array and verifies the assumptions for a given system. We specialize the formulas to two applications: a strain-gradient regularization of the nonlinear $p$-system, whose quadratic case contains a previously studied model as a special case, and a first order conservative bilinear family, not previously analyzed, in which every bifurcation scenario allowed by the general classification is realized.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 26 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Revised version: proofs and references updated, shortened. Submitted to Zeitschrift für angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global well-posedness and asymptotic behavior of large strong solutions to the 3D full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary: It is well known that the global well-posedness of the Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients is a challenging problem, especially in multi-dimensional space. In this paper, we study the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients in the whole space. When the initial density and the initial temperature are linearly equivalent to some large constant states, we establish the first result on the global existence of large strong solution. Moreover, the optimal decay rates of the solution to its associated equilibrium are established when the initial data belong to $L^{p_0}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for some $p_0\in[1,2]$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Good-Vorticity Low-Regularity Integrator for the Inviscid Oldroyd--B System with Stress Diffusion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish sharp convergence results for a sequential semi-implicit good-vorticity integrator for the two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd--B system with stress diffusion on the torus. For exact solutions satisfying $u\in C_tB^{1+α}_{\infty,1}$ and $τ\in C_tB^α_{\infty,1}\cap L^1_tB^{2+α}_{\infty,1}$, $0\leα\le2$, we prove convergence in the critical norms $B^1_{\infty,1}\times B^0_{\infty,1}$, uniformly over the time nodes on every finite interval where these regularity assumptions hold, including the critical endpoint $α=0$. For $0<α\le2$, we obtain the rate $O(h^{α/2})$ without any additional time Hölder assumption, reaching first order at $α=2$. These algebraic exponents are optimal for this Eulerian scheme over the stated solution classes, as shown by fixed-data lower bounds in the case $a=b=0$ with nonzero velocity mean. For a fixed shear solution at critical regularity, we establish matching logarithmic upper and lower bounds on the numerical error, ruling out every positive algebraic convergence rate. We also prove that the gain of one stress derivative at the time nodes is optimal when the velocity is controlled in $B^1_{\infty,1}$, even for smooth initial stress.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schrödinger equation on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On hot spots of the torsion function and the ground state of the Laplacian
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We compare the maximum points \(P_Ω\) and \(Q_Ω\) of the
  torsion function and the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction. We begin with a systematic analytic description of both
  hot spots over the full range of opening angles of circular sectors: uniqueness,
  strict monotonicity with respect to the angle, distinct
  small-angle asymptotics, and explicit limiting equations in the
  slit-disk limit. We also prove the existence of a coincidence angle and establish arithmetic
  properties of the limiting coordinates. We then consider bounded convex planar domains with a line of symmetry, and we prove the sharp diameter-normalized identity
  \[
  \sup_Ω
  \frac{|P_Ω-Q_Ω|}{\operatorname{diam}(Ω)}=\frac12.
  \]
  Its upper-bound argument uses standard localization in the heart and
  an elementary geometric enclosure. Sharpness follows from thin convex
  domains with a vanishing relative width perturbation peaking near one
  endpoint: the torsion hot spot approaches that endpoint, whereas the
  ground-state hot spot approaches the midpoint.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical $p$-Laplace equations with monotone coefficients: Liouville classification and a Schoen-type Harnack inequality
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We investigate positive weak solutions of the critical $p$-Laplace equation $$
  -Δ_p u = u^{p^*-1} h(u), \qquad 1 < p < n, $$ where $h$ is a positive, bounded, continuous, and nonincreasing function. Our first main result is a complete classification of normalized, bounded, positive entire solutions for every equation in a compact family determined by $h$: Any such solution must coincide with an Aubin--Talenti profile. Moreover, the existence of an Aubin--Talenti profile as a solution implies that $h$ is constant on the entire interval of values attained by that profile.
  Subsequently, applying this classification result, we establish the following scale-invariant Schoen-type estimate $$
  \left(\sup_{B_R} u\right)\left(\inf_{B_{2R}} u\right)^{p-1}
  \le C R^{p-n} $$ for nonnegative weak solutions defined in $B_{3R}$. As a direct corollary, we apply the profound result of Ciraolo--Gatti \cite{CG2026} to obtain a fully unrestricted Liouville theorem: Every positive entire solution must coincide with an Aubin--Talenti profile. For the purely critical equation, we also show that the corresponding Liouville classification is equivalent to a Schoen-type Harnack inequality.
  The arguments in this work give quasilinear versions of the Kelvin transform and the method of moving spheres, which was previously available only in the semilinear setting, and also yield alternative proofs of the classical results. The technique developed here can likely be extended to a wider class of Liouville-type problems for critical equations.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 66 Pages. See Appendix B for a concise outline for the pure-power case with p=2. In the abstract, we now explicitly emphasize the important role of Ciraolo--Gatti in the classification result!

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the stabilizing effects of rotation on stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the half spaces in scale-critical spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier--Stokes equations with the Coriolis force in the half space with the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We show the existence of a unique small solution in the scale-critical Besov spaces. In particular, for any boundary data with a vanishing normal component, and for any external forces, we establish the well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary value problem when the speed of rotation is sufficiently large. In the proof, to exploit the stabilizing effect of the Coriolis term, we employ two explicit formulas depending on the relation between the horizontal frequency and the magnitude of the rotation speed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local Well-Posedness of the Unsteady Boundary Layer System for Dilatant Power-Law Fluids
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish local-in-time existence and uniqueness of monotone classical solutions to the two-dimensional nonstationary boundary layer equations for dilatant power-law fluids in a periodic half-space, for every fixed exponent $n>1$. The result holds under Oleinik's monotonicity condition and suitable weighted Sobolev, algebraic decay, and compatibility assumptions. The main difficulties are the tangential derivative loss caused by the normal velocity and the degeneracy at infinity of the principal coefficient $nω^{n-1}$ in the nonlinear vorticity diffusion $\partial_y^2(ω^n)$, where $ω=\partial_y u$. We adapt the Masmoudi-Wong energy method and use a good unknown to control the tangential derivative loss. For the nonlinear diffusion, we separate the estimates near the boundary from the treatment of degeneracy in the far field. Nonlinear boundary reduction and localized trace estimates control the boundary terms, while weighted estimates exploit the compensating decay of vorticity derivatives to control the diffusion commutators. Together with tangential regularization and weighted maximum and minimum principles, these estimates yield bounds uniform in the regularization parameter and preserve weighted monotonicity. Under these assumptions, the result provides an affirmative local-in-time answer to the existence and uniqueness question in Open Problem~11 of Oleinik and Samokhin.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical Optimizers for the Finite-Rank Fractional Lieb--Thirring Inequality
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study optimal potentials for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring problem at the eigenvalue-counting endpoint, for \(0<s<1\) and \(d>2s\). Using the zero-energy Birman--Schwinger formulation, we prove a profile decomposition of normalized optimizing sequences with exact splitting of rank and potential mass, and strong approximation in \(L^{d/(2s)}\). Strict subadditivity yields existence and compactness modulo translations and dilations. At rank two, the optimal constant equals the rank-one constant, the supremum is not attained, and every normalized optimizing sequence splits into two Sobolev potentials. We also prove strict increase of the minimal potential masses and a uniform spectral gap for optimizing sequences. For each optimizer, we derive an Euler--Lagrange system and establish boundedness, local Hölder regularity and \(V(x)=|x|^{-4s}(c_\infty+o(1))\) as \(|x|\to\infty\), with \(c_\infty\geq0\). The conformal orbit of every optimizer contains a representative with a strictly positive asymptotic coefficient.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to the Liouville Equation on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study stable solutions of the discrete Liouville equation \[ -Δu=e^u \] on infinite, locally finite graphs with polynomial volume growth. We prove that no stable solution exists whenever the order $d$ of polynomial volume growth satisfies $d<10$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Long-Time Behavior towards Generic Riemann Solutions for Radiative Euler Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional radiative Euler equations, where the Riemann pattern consists of a $1$-rarefaction wave, a $2$-contact discontinuity, and a $3$-shock wave. We prove that, for sufficiently small wave strengths and initial perturbations, the Cauchy problem admits a unique global solution, which converges uniformly as $t\to \infty$ to a composite wave of the $1$-rarefaction wave, $2$-viscous contact wave, and $3$-radiative shock profile with a time-dependent shift. As a key ingredient, we establish a comprehensive set of quantitative estimates for weak radiative shock profiles.
  Our proof is based on the method of $a$-contraction with shifts. In all previous applications of the $a$-contraction method to the study of long-time behavior, the proof has relied essentially on the parabolic structure provided by either viscosity or heat conduction. In this work, we extend the method to a hyperbolic-elliptic system without parabolic structure.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharpness transitions for weighted Triebel--Lizorkin Hardy inequalities with p < q
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For two-weight fractional difference energies with inner and outer exponents $1<p<q$, we study the optimality of the Hardy constant generated by a homogeneous power. We prove nontrivial sharpness intervals for every sign of $D=d+2β-sp$, including a two-sided interval when $D=0$, and strict loss of optimality near both finite-energy endpoints. For $q\ge2$, sharpness extends beyond the elementary pointwise scalar criterion through an integrated remainder estimate: after opposite logarithmic displacements are combined, a positive contribution at bounded displacements absorbs the negative contribution at larger displacements. A single quadratic reference energy controls this comparison and the angular fluctuations of near-extremizers. When $1<p<q<2$, optimization of the scalar supporting-line inequality gives the exact power exponent for that criterion and a larger explicit sharpness interval. Angular variations provide explicit strict-loss examples. The method extends to flat singular sets and regional half-space energies, with separate finiteness ranges for test energies and the homogeneous candidate. Complementary results for $p>q$ include flat-subspace inequalities. The constants are optimal on the stated smooth test classes and extend unchanged to their difference-norm completions whenever they are positive.

Functional Analysis.title: A Nearly Quadratic Lower Bound for Linear Optimization over Convex Bodies in the Membership Oracle Model
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove nearly quadratic lower bounds for randomized algorithms for linear optimization and uniform sampling over convex bodies in the membership oracle model. For linear optimization, this matches the known nearly quadratic upper bound up to a polylog factor in the dimension. For uniform sampling, this improves on the previous linear lower bound. Our construction also implies the same lower bound for volume estimation.

Functional Analysis.title: Norm and Minimum Attainment of Foguel-Type Operators
Functional Analysis.summary: In this article, we study Foguel-type operators $\EuScript{F}=\begin{bmatrix} V_1^{*} & T\\ 0 & V_2\end{bmatrix}$ on $H_1\oplus H_2$, where each $H_j$ is a separable Hilbert space, $V_j\in \mathcal{B}(H_j)$ is an isometry for $j=1,2$, and $T\in \mathcal{B}(H_2,H_1)$. We examine how the norm and minimum attainment properties of $\EuScript{F}$ depend on the corner entry $T$ and on the defect spaces of the isometries. The norm formula $\|\EuScript{F}\|=\frac{\|T\|+\sqrt{\|T\|^{2}+4}}{2}$ holds for every $T$ when $V_1,V_2$ are isometries, and more generally when $V_2$ is a contraction that is isometric on the range of $T^{*}$. Moreover, $\EuScript{F}$ attains its norm if and only if $T$ does. We characterize the positive $2\times 2$ block operator matrices that are absolutely norm attaining and absolutely minimum attaining, and use this to prove that $\EuScript{F}$ is absolutely norm attaining if and only if it is absolutely minimum attaining if and only if $\dim N(V_1^{*})<\infty$ and $T$ has finite rank. The closure of the absolutely norm attaining class is described by $\dim N(V_1^{*})<\infty$ and compactness of $T$. Further, we establish that the reduced minimum modulus is $γ(\EuScript{F})=\frac{\sqrt{\|T\|^{2}+4}-\|T\|}{2}=\frac{1}{\|\EuScript{F}\|}$, and $\EuScript{F}$ attains it if and only if $T$ is norm attaining. We also show that $\EuScript{F}$ is Fredholm if and only if $\dim N(V_j^{*})<\infty$ for $j=1,2$, with index $\dim N(V_1^{*})-\dim N(V_2^{*})$, and we give its Moore--Penrose inverse. Finally, for $V_1=V_2=T_z$ and more generally $V_j=T_{θ_j}$ with $θ_j$ inner, and Toeplitz or Hankel corner entries, the results become explicit conditions on the symbol.
Functional Analysis.comment: 26 pages. Submitted to a journal. Comments and suggestions are welcome

Functional Analysis.title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
Functional Analysis.summary:
We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246].
  We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties.
  The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states.
  Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed.
  As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.
Functional Analysis.comment: 38 pages, preliminary version, one comments and references are welcome

Functional Analysis.title: The edge case of the Hilbert matrix operator between weighted Bergman spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
The Hilbert matrix operator $H$ is bounded on the standard weighted Bergman spaces $A^p_α,\, p>α+2>1$. We examine the limiting case when $α=p-2$, and for $p\leq 2$, we characterize the logarithmic modification of the standard weight needed for the domain $A^p_{v_{γ,p}}$ and codomain $A^p_{v_{β,p}}$ to ensure boundedness. In particular, we prove that $H:A^2_{\log^γ} \to A^2_{\log^β}$ is bounded if and only if $γ-β\geq 2$ and $γ>1$, solving an open problem posed by B. Karapetrović and M. Jevtić. We also settle the situation for $p>2$ in all cases, except when the logarithmic exponents $γ$ and $β$ satisfy $γ-β=p$.
  Moreover, we completely solve the same problem when the domain and codomain are certain weighted reflexive $\ell^p$ spaces. All results are extended to the generalized Hilbert operator $H_g$.
Functional Analysis.comment: A generalization of the results presented in v1

Functional Analysis.title: Matrix-valued regular functions of a quaternionic variable - a decomposition and some approximation results
Functional Analysis.summary: A quaternionic matrix-valued regular function is a map $F: Ω\rightarrow M_n(\mathbb{H})$ whose entries are (left) regular functions of a quaternionic variable, where $Ω$ is a domain in $\mathbb{H}$. Given any $n \times n$ matrix-valued regular function $F(q)$ over $\mathbb{H}$ having norm at most $1$, we derive a decomposition of $F(q)$ in the form $U \star \begin{bmatrix} ||F(q_0)|| & 0\\0 & G(q)\end{bmatrix} V$ for some constant unitary matrices $U, V$, some vector $q_0$ and an $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ matrix-valued regular function $G(q)$, where $\star$ denotes the star product over $\mathbb{H}$. We use this to prove a Fisher-type approximation result for matrix-valued regular functions $F(q)$ on the quaternionic unit ball $\mathbb{B}$: if $F(q)$ has norm at most $1$ and is continuous on the boundary of the ball, then $F(q)$ can be uniformly approximated by a convex combination of matrix-valued rational unitary functions on $\overline{\mathbb{B}}$.

Functional Analysis.title: On approximate support versions of Donoho--Stark uncertainty principles for $k$-Hadamard operators
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper we present results related to Donoho--Stark type uncertainty principles that were proved in the article "The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme" by Wigderson and Wigderson for $k$-Hadamard operators in the finite-dimensional setting. Namely, the authors showed that Donoho-Stark principles can be generalized to versions for approximate supports with respect to norms $\ell^{p}$ for $p=1$ and $p=2$. In the second case they assumed the so-called speciality condition, namely that a suitable matrix satisfies $A^{*}A = kI$. First we show that such theorems cannot be generalized to $p>1$ if matrices are not special $k$-Hadamard. Next we prove Donoho-Stark type principle for special $k$-Hadamard operators for $\ell^{p}$ norms within the range $1\leq p\leq 2$. Finally, we show that such theorems are false for $p>2$ even in the presence of the speciality condition.

Functional Analysis.title: Taylor-type joint spectrum and essential spectrum of row-bounded sequences of commuting operators
Functional Analysis.summary: As the cornerstone of multivariable operator theory, (essential) Taylor's joint spectrum plays crucial roles in many areas. The present paper is devoted to developing the theory of (essential) Taylor-type joint spectrum of row-bounded sequences of commuting operators on Hilbert spaces and to establishing the associated Fredholm index theory. Furthermore, the holomorphic functional calculus for row-bounded sequences is established. At last, we obtain a Gleason-Richter-Sundberg type index theorem in the infinite-variable setting, which connects the Fredholm index, the asymptotic Arveson's curvature invariant and fibre dimensions.

Functional Analysis.title: The Floquet-Magnus expansion of unbounded operators
Functional Analysis.summary: The Floquet-Magnus expansion is a widely used tool to derive effective descriptions of time-periodic quantum systems by approximating their dynamics with a time-independent Hamiltonian. However, its standard formulation is, strictly speaking, restricted to bounded Hamiltonians. In this work, we extend its definition and analysis to a broad class of time-periodic unbounded Hamiltonians. Our approach is based on an a priori distinct nonperturbative framework for the construction of effective Hamiltonians, which we show to reproduce the Floquet-Magnus expansion. A particular strength of our framework is that it allows us to prove that the resulting effective dynamics approximates the original time evolution propagators to arbitrary order in the high-frequency limit without requiring convergence of the Floquet-Magnus expansion, a condition that is already highly restrictive even in the bounded setting. We illustrate the scope of the method on representative models: the quantum Rabi Hamiltonian in the interaction picture, and the periodically driven quantum harmonic oscillator.

Functional Analysis.title: Intrinsic uniform structure on median algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce the median uniformity $\mathcal U_{\mathrm m}$, an intrinsic precompact convex uniform structure on a median algebra. It is Hausdorff under natural assumptions, for instance for finite-rank median algebras. In the Hausdorff case, its uniform completion yields the Minimal Median Compactification (MMC). The induced topology $τ_{\mathrm m}$ provides a natural higher-rank analogue of the interval topology on linearly ordered sets and of the shadow topology on rank-one median algebras. When the intrinsic topology $τ_{\mathrm m}$ is Hausdorff and all intervals are compact, the MMC is the unique proper median compactification and is canonically isomorphic to the Roller--Fioravanti compactification. We apply this uniform framework to continuous actions of a topological group $G$ by median automorphisms. We show that the MMC is a median $G$-compactification. In the finite-rank case, the resulting compact $G$-system is Rosenthal representable and dynamically tame.

Functional Analysis.title: Hereditary Approximation under Hilbertian Extension
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we prove that if a Banach space $X$ has the hereditary approximation property, then $X\oplus_2 H$ has the hereditary approximation property for every Hilbert space $H$. This answers a question of Johnson and Szankowski. In addition, if $X$ is also reflexive, then every closed subspace of $X\oplus_2H$ has the metric approximation property. The proof uses Grothendieck's characterization of the approximation property, a factorization of nuclear operators through quotients of $X$, and a nuclear perturbation of the coordinate projection on a closed graph.

Functional Analysis.title: Quantum Bernstein--Kolmogorov--Arnold approximation
Functional Analysis.summary:
This paper addresses the expressivity and representation gap in Quantum Neural Networks by establishing a quantum analogue of the classical Kolmogorov--Arnold representation theorem.
  We propose a constructive approximation framework over fixed input coherent states, where the dependence of the function argument is embedded entirely in coordinate qubits, while the target function dictates a single outer unitary evolution.
  By applying a Sprecher-type representation to the rotation angle of the state, we demonstrate that the multidimensional operator factorises into \(2d+1\) commuting universal inner observables.
  We prove that the resulting measurement probability precisely reproduces the multidimensional Bernstein polynomial of the target function.
  For any continuous multivariate function, the joint quantum state converges uniformly to the target output register, linking classical superposition theory with probabilistic and coherent quantum circuits.

Functional Analysis.title: The role of symmetry in the performance of the Thresholding Greedy Algorithm
Functional Analysis.summary: This paper continues the study of conditional symmetric systems initiated in arXiv:2601.15784 and solves several problems posed there. While the interaction between unconditionality and symmetry is well known in the Banach setting following the work in arXiv:2304.05888 and arXiv:2601.15784, we broaden the scope and address similar questions for spreading systems in the more general setting of quasi-Banach spaces. Our aim is twofold. On the one hand, we characterize which spreading systems of Banach spaces are unconditional. On the other hand, we provide examples of quasi-Banach spaces equipped with conditional systems with symmetry-related properties to illustrate the connections between symmetry, greedy-like properties, and the Schauder basis property in the absence of local convexity.

Functional Analysis.title: A general equivalence relation on the global class of morphisms of a category
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce a general equivalence relation on the global class of morphisms of a category that subsumes several classical notions of equivalence in mathematics. We show that group-action equivalence relations, pullback equivalence relations, and coarse analysis-operator-based equivalence relations on continuous Bessel families are special cases of this general definition.

Functional Analysis.title: Truncated Dirichlet estimates for Bloch functions
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study the truncated Dirichlet functional
  \[
  Φ_n (f) = \sum_{k = 1}^n k |a_k|^2, \quad f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^\infty a_k z^k,
  \]
  when $f$ belongs to the Bloch space. If $n \geq 27$, we find a normalized Bloch function $f_n$ such that
  \[
  Φ_n (f_n) > n B_n^2,
  \]
  where $B_n = \max \{ |a_n| : \| f \|_{\mathcal{B}} = 1 \}$, thus proving that an inequality by Kayumov and Wirths cannot be extended to large values of $n$. Nevertheless, we show that the inequality $Φ_n(f) \leq n B_n^2$ holds for all normalized functions when $n \leq 9$.

Functional Analysis.title: Fock Projections between Gaussian Mixed-Norm Spaces: Full-Range Boundedness and Compactness
Functional Analysis.summary: The Fock--Bargmann projection \(P_t\) is initially an orthogonal projection on a Gaussian Hilbert space. We characterize the boundedness and compactness of \[ P_t:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow \mathcal F_β^{p_2,q_2} \] and of its associated maximal projection \[ P_t^+:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow L_β^{p_2,q_2} \] for all \(t,α,β>0\) and \(0<p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2\le\infty\).
