Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study curvature flows for the dual Orlicz--Minkowski problem for strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. The prescribed function has the form $φ(h)G(X)$, where $X=\nabla h+hν$ and $G$ may be nonradial and nonhomogeneous. For acute contact angles, the evenness assumption together with either of the two integral conditions yields a smooth weighted-volume-preserving flow for all $t>0$ and a smooth solution to the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation. Without the evenness assumption, two strict spherical-cap barriers yield the same conclusions for an unnormalized flow, whose limiting hypersurfaces solve the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation with $c=1$. A uniform strict monotonicity condition under rescaling ensures uniqueness for $c=1$ and convergence of the unnormalized flow in any $C^k$ norm at an exponential rate. The problem considered here includes the capillary $L_p$-Minkowski and $L_p$ dual Minkowski problems as special cases.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness for the inverse Schrödinger problem in the plane with $L^p$ potentials, $p>1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded smooth domain. We prove that the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for $-Δ+V$ uniquely determines every complex-valued potential $V\in L^p(Ω)$, $p>1$, provided that zero is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue. This extends the previously known range $p>4/3$ to all $p>1$. The proof uses Bukhgeim's quadratic-phase solutions and an average of Alessandrini's identity over the phase center. After separating the Neumann-series tails, we show that each remaining Born term tends to zero. The fixed-order estimates combine bounds for the absolute kernels with oscillatory cancellation and a duality argument for the product of the two Cauchy transforms.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local null controllability of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis system by a Neumann boundary control
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove local null controllability for a parabolic equation coupled to an elliptic equation on a bounded interval. The drift depends on the elliptic variable, and a single control acts through the Neumann condition at the left endpoint. For every positive control time and every locally Lipschitz drift function, sufficiently small initial data in $L^\infty$ can be driven to zero by an $L^\infty$ boundary control. To construct the control, we extend the linear equation to a larger interval using an even extension of the initial datum and an odd extension of the drift. A distributed $L^2$ control in the added interval then gives a boundary control on the original interval. A heat kernel estimate bounds the derivative trace needed for this construction. We obtain the nonlinear result by a set-valued fixed point argument.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local stability of direct Mach configurations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the local stability of direct Mach configurations for the two-dimensional steady compressible Euler equations. Given a piecewise constant direct Mach configuration with subsonic flow behind both the reflected shock and the Mach stem, we prove that under a transversality condition on the shock polar loops and a suitable condition on the truncation segment, every sufficiently small perturbation of the incoming flow gives rise to a Mach configuration that is a small perturbation of the background one, in the sense that the reflected shock, the Mach stem and the slip line, together with the downstream subsonic flow, stay close to their background counterparts. The triple point is fixed at the origin, and the domain is truncated at a finite distance. Euler--Lagrange coordinates are employed to transform the unknown contact discontinuity curve (slip line) into a fixed boundary and to write the full Euler system as a first-order elliptic system for the flow direction and pressure coupled to transport equations for the Bernoulli and entropy quantities. The key idea in dealing with the contact discontinuity is to solve a mixed boundary value problem, in divergence form with discontinuous coefficients, for a single elliptic equation, so that continuity of the scalar unknown and its conormal flux allows reconstruction of the flow direction and pressure with the required contact discontinuity conditions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Supermodularity and robust optimization in elliptic PDEs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study distributionally robust optimization problems constrained by semilinear elliptic PDEs. Uncertain nonnegative loads enter the PDE through $m$ intensity parameters, and damage is measured by integrating a nondecreasing convex function of the solution. We prove that, for coercive operators satisfying a positivity-preserving lattice condition, a nondecreasing concave reaction $g$ makes the damage nondecreasing, convex, and supermodular in the load intensities. Under nonnegative loading and $g(0)=0$, concavity is also necessary for these properties to hold for all admissible operators and damage functions. For Wasserstein uncertainty sets based on a weighted $\ell_1$ distance and $N$ observations, we show that at most $m+1$ nested stress corners are needed per observation. These corners form a set of at most $N(m+1)$ points that does not depend on the Wasserstein radius and supports a worst-case distribution for every radius. We compute the exact robust value by checking $λ=0$ and at most $Nm$ positive breakpoints, and we construct a worst-case distribution that moves each observation to a chain corner and splits at most one observation between two adjacent corners. We apply the results to a convex remediation-planning problem with Monod biodegradation. Numerical experiments show that the method requires far fewer PDE solves than enumerating all corners. Finally, a counterexample shows that supermodularity can fail for the fractional $p$-Laplacian when $p>2$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stabilization of gravity-capillary water waves with constant vorticity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish an exponential stabilization result for two-dimensional periodic gravity-capillary water waves of finite depth with constant vorticity, using an external pressure localized on the free surface. The pressure is prescribed as the product of a nonnegative cut-off function and the time derivative of the surface elevation and serves as a feedback control. To prove the main result, we derive the energy dissipation identity and estimate the time integral of the energy relative to the flat Couette flow, by means of the multiplier method and periodic Pohozaev identities. A remaining lower-order term led by the vorticity is removed by a compactness argument based on unique continuation for the linearized equations. Under a condition relating the cut-off to gravity and surface tension, the relative energy decays exponentially on any interval on which a regular solution remains uniformly small in Sobolev norms. We do not assume the evenness on the solution and smallness on the vorticity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularizing the Navier-Stokes Equations by One Noise Component
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the torus with multiplicative Itô noise which is driven by a single Brownian motion and acts only through the vertical velocity component. Such a noise is strongly degenerate: An infinite-dimensional part of the velocity field is not forced at all. We show that it nevertheless has a regularizing effect. For a linear noise, strong solutions whose initial data have no unforced part are global with probability tending to one as the noise intensity grows. For a suitable nonlinear noise, the same holds for arbitrary $\mathrm{H}^1$ data, together with smallness of the space-time $\mathrm{L}^6$-norm of the vertical velocity. As a deterministic counterpart, we give a self-contained proof that a quintic damping of the vertical component yields global regularity, and the same argument shows that, under the linear noise, blow-up can only occur if the vertical velocity leaves $\mathrm{L}^6_{t,x}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Radial and nonradial solutions for nonlinear scalar field equations and a new proof for certain Gagliardo-Nirenberg type inequality on the plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
A nonlinear scalar field equation is studied, which takes the form
  \begin{equation*}
  - \triangle{u}=g(u) \ \textrm{in} \ R^{N}, \quad \quad u \in E,
  \end{equation*} where $E$ is a suitable Banach space.. The nonlinear term $g(s)$ has subcritical growth at infinity. Near $s=0$, the nonlinear term $g(s)$ grows like $s^q$ for any $q>0$ if $N=2$ and for any $q \in (0,\ (N+2)/(N-2))$ if $N\ge 3$.
  Through the technique of adding one dimension of space, by mountain pass theorem and symmetric mountain theorem, we prove the multiplicity of radial solutions if $N\ge 2$ and the multiplicity of nonradial solutions if $N\ge 4$. Unlike [1] and [2], the proof presented here does not rely on any decomposition results. During the treatment for $N=2$, we provide a new proof for certain Gagliardo-Nirenberg type inequality on $R^2$, which is originally due to [3]. Based on this inequality we get a Trudinger-Moser type inequality involving gradient norm through Taylor expansion. Eventually we construct a special path to obtain the least energy level for solutions.
  [1] J. Mederski, Nonradial solutions of nonlinear scalar field equations. Nonlinearity 33 (2020), 6349--6380.
  [2] L. Jeanjean, S.S. Lu, Nonlinear scalar field equations with general nonlinearity. Nonlinear Anal. 190 (2020), 111604.
  [3] D.E. Edmunds, A.A.Ilyin, Asymptotically sharp multiplicative inequalities. Bull. London Math. Soc. 27 (1995) 71--74.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Validity of three-dimensional axisymmetric steady Prandtl expansion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study steady axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flows with swirl in the circular cylinder $\mathcal C_L=(0,L)\times B_2(0,1)$ with the no-slip condition on the stationary lateral wall. For the leading Euler velocity $(u_e^0,w_e^0,θ_e^0)=(1,0,r K(r))$, where $K(r)=H(r^2)$ is a prescribed smooth radial function, we construct and justify a Prandtl expansion as $\varepsilon \to 0$ for sufficiently small fixed $L$. The expansion accounts for both axial and azimuthal boundary layers, including the case of a Blasius leading axial profile with nonzero swirl. Weighted estimates at the symmetry axis and coupled remainder estimates yield a uniform velocity error bound.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The geometric case of the Erdős Similarity Conjecture. A human exposition of the OpenAI proof
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For a fixed $q\in(0,1)$, can a set of positive Lebesgue measure avoid every translated and dilated copy of $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$? OpenAI's release of October 6, 2026 shows that it can, with a compact subset of $[0,1]$ whose measure is arbitrarily close to one. We give a detailed exposition of the proof, using only finite probability and basic measure theory. The proof removes a small open set intersecting every copy, obtained from a random construction: fair random choices, attached to the cells of nested grids, route each point down a finite tree, and at the leaf reached a further random choice removes the point with probability $p$. The removed set therefore has expected density $p$, however large the tree, while the branching gives each copy many independent chances to intersect it. Each chance depends on only part of the tree, so its outcome changes at only a controlled number of dilations, and a union bound over finitely many representative dilations then covers every dilation. We also relate the proof to the earlier random-cell arguments going back to Kolountzakis (Bull. London Math. Soc. 29 (1997), 415--424) and to recent work on two-fold sumsets (arXiv:2607.03584) and on Rajchman measures (arXiv:2609.04456), and we show how the method of conditional expectations makes the construction deterministic.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The polyharmonic Hénon--Lane--Emden conjecture
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study positive classical solutions of the polyharmonic Hénon--Lane--Emden system $(-Δ)^m u=|x|^αv^p$, $(-Δ)^m v=|x|^βu^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $m\ge2$, $p,q\ge1$, $pq>1$, and $α,β\ge0$. We prove that there is no such solution whenever $\frac{n+α}{p+1}+\frac{n+β}{q+1}>n-2m$, in every dimension and without any assumption on the behavior of the solutions at infinity. Combined with an existence result of Villavert, this proves the polyharmonic Hénon--Lane--Emden conjecture of Phan for $m\ge2$: for these exponents and weights, a positive classical solution exists if and only if $\frac{n+α}{p+1}+\frac{n+β}{q+1}\le n-2m$. The proof has two parts. We first show that positivity forces $(-Δ)^i u>0$ and $(-Δ)^i v>0$ for $1\le i\le m-1$. For $m$ even this needs $pq>1$, and explicit radial examples show that it fails when $pq<1$ and when $p=q=1$. The system is then equivalent to a weighted integral system with a Riesz kernel of order $2m$. For such integral systems we prove the corresponding Liouville theorem for every Riesz order $μ\in(1,n)$, adapting a recent argument for the second-order case that combines a localized virial identity with an interval comparison along source layers.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This research was initially deposited on Zenodo on October 9, 2026 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23268558)

Analysis of PDEs.title: Linear decay of the beta-plane equation near Couette flow on the plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove new time decay estimates for the linearized $β$-plane equation near the Couette flow on the plane that combine inviscid damping and the dispersion of Rossby waves. Specifically, we show that the profiles of the velocity field components (i.e. $u(t,x+ty,y)$) decay pointwise on any compact set with polynomial rates. While mixing dominates for streamwise frequencies that are $O(1)$, dispersive effects need to be extracted for low streamwise frequencies that appear along a critical ray in frequency space.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the stabilizing effects of rotation on stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the half spaces in scale-critical spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier--Stokes equations with the Coriolis force in the half space with the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We show the existence of a unique small solution in the scale-critical Besov spaces. In particular, for any boundary data with a vanishing normal component, and for any external forces, we establish the well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary value problem when the speed of rotation is sufficiently large. In the proof, to exploit the stabilizing effect of the Coriolis term, we employ two explicit formulas depending on the relation between the horizontal frequency and the magnitude of the rotation speed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonradial entire solutions of the critical Hénon equation for every $α>2$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the critical Hénon equation $-Δu=|x|^αu^{(N+2+2α)/(N-2)}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$. Gladiali, Grossi, and Neves (\emph{Advances in Mathematics}, 2013) constructed nonradial continua bifurcating at $α_k=2(k-1)$, $k\ge2$, and conjectured that these continua are confined to the even parameters. Jiang and Xiong (2026) disproved this conjecture by obtaining nonradial solutions in punctured neighborhoods of $α_k$ for even $k>(N-2)/2$. We prove that positive nonradial finite-energy entire solutions exist for every $α>2$ in every dimension $N\ge3$. The proof introduces a global variational construction by direct minimization on a monotonicity cone on the Emden--Fowler cylinder. Angular and axial order restore compactness in every finite $L^r$, $r>2$, despite Sobolev supercriticality, and invariance of the linear resolvent yields the full equation. This constructs a solution at each prescribed parameter without continuing local bifurcation branches. The solutions have Newtonian decay, are invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and the Kelvin transform, and have energy strictly below the radial level. We also obtain a second solution for every $α>6$ in even dimensions, nonvertical branches at every $α_k$ with $k\ge2$ even without dimension restrictions, a cubic energy law, and rigidity near $α=0$ under bounded cylindrical amplitude.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This work was first announced on October 15, 2026, on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23384720)

Analysis of PDEs.title: Normalized solutions to a focusing biharmonic Schrödinger equation with mixed dispersion and Sobolev critical growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper investigates normalized solutions to a focusing biharmonic Schrödinger equation with mixed dispersion and combined nonlinearities involving a lower-power perturbation and a Sobolev critical term. Under a suitable smallness condition on the prescribed mass and in the range \(2<p<2+\frac{4}{N}\), we establish the existence of a local minimizer of the associated energy functional on \(S_r(c)\) and infinitely many pairs of radial normalized solutions by combining the truncation technique, the concentration-compactness principle and genus theory. In particular, our results extend those of Alves et al. (Anal. Appl., (2025), doi: 10.1142/S0219530525500447) by removing the additional assumptions imposed in their work. In the range \(2+\frac{8}{N}<p<4^*\), we prove the existence of bounded radial constrained Palais-Smale sequences at mountain pass levels below the critical Sobolev threshold for sufficiently large \(μ\). We further show that their nonzero weak limits are radial weak solutions, with strong convergence in the derivative norms and in the critical Lebesgue norm. Moreover, under an additional condition \((N)\) ensuring the strict negativity of the limiting Lagrange multiplier, the weak limit preserves the prescribed \(L^2\)-mass, and the Palais-Smale sequence converges strongly in \(H^2(\mathbb R^N)\). These results extend the previous studies of Chang et al. (arXiv preprint, (2023), arXiv: 2305.00327v1) and Bonheure et al. (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., (2019), doi:10.1090/tran/7769).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
(Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.)
  We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations.
  As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 94 pages. Minor updates. To appear in Mem. Eur. Math. Soc

Analysis of PDEs.title: Arbitrary Dirichlet Eigenvalue Multiplicities on Smooth Star-Shaped Euclidean Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In every fixed dimension \(N\ge3\), for any finite list of positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\), we construct smooth strictly star-shaped Euclidean domains whose first \(\ell+1\) distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues can have multiplicities \(1,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\) respectively. The condition "star-shaped" is almost optimal in the sense that this statement can not hold for bounded convex domains. In fact, we show that the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue of any bounded convex domain has multiplicity at most $(N-1)(k-1)+1$, and this bound $N$ for the second Dirichlet eigenvalue is sharp.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Thresholds of Instability for the Biharmonic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the time-dependent biharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equations with and without a mixed dispersion. We find the sharp threshold of blow-up and global existence for the biharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equations without a mixed dispersion by establishing the modified cross-constraint variational method. Building on this work, we prove that the standing waves are strongly unstable without further assumptions on the frequency. The main new ingredients of which require us to provide a comparison of two variational problems, improved the method in Zhang [Comm PDEs, 2005, 30: 1429-1443]. In the latter part of the paper, we study the biharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equations with a mixed dispersion, which destroys the scaling invariance. The single variational approach is utilized to obtain the sharp threshold of blow-up and global existence, and strong instability of standing waves.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Near-Critical Asymptotics and Radial Sharpness for a Two-Weight Hardy Inequality
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the optimal constant $C(p,γ)$ in a planar two-weight Hardy inequality relating the gradient and Hessian of a scalar potential, posed by Maz'ya in [14, Problem 3.11]. For every $1\le p<\infty$, we prove \[ \lim_{γ\toγ_c} 2^{p/2}|γ-γ_c|^p C(p,γ)=1, \qquad γ_c=1-\frac2p. \] The proof reduces the curl-free constraint to an angular minimization problem and yields qualitative rigidity of almost extremizers for $p>1$. Moreover, we determine the sharp constant in the radial class for every $1\le p<\infty$ and $γ\neγ_c$, thereby resolving the radial case of Maz'ya's problem. We also show that the radial inequality remains valid at $γ=γ_c$, with the same sharp constant \[ C_{\rm rad}(p,γ) =\left[1+\left(γ-1+\frac2p\right)^2\right]^{-p/2}. \] For general, not necessarily radial, potentials, we identify explicit parameter regions where this constant remains sharp and establish two sufficient criteria for symmetry breaking. The exact transition remains open for $p\ne2$. In the quadratic case, we recover the known sharp constant and derive a decomposition of its deficit. At the critical exponent, we obtain an exact remainder identity for the logarithmic Hardy inequality, whose classical constant remains sharp among radial potentials. The logarithmic inequality fails at $p=1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An explicit solution of the five-expert prediction PDE and the exact optimality set of COMB
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we derive an explicit solution of the stationary prediction with expert advice PDE for five experts. The formula is given in three regions. In the first two regions, it is the four-expert solution plus a single integral with an elementary positive density. In the third region, it is a finite sum of hyperbolic products whose coefficients are determined by one scalar quadrature. Our formula establishes that the rank ordered adversary $(1,0,1,0,0)$ achieves the Hamiltonian maximum in the PDE everywhere in the ordered sector, while the COMB strategy $(1,0,1,0,1)$ is optimal only on a lower dimensional subset of the sector (where $x_1=x_2$ and $x_3=x_4$). The verification of the Hamiltonian inequalities is a tedious task, part of which is completed with a computer assisted proof. The verification reduces to 21 scalar inequalities, which we prove using 147 exact rational Bernstein polynomial certificates. The exact certificates and their independent arithmetic checks are included in a supplement to this paper, and a Lean 4 formalization machine-checks the verification and both main theorems, apart from the viscosity characterization.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The first non-trivial Fučík curve for the sublinear Dirichlet Laplacian
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded open connected set, and let $q\in(1,2)$. We consider the sublinear $q$-eigenvalue problem for the Dirichlet Laplacian $-Δu=λ\|u\|_{L^q(Ω)}^{2-q}|u|^{q-2}u$, $u\in H^1_0(Ω)\setminus\{0\}$, whose first eigenvalue $λ_1(Ω)$ is simple, with eigenfunctions of constant sign. The definition of a second eigenvalue is not unique. Following the approach introduced by Molle and Passaseo for the linear Laplacian, we construct the first non-trivial curve of the corresponding Fučík spectrum, and show that it has a unique diagonal point $(γ(Ω),γ(Ω))$. The Fučík-selected second value $λ_2^F(Ω)=2^{1-\frac{2}{q}}γ(Ω)$ is strictly larger than $λ_1(Ω)$, admits a two-phase variational characterisation, and satisfies a sharp Hong-Krahn-Szegő inequality: among sets of given measure it is minimised by the union of two equal balls. The selected solution at the diagonal point is a classical $(2,q)$-eigenfunction exactly when its nodal $L^q$-masses are balanced. We finally show that on balls in dimensions $N\geq2$ every Fučík-selected solution is foliated Schwarz symmetric.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Discontinuities in optimal transport between nonconvex domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop a new approach to studying discontinuity sets of measure-preserving convex gradient maps between nonconvex domains. Such maps optimize the Euclidean distance squared. Our idea is to introduce a new `phantom' optimal transport problem, that transports the missing mass from the convex hull of the target to the `excess' Monge--Ampère measure of the minimal convex extension of the Brenier potential. We show that the closure of the discontinuity set of the original map contains the support of this phantom target. Moreover, inside a planar source domain these two sets actually coincide; on $n$-dimensional domains they coincide $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$-a.e. The Hausdorff exponent $n-1$ is sharp in every dimension $n\geq3$. For planar polygonal targets, we establish a quantitative global length bound for the closure of the discontinuity set depending only on the target geometry, valid for bounded positive densities.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large time dynamics for non-autonomous weakly damped KdV-Burgers equations on the real line
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The large time dynamics of the weakly damped non-autonomous Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation \begin{equation*} u_t + u_{xxx}+ uu_x + λu - μu_{xx} = g(x,t) \end{equation*} in the phase space $L^2(\mathbb R)$ is investigated. Due to the low regularity of the initial data, the framework of Bourgain spaces is employed. We first obtain the existence of a unique pullback attractor $\{\mathcal A_μ(t)\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ in $L^2(\mathbb R)$ for each $μ\ge 0$. Then we show an optimal asymptotic smoothing effect of the equation, namely the pullback attractor is compact in $H^3(\mathbb R)$. These results are proved by using an energy equation method, splitting solutions into parts with low and high frequencies and exploiting a dispersive regularization. Furthermore, the attractors are shown to be upper semicontinuous as $μ\to 0$ and have finite fractal dimensions in $H^1(\mathbb R)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Low-regularity global well-posedness for the one-dimensional, defocusing, septic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we show that the one dimensional septic nonlinear Schrödinger equation is globally well-posed in $H^s (\mathbb{R})$ when $s > 39/89$ with accompanying polynomial bounds in time. We utilize bilinear estimates to obtain improved bounds on the modified energy increment and prove new $L^{p+3}_{t,x}$ almost Morawetz estimates for the defocusing $p$-NLS adapted to the low-regularity setting, before specializing to the septic case $p=7$. These tools together allow us to reach Sobolev regularities $s<1/2$, showing for the first time a global existence result in the mass supercritical regime for a class of unbounded, discontinuous data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A holomorphic Lie-Trotter product formula for nonlinear local semigroup
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove a new, holomorphic version of the Lie-Trotter product formula for nonlinear local semigroups with a parameter. We show that the product converges to the solutions of a nonlinear evolutions equation with a parameter. The solution is holomorphic in time on a centered at zero conic set in the complex plane and depends continuously on the parameter, and analytically on the initial data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Curve-Supported Concentrations of Vortices and Screw Dislocations Subject to Confinement
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the concentration of logarithmically interacting defects, such as Ginzburg--Landau vortices and screw dislocations, on closed curves in two dimensions, subject to a confining field. We prove that a measure supported on a smooth closed curve solves the mean-field transport equation exactly when, in Lagrangian labels, the curve moves with the negative induced velocity and each label keeps its mass. This contour law is a gradient flow of the mean-field energy. We prove that the gradient of the energy on a curve has a leading term proportional to the operator $|D|$ with Fourier symbol $|k|$, which prevents every smooth equilibrium curve from being a local minimizer, in a gradient-flow analogue of the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability of vortex sheets. In a radially symmetric case with quadratic confinement, we find an explicit circular equilibrium whose linearization is diagonal in Fourier modes, and we show that, as $N\rightarrow \infty $, the linear spectrum of the regular $N$-gon converges, mode by mode, to that of the circle. Finally, we compute a critical point on two concentric circles with lower energy than the single circle, indicating a rich family of multi-circle equilibria.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stationary distribution of active Brownian particles in a bounded domain
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Self-propelled particles such as swimming micro-organisms often accumulate at boundaries. Active Brownian particles (ABPs), that is, particles moving at constant speed with an orientation undergoing rotational diffusion, provide a simple model. ABPs have a finite probability to be on the boundary. Their probability density therefore includes both regular bulk and singular boundary components. Exchanges between these represent capture at the boundary and re-entry into the bulk.
  We examine the distribution of ABPs in the stationary regime. We first obtain a similarity solution that describes the probability density near the turning points, where orientation is tangential to the boundary and particles re-enter the bulk. This shows that the bulk density is singular and the boundary density is non-differentiable. We then add spatial diffusion to the ABP model and investigate the limit $\eps \to 0$ of small spatial diffusivity. We use matched asymptotics to describe the regularising effect of a finite $\eps$, focusing on the vicinity of the turning points. We assess our predictions against numerical simulations using both lattice Markov chain and finite-element discretisations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Weighted Hardy-Type Inequalities for Homogeneous Magnetic Potentials
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove a sharp magnetic improvement of the family of weighted inequalities on the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}_+$ that interpolate between the Hardy inequality and the trace Hardy inequality. The magnetic potentials are of Aharonov-Bohm type, $\mathbf{A}(x)=|x|^{-1}\boldsymbol{a}(x/|x|)$, where the tangential field $\boldsymbol{a}$ may be singular on a closed subset of the sphere. We compute the sharp constant explicitly: it is given by the constant of the corresponding nonmagnetic inequality, evaluated in a virtual dimension that depends on the first eigenvalue of the magnetic Laplacian on the sphere. In particular, the magnetic trace Hardy constant strictly exceeds its Euclidean value whenever this eigenvalue is positive. The proof rests on a ground state representation of the deficit, which also shows that the sharp constant is not attained in the energy space.
  As a consequence, we obtain the sharp Hardy inequality for the fractional powers $(-Δ_{\mathbf{A}})^σ$, $0<σ<1$, of the magnetic Laplacian: the constant is the same on smooth functions supported away from the singular set and on the form domain of $(-Δ_{\mathbf{A}})^σ$, and it is not attained. Examples include the planar Aharonov-Bohm potential with nonintegral flux and, in dimension three, the Aharonov-Bohm potential and the Dirac monopole.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On uniqueness of probability solutions to one-dimensional Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We give new sufficient conditions for uniqueness of probability solutions to one-dimensional Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations in the case where the drift coefficient depends on time.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Solutions of the space-fractional heat equation with polynomial growth: Liouville theorems and Schauder estimates
Analysis of PDEs.summary: With the aim of extending to parabolic equations the framework developed by the first three authors in [Dipierro, Savin, and Valdinoci, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. (2019)], we introduce a notion of (viscosity) solutions for the space-fractional heat equation modulo $k$. In turn, we are able to define $s$-caloric functions with polynomial growth at infinity, showing also related Schauder estimates, a Liouville-type result, and a stability property with respect to the $L^\infty_{\rm{loc}}$-convergence.

Functional Analysis.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture from the viewpoint of lineability
Functional Analysis.summary: Algebraic genericity in the family of polynomial counterexamples to the recently solved Jacobian Conjecture for $N\ge3$ is investigated. The notion of affine-coneability is introduced and it is shown that this family is affine-coneable and 1-lineable, but not 2-lineable. Semigroupability is further studied with respect to coordinatewise multiplication and composition.

Functional Analysis.title: QWEP stability under twisted crossed products
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the QWEP property of twisted crossed products and its relation to Fourier multiplier transference on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We show that QWEP is not preserved by crossed products of QWEP von Neumann algebras by hyperlinear groups. Our examples include trace-preserving actions of a torsion-free residually finite Kazhdan group on a diffuse abelian algebra and on the hyperfinite type II$_1$ factor. We also obtain non-QWEP crossed products with nontrivial scalar cocycles. For scalar twists, we prove that a finite trace-preserving crossed product is QWEP if and only if its ordinary crossed product and its twisted group von Neumann algebra are QWEP. In the positive direction, we establish a restriction theorem for scalar twists of regular wreath products. These results provide QWEP inputs for Fourier multiplier transference and identify a completely bounded multiplier norm obstruction to QWEP. Finally, operator-valued cocycles give finite QWEP crossed products whose acting groups are not hyperlinear.

Functional Analysis.title: The first chiral homology group in higher genus
Functional Analysis.summary:
We extend the theory of the first chiral homology group of vertex algebras, developed by van Ekeren and Heluani for elliptic curves, to compact Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus. Our approach realizes a genus $g$ surface by iterated self-sewing of $g$ handles onto the Riemann sphere, each governed by a sewing parameter $ρ_i$ in a punctured disc.
  We construct an explicit complex computing the chiral homology groups $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_0$ and $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_1$ of a vertex algebra $V$ on a genus $g$ surface with $n$ marked points, and equip it with a projectively flat connection, with an explicit central-charge anomaly, over the $g$-dimensional space of sewing parameters. We prove a genus $g$ Fourier-space Borcherds identity for the associated modified vertex operators.
  We show that two finiteness assumptions 1) finite dimensionality of the first Poisson homology $\HP_1(R_V)$ of the Zhu $C_2$-algebra, and 2) finite generation of a certain Koszul homology of the associated graded algebra, imply finite dimensionality of $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_1(X,V)$ for every genus $g$ and every vertex algebra $V$.
  Using the degeneration $ρ_i \to 0$ together with the factorization theorem of Damiolini-Gibney-Tarasca, we relate the totally degenerate limit of $H_1^{\mathrm{ch}}$ to the Hochschild homology of an iterated construction on the Zhu algebra, and deduce vanishing of the first chiral homology group in every genus for rational vertex algebras.

Functional Analysis.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectra of Beurling algebras of abelian groups
Functional Analysis.summary:
We give a complete classification of all sets which are spectra of Beurling algebras of any locally compact abelian group, parametrizing them by compact convex sets in the dual of a certain locally convex vector space generated by the group.
  Hence, for example, a finitely generated free abelian group may enjoy a more complicated range of such spectra than the does rational numbers.

Functional Analysis.title: An explicit formula for the limit of the heat kernel measures on the spheres embedded in $\mathbb {R}^\infty$
Functional Analysis.summary: We show that the heat kernel measures based at the north pole of the spheres $S^{N-1}(\sqrt N)$, with a properly scaled radius $\sqrt N$ and adjusted center, in the sense of finite-dimensional marginals, to a Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^\infty$. In particular, in the direction of the base point, the variance of this limiting measure is $1-e^{-t}-te^{-t}$, and in the orthogonal directions, the variance is $1-e^{-t}$.

Functional Analysis.title: Frame Properties of Effective Stationary Sequences
Functional Analysis.summary: The Kaczmarz algorithm is an iterative projection method for reconstructing vectors in a Hilbert space from inner product data. However, sequences that are effective for this algorithm need not be frames and may lack standard frame reconstruction properties. We investigate these properties for stationary effective sequences, which were classified by Kwapień and Mycielski according to their spectral measures. In particular, we show that the corresponding Kaczmarz reconstruction series always converge unconditionally if and only if the spectral measure is atomic with finitely many point masses. We show that if the spectral measure is atomic, the stationary effective sequence and its auxiliary Parseval frame can be interchanged in the Kaczmarz reconstruction formula. Finally, we construct two stationary effective sequences with singular continuous spectral measures, one of which can be interchanged with its auxiliary Parseval frame in the reconstruction formula, and one of which cannot be interchanged.

Functional Analysis.title: A counterexample concerning weighted convolution on the integers
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $w:\mathbb{Z}\to(0,\infty)$ be a weight. When is the weighted space $\ell^p(\mathbb{Z},w)$ an algebra with respect to convolution? A well-known sufficient condition is that $(w^{-q}*w^{-q})/w^{-q}$ be bounded on $\mathbb{Z}$, where $q:=p/(p-1)$ is the index conjugate to $p$. We present an example to show that this sufficient condition is not necessary.

Functional Analysis.title: Circular orders: topology and continuous actions
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the topology of circularly ordered sets. While the algebraic notion is classical, the general topological theory has received comparatively little attention. In this work we provide a self-contained topological exposition and present several new directions and results. Our aim is to initiate a systematic study of generalized circularly ordered topological spaces and of continuous group actions on them. Provide a convex uniform structure description of circularly ordered compactifications. This yields a topological analysis of Novak's regular completion and its uniformity. Demonstrate that this uniform-structure approach yields several new results in the theory of $G$-compactifications for topological group actions on abstract ordered spaces. Reexamine functions of bounded variation on circularly ordered sets and prove generalizations of Helly's selection theorem (for circular and linear orders). These developments and the systematic analysis of circular order topologies are motivated by recent applications in topological dynamics, particularly in joint works with Eli Glasner.

Functional Analysis.title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Prékopa--Leindler inequality
Functional Analysis.summary:
We give a new, simpler proof of sharp stability for the Prékopa--Leindler inequality. In contrast to the main arguments from Figalli, van Hintum and Tiba~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}, our proof hinges mostly on the sharp stability theory for the Brunn--Minkowski problem, developed by the same authors \cite{figalli2024BM}, and on the idea of using a height transportation approach in order to match level sets.
  As a by-product of our techniques, we are able to prove the sharp dependency on $τ= \min\{λ,1-λ\}$ in the Prékopa--Leindler stability constant whenever one of the inputs is logarithmically concave, producing a new, simplified proof of two of the main results from~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}.
  Finally, in the same fashion as Kristály and Pîrvuceanu \cite{kristaly2026quantitative}, we are able to obtain new stability results for the Bakry-Emery log-Sobolev inequality and for the Talagrand inequality. Due to the sharpness of the inputs, these results are optimal in terms of exponents. We moreover show that the $L^1$ nature of the distance in such results \emph{cannot} in general be improved to any other $L^p$ distance, where $p>1.$

Functional Analysis.title: Quantum integrals II: Dominated and almost uniform convergence
Functional Analysis.summary: One main aim of our paper is to formulate noncommutative versions of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem in the setting of quantum integration theory on von Neumann algebras. Our starting point is a reformulation of classical dominated convergence in terms of weak* convergence. Using our recent sequential-continuity theorem, we obtain dominated convergence formulations for sequentially normal states and, under domination by a fixed bounded integrable majorant, for sequentially normal weights. Integrable, possibly unbounded, majorants are treated first in the tracial setting, then for arbitrary von Neumann algebras using Haagerup's \(L^1\) space, and finally using normal semifinite weights and their GNS representations. For any faithful normal semifinite weight phi, weak* convergence of norm-bounded sequences is characterized by `integrating against' bounded positive integrable majorants. We also study noncommutative almost uniform and local almost uniform convergence, and make the relationship with the order convergence results of Chetcuti et al. explicit. In particular, for norm-bounded sequences, local phi-bilaterally almost uniform convergence implies weak* convergence and \(\|h^{1/2}(x_n-x)h^{1/2}\|_1\to0\) for every positive Haagerup L1 density h, without assuming \(σ\)-finiteness. We also prove a dominated convergence theorem in the predual: fixed positive order domination and Petz's almost uniform convergence imply convergence in the predual norm. We establish implications and equivalences among these convergence notions, connecting dominated convergence with tracial and nontracial integration.
Functional Analysis.comment: Revision with new appendix, and some extra results and shortenings, etc

Functional Analysis.title: Characterization of the group Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
Functional Analysis.summary: A remarkable theorem of S. Alesker, S. Artstein-Avidan, and V. Milman characterizes the Fourier transform on $\mathbb{R}^n$ as, in essence, the unique transformation on the space of tempered distributions that exchanges convolution with pointwise multiplication. In this paper, we extend this perspective to the setting of the Heisenberg group $\He$, focusing on functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $\Hi$. We establish a characterization of the group Fourier transform on $\He$ in terms of convolution. More precisely, we characterize the group Fourier transform on $L^1(\He,\Hi)$ and $L^2(\He,\Hi)$. In addition, we obtain a similar characterization for the group Fourier transform of $\Hi$-valued Schwartz class functions on the Heisenberg group.

Functional Analysis.title: Lower bounds for Riesz interaction functionals
Functional Analysis.summary: Motivated by the pressure formation problem for hydrodynamic models with nonlocal interactions, we classify strong Lebesgue lower bounds for the Riesz energy functional and for a determinant functional arising from the theory of compensated integrability. The classification covers all integrability exponents in $(0,\infty]$ within the class of confined log-concave densities. These geometric assumptions are motivated by counterexamples for general densities. On the whole space, neither functional controls any fixed Lebesgue quasi-norm. Under confinement, lower bounds fail for exponents greater than one, whereas $L^1$ bounds hold for the energy in every dimension and for the determinant only in dimension one. The log-concave estimates hold at sharp integrability exponents and follow from endpoint Lorentz bounds for confined quasiconcave densities and a weak-to-strong lemma. In particular, the energy estimates provide a geometric lower-bound counterpart to the classical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality.

Functional Analysis.title: A Stieltjes representation of order $p$ for $ \mathrm{tr}[(A+tB)^{-p}]$: Heinävaara's measure, B-splines, and Stahl's theorem
Functional Analysis.summary: For $A$ positive definite, $B$ positive semidefinite and $p\ge1$ we show that $\mathrm{tr}[(A+tB)^{-p}]=\int(1+t\ell)^{-p}\,dρ_p(\ell)$ for a positive measure $ρ_p$ on the spectral interval of $L=A^{-1/2}BA^{-1/2}$, and we identify the measure: it has atoms $\mathrm{tr}[(P_sA^{-1}P_s)^p]$ at the eigenvalues of $L$ and a continuous density, an integral of Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure along rays. For integer $p$ the positivity of $ρ_p$ follows from the positivity of Heinävaara's measure alone, and the density is a sum of Curry-Schoenberg B-splines; for real $p$ the representation is obtained by inverting Heinävaara's transform. For $0<p<1$ the function is a Stieltjes function of order $p$ only if $[A,B]=0$, but a positive representation of order one holds, with an explicit density. Along $A_p=pI+A_0$, $p\to\infty$, the measures converge to the measure of Stahl's theorem (the Bessis-Moussa-Villani conjecture) for $\mathrm{tr}\,e^{-(A_0+tB)}$.

Functional Analysis.title: Unique Hahn-Banach extensions in Bochner $L^p$ spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $Y$ be a closed subspace of a real Banach space $X$. Let $(Ω,Σ,μ)$ be a complete finite measure space and let $1<p<\infty$. We prove that $Y$ has property-$(U)$, property-$(SU)$, property-$(wU)$ in $X$ if and only if $L^p(μ,Y)$ has the corresponding property in $L^p(μ,X)$. No Radon-Nikodým assumption on $X^*$ is required. The proofs use $w^*$-measurable representations of dual functionals and a simultaneous scalar-lifting construction. A norm-minimal representation for an element in $L^p(μ,X)^*$ is found suitable in this case. We also study the point of continuity of the identity map under different topologies on the unit sphere of $L^p(μ,X)^*$. For Bochner-integrable functionals, the pointwise $w^*-w$-continuity yields the uniqueness of the extension to $L^p(μ,X^{**})$. Examples show why arbitrary $w^*$-measurable representatives cannot replace the norm-minimal representatives in this context.

Functional Analysis.title: A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $(X,d)$ be a uniformly locally finite metric space, and $T$ an operator in the uniform Roe algebra $C_u^*(X)$ (or uniform quasi-local algebra $C_{ql}^*(X)$). In this paper, we introduce the concept of limit operators of $T$ on galaxies in the nonstandard extension of $X$, and prove that $T$ is a generalized Fredholm operator with respect to the ghost ideal in $C_u^*(X)$ (or $C_{ql}^*(X)$) if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible, and their inverses are uniformly bounded. In particular, if $X$ has Yu's Property A, then $T$ is a Fredholm operator if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible. Using techniques in nonstandard analysis, our result strengthens a work of Špakula--Willett \cite{SpW} on the characterization of Fredholmness by using less limit operators.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is the accepted version of the following article: Guo, L., Qian, J. and Wang, Q. (2026), A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras. Bull. London Math. Soc., 58: e70534, which has been published in final form at https://doi.org/10.1112/blms.70534. A minor error in the previous version is pointed out by the referee and is corrected (see Remark 1)

Functional Analysis.title: Near-optimal bounds for the critical 2d SHF and the delta-Bose gas
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish a near-optimal upper bound $\exp(\exp(CN^{1+o(1)}))$ for the $N$-th moment of the critical two-dimensional stochastic heat flow, improving on the bound $\exp(\exp(CN^{2}))$ of Gu, Quastel, and Tsai. Near-optimality follows from the lower bound $\exp(\exp(cN))$ of Ganguly and Nam. These estimates establish the exponential scale of the ground-state energy of the two-dimensional $N$-body delta-Bose gas predicted by Rajeev's conjecture, up to a vanishing error in the exponent. As a further step toward this conjecture, we derive, for each fixed $N$, a formula for the ground-state energy in terms of the bottom of the spectrum of a principal operator.

Functional Analysis.title: A Note on Fractional Sobolev inequalities revisited
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we extend the analysis of homogeneous fractional Sobolev inequalities in the paper by A.D. Nguyen, J. I. Dıaz, and Q.-H. Nguyen (2020). We combine their subcritical proof with the first author's adaptation to the supercritical case to provide a short interpolation-based proof for the critical case.

Functional Analysis.title: Rigidity of the Peres-Virág class
Functional Analysis.summary: Consider the hyperbolic Gaussian analytic function (GAF) \begin{equation*} F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }ξ_{n}z^{n},\qquad |z|<1, \end{equation*} where the $ξ_{n}$ are independent standard complex Gaussian variables. Peres-Virág theorem tells that the distribution of the zeros of $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is provided by a Determinantal Point Process (DPP). We prove that $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is the only GAF whose zeros are determinantal with a Hermitian kernel, up to multiplication by a zero-free holomorphic function and a one-to-one holomorphic change of variable, with a \ non-degeneracy condition imposed to exclude trivial cases. The proof identifies a geometric property of GAF's with (local) determinantal zeros: the metric defined by the first intensity must have constant curvature $-4$.

Functional Analysis.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
Functional Analysis.summary: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.

Functional Analysis.title: Pointwise function spaces over compacta are not weak Banach spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional real Banach space. We prove that there is no continuous bijection $h\colon C_p(K)\to E_w$ whose inverse is continuous at $h(0)$. Consequently, $C_p(K)$ and $C_w(L)$ are not homeomorphic for any infinite compact Hausdorff spaces $K$ and $L$. This settles Krupski's problem and its two-space version due to Krupski and Marciszewski, and answers a question of Kąkol, Leiderman, and Michalak concerning $C_p([0,1])$ and weak Banach spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Joint Moments of Bilinear Resolvents
Functional Analysis.summary: Given $A,B\in B\left(H\right)_{+}$, we consider the existence and uniqueness of a positive operator $C\in B\left(H\right)_{+}$ such that \[ \left(I+mA+nB+mnC\right)^{-1}=\int_{\left[0,1\right]^{2}}s^{m}t^{n}dE\left(s,t\right),\quad m,n\geq0, \] for a positive operator-valued measure $E$. This is a joint Hausdorff moment problem. Without $C$, it holds if and only if $AB=BA$. In dimension two we give a complete criterion for noncommuting pairs. In higher finite dimensions, nonexistence is generic. Under certain spectral and cyclicity assumptions, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition on arbitrary Hilbert spaces. The completion is unique in this case. We also classify these pairs up to unitary equivalence. The class includes irreducible infinite-dimensional examples, even with continuous spectrum.

Functional Analysis.title: Operator Fejér--Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial with bounded-operator coefficients that is positive semidefinite on $K$ belongs to the operator quadratic module generated by $S$. We also show that if such a polynomial has degree at most $\tt{d}$, then it admits a certificate of weighted degree at most $\tt{d}+c_S$, where $c_S$ depends only on $S$, not on the polynomial or the coefficient Hilbert space.
  In contrast to the scalar case, where natural preorderings admit the degree bound $\tt{d}$ independently of $K$, we show that no uniform additive constant exists for natural matrix preorderings. We construct quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials positive semidefinite on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees in the corresponding natural preorderings diverge as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap length remains bounded below. Conversely, we establish uniform bounds of the form $\tt{d}+C$ for families of interval unions contained in a fixed compact interval when interval lengths and gap lengths have uniform positive lower bounds.
  Our proofs develop two techniques that may be of independent interest. First, a quadratic reduction principle represents arbitrary-degree operator polynomials as compressions of quadratic ones on enlarged Hilbert spaces. A perturbation argument and the closedness of truncated operator quadratic modules then extend uniform degree bounds from the quadratic case to arbitrary degrees with linear degree bounds of slope $1$. Second, a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil transfers positivity on interval unions to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fejér--Riesz theorem yields certificates.

Functional Analysis.title: High-order fractional linear differential equations do not describe stochastic processes with finite state space
Functional Analysis.summary: The replacement of the classical derivative in the governing equation of a continuous-time Markov process with finite state space by a fractional derivative of arbitrary order $α>1$ produces solutions that are mathematically incompatible with the theory of stochastic processes.
Functional Analysis.comment: AI software is not used at all. Delft University of Technology, report 20260421 on https://www.nas.ewi.tudelft.nl/people/Piet/TUDelftReports.html

Functional Analysis.title: Corona and Gleason problems for certain Banach spaces of holomorphic functions
Functional Analysis.summary: We use a combination of the classical dead-end space method and the interpolation (by bounded holomorphic functions) method to affirmatively solve Corona and Gleason problems for familiar Banach spaces of holomorphic functions such as (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces of holomorphic functions on bounded symmetric domains (including the unit ball and polydisc) in $\mathbb{C}^n$, holomorphic mean (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces, (Besov-)Hardy-Sobolev spaces and some special classes of holomorphic mixed-norm (Bergman) spaces (including weighted Bergman spaces) as well as some special classes of holomorphic (mean) Besov-Lipschitz spaces on the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Indeed, we extend our recent work on both problems for holomorphic Lipschitz algebras.
Functional Analysis.comment: 33 pp.; The arXiv: 2302.03433 is divided in 3 parts: (1) discusses the test case for the corona problem, Extracta Math. Vol 41 (2026), which also gives a solution to Fornaess and Ovrelid's problem (1983); (2) provides a solution to the original corona problem; and (3) this article provides solutions to corona and Gleason's problems for certain familiar Banach spaces of holomorphic functions

Functional Analysis.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
Functional Analysis.summary: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.

Functional Analysis.title: Bilinear maximal functions associated with some degenerate surfaces on the Heisenberg group
Functional Analysis.summary: Motivated by the works of Lee--Shuin and Borges--Foster on the Euclidean space, in this article we consider bilinear averages on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n$ corresponding to some degenerate surfaces associated with the Korányi norm as well as Nevo--Thangavelu type averaging structures, and study the boundedness of the their full and lacunary maximal functions on various $L^{p}(\mathbb{H}^n) \times L^{q}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ spaces, for $n \geq 2$. For the full maximal functions, we obtain optimal range except possibly at the end points.

Functional Analysis.title: Extension of kappa-additive measures
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish an extension theorem for kappa-additive probability measures, where kappa is an arbitrary uncountable cardinal. Starting from a <kappa-algebra, we define an outer measure using coverings of cardinality at most kappa and characterise measurable sets by approximation in outer measure of symmetric differences. We prove that these sets form a kappa-algebra carrying a complete kappa-additive extension of the original measure. The extension is unique on the generated kappa-algebra, and its completion is the minimal domain admitting a complete kappa-additive extension. We also establish attainment of the covering infimum and show why the closure assumption on the initial algebra is essential. Examples include a strict extension of classical Lebesgue measure under the additional hypothesis add N = aleph_1 < cov N.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for solvable and semisimple Lie groups
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we obtain the sharp constants for Hausdorff--Young inequalities on simply connected, completely solvable Lie groups, and connected real semisimple Lie groups with finite center.

Functional Analysis.title: Planar Convexity of Isotropy Orbits via Cohomology and Common Zeros
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a noncompact simple real Lie algebra with a Cartan decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{p}$. Let $K$ denote the connected Lie group corresponding to $\mathfrak{k}$. Then $K$ acts on $\mathfrak{p}$ via the adjoint representation. In this paper, we prove that for every $C\in\mathfrak{p}$ and every real linear map $L:\mathfrak{p}\to\mathbb{R}^2$, the linear image $L(K\cdot C)$ of the orbit $K\cdot C\subset\mathfrak{p}$ is convex in $\mathbb{R}^2$, except for the circle orbits when $\mathfrak{g}\cong\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $C\ne0$. By the two-piece property of isotropy orbits, any point omitted from the interior of the convex hull of a planar projection induces a nonzero class in the first integral cohomology of the orbit. This class vanishes directly in the non-Hermitian case, whereas in the Hermitian case we show that it vanishes by using the central circle action and a common-zero theorem of Gichev for Laplace eigenfunctions. Our approach treats classical and exceptional noncompact simple real Lie algebras uniformly and extends to real semisimple Lie algebras via Minkowski sums.

Functional Analysis.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be induced by a normal $τ$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},τ)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.

Functional Analysis.title: Jensen--Mercer-type Inequalities and Strongly $f$-Divergences
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we develop refined Jensen--Mercer-type inequalities for strongly convex functions, including reverse inequalities in the differentiable case. We identify the relationships between these inequalities and known bounds. Our method exploits a structural decomposition of strongly convex functions together with classical convexity arguments. As applications, we obtain explicit and computable bounds for strongly $f$-divergences, leading to new quantitative estimates for major divergence measures such as the Kullback--Leibler divergence, $χ^{2}$-divergence, Hellinger divergence, Bhattacharyya-type divergence, and Jeffreys divergence.

Functional Analysis.title: A Constructive Framework for Generalized Fourier Transforms via Truncate-and-Generalized Limits
Functional Analysis.summary:
This paper introduces a constructive definition of generalized Fourier transforms based entirely on ordinary truncated Fourier integrals and ordered dual-domain limits, within the framework of improper Riemann integration and classical analysis. The proposed truncate-and-generalized-limit (t.g.l.) formulation does not require test-function spaces, Lebesgue measure theory, or duality pairings in its proofs: the forward and inverse transforms are defined directly through finite-domain truncation of the target function, followed by successive ordered limits in the time and frequency domains.
  As consequences of this constructive definition, the formulation provides a unified treatment of non-decaying, oscillatory, and locally singular functions beyond the classical L1(R) setting; reveals an inherent asymmetry between the forward transform, interpreted as a first-order generalized-limit family, and the inverse transform, which requires frequency-domain truncation to generate pointwise reconstruction through Dirichlet-type oscillatory localisation; and clarifies the distinction between the t.g.l. approach and distribution theory, where generalized Fourier transforms are introduced through duality pairings rather than constructed from ordinary integrals. The inversion formula is established rigorously for two concrete admissible classes using only the classical Dirichlet convergence theorem. Several examples confirm that the framework covers constants, polynomials, periodic functions, singular kernels, and chirp signals within a single constructive scheme.
Functional Analysis.comment: Submitted to the Journal of Fourier Analysis and Applications v2: Added Section 6.7 discussing the suitability of improper Riemann integration for oscillatory Fourier integrals and its relation to the Dirichlet kernel. Added reference to Feichtinger and Jakobsen (2020). Submitted to the Journal of Fourier Analysis and Applications

Functional Analysis.title: On the dichotomy of $p$-walk dimensions on metric measure spaces II
Functional Analysis.summary: On a volume doubling metric measure space endowed with a family of $p$-energies such that the Poincaré inequality and the capacity upper bound with $p$-walk dimension $β_p$ hold, for $p$ in an open interval $I\subseteq(1,+\infty)$, we prove the following dichotomy: either $β_p=p$ for all $p\in I$, or the function $p\mapsto \frac{β_p}{p}$ takes values in $(1,+\infty)$ and is strictly decreasing on $I$. Moreover, if the metric measure space is $d_h$-Ahlfors regular, we prove the following dichotomy: either $β_p=d_h+p-1$ for all $p\in I$, or the function $p\mapsto \frac{β_p-d_h}{p-1}$ takes values in $(-\infty,1)$ and is strictly increasing on $I$.

Functional Analysis.title: Revisiting the Upper Bild of Quaternionic Numerical Ranges
Functional Analysis.summary:
The upper bild of the quaternionic numerical range provides a convex representative of the generally nonconvex quaternionic numerical range. Although its convexity is known, the geometry of the upper bild is difficult to describe explicitly, even for 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices.
  In this paper, we revisit the upper bild of quaternionic numerical ranges from both algebraic and geometric viewpoints. We first point out gaps in Kumar's proof. We then investigate several special classes of 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices and describe their shapes and boundary structures in the closed upper complex half-plane directly in terms of the standard eigenvalues and the off-diagonal entry of the Schur form.
  For the general 2-by-2 case, we use a different canonical form. Following So and Thompson, we prove the concavity of the upper-boundary function through the associated complex representation. For the lower boundary, we obtain a distance-to-a-disk representation and use convex optimization to prove its convexity. We also treat the degenerate cases. Together with the connectedness of the vertical sections, these results give an alternative proof of the convexity of the upper bild for arbitrary quaternionic matrices.

Functional Analysis.title: Pseudo-Fredholm operators form a regularity on Hilbert spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. We prove that the class of pseudo-Fredholm operators on $H$ is a regularity in the sense of Kordula and Müller. We also prove that the classes of left and right generalized Drazin invertible operators are regularities on $H$. Consequently, the generalized Kato spectrum and the corresponding generalized Drazin spectra satisfy the spectral mapping theorem. We construct an operator $T$ on a separable complex Banach space such that $T^2$ is right generalized Drazin invertible whereas $T$ is not pseudo-Fredholm. In particular, the power axiom need not hold for pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach spaces. Finally, we show that the accumulation sets of the approximate point and surjectivity spectra define regularities on Banach spaces, yielding another proof of the regularity of generalized Drazin invertible operators in $\B(X)$.

Functional Analysis.title: A Hardy space approximation supporting zero-free half-planes for the $ζ$-function
Functional Analysis.summary: By a theorem of Bagchi, the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if $E(s) = 1/s$ belongs to the closed linear span of $G_k(s) = (k^{-s} - k^{-1})ζ(s)/s$, $k \geq 2$, in the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{C}_{1/2})$, where $\mathbb{C}_α$ is the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s) > α$. The formal Möbius expansion $E = \sum_{k \geq 2} μ(k) G_k$ diverges on the critical line, by a theorem of Báez-Duarte. We study it in the scale of spaces $H^2(\mathbb{C}_α)$, where its convergence forces $ζ$ to be zero-free in $\mathbb{C}_α$. We prove that the partial sums $S_n$ converge to $E$ in $H^2(\mathbb{C}_α)$ for every $α> 1$, and that a single zero of $ζ$ in $\mathbb{C}_α$ keeps the best-approximation error $d_n(α)^2$ uniformly away from zero. We express the Möbius error $s_n(α) = \|S_n - E\|^2_α$ as a series with elementary terms, free of $ζ$, and compute it for $n \leq 10^6$: $s_n(1/2)$ oscillates without decaying, whereas for $α> 1/2$ it decays at a rate close to $n^{1-2α}$, much faster than the bound known under RH. On the critical line, $d_n(1/2)^2$ behaves like $0.046/\log n$ for $100 \leq n \leq 5120$, in agreement with earlier computations by Báez-Duarte, Balazard, Landreau and Saias.

Functional Analysis.title: Small Hankel operators on weighted Besov spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We characterize bounded small Hankel operators from $B_p(\om)$ to $\overline{B_q(\om)}$ on the polydisc for $0<p,q<\infty$, under explicit conditions relating the kernel parameter to the weight. When $q<p$, boundedness is equivalent to a weighted Besov condition on the symbol; when $p\le q$, it is equivalent to a weighted supremum condition on a shifted radial derivative. In particular, the diagonal case is characterized by the product Bloch space. The proof combines weighted Bergman duality and atomic factorization with local kernel estimates and randomized atomic tests.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Pathwise uniqueness by noise for singular stochastic PDEs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Uniqueness for stochastic PDEs with drift in differential form is a main open problem in the recent literature on regularisation by noise. This paper establishes a self-contained theory in the framework of stochastic evolution equations on separable Hilbert spaces and provides a first result to address such an issue, in the direction of both pathwise and weak uniqueness, as well as continuous dependence on the initial data. The singularity of the drift allows to achieve novel uniqueness results for several classes of examples, ranging from fluid-dynamics to phase-separation models.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Weak and Sharp Stretched-Exponential Flocking in the Kinetic Cucker-Smale Model with Noncompactly Supported Initial Data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the long-time behavior of the kinetic Cucker-Smale model under initial data with unbounded support in both position and velocity. Such data invalidate classical diameter-based flocking arguments and make sustained spatial cohesion difficult to establish. We prove an estimate for spatial characteristics under a finite spatial second moment and a sufficiently high velocity moment, without any requirement on coupling strength. We also prove weak flocking, i.e. control of spatial variance and integrability of velocity fluctuations in time. Under stronger assumptions on the initial tails, we establish uniform propagation of spatial exponential moments of explicitly determined order, a substantially stronger conclusion than bounded spatial variance. These estimates lead to explicit stretched-exponential rates of velocity alignment and convergence of the centered spatial distribution toward a limiting profile. Another contribution is the construction of countably atomic solutions that show optimality of the decay exponent in the spatial-tail-limited class. Together, the results clarify how initial phase-space tails govern spatial confinement and quantitative flocking for kinetic distributions without compact support.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the Gross-Pitaevskii equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove a nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the repulsive Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation with a time-dependent trapping potential $V(x,t)$. If either (i) $V(\cdot,t)$ is smooth, subquadratic in space and with uniformly bounded spatial derivatives of order $\geq 2$, or (ii) $V(\cdot,t)$ is a uniformly bounded perturbation of a fixed non-negative potential which is asymptotically $|x|^m, m\geq 2$, then the GP equation has a global solution, which remains uniformly close to the instantaneous minimizer of the time-independent GP functional, provided the initial condition is a ground state. In fact, we show that the existence of a solution of the GP equation is the real bottleneck: If existence is assumed, then adiabaticity holds under very minimal assumptions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Wave packet decompositions and sharp bilinear estimates for rough Hamiltonian flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The goal of this paper is to prove bilinear $L^p$ estimates for rough dispersive evolutions satisfying non-degeneracy and transversality assumptions. The estimates generalize the sharp Fourier extension estimates for the cone and the paraboloid. We obtain the sharp dependence on transversality and sharp up to endpoints $L^p$ range. To this end, we combine an axiomatic induction-on-scales with the construction of a wave packet parametrix for dispersive equations with $C^{1,1}$-coefficients by using the FBI transform.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and radial symmetry of magnetic skyrmions
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This paper establishes radial symmetry and uniqueness of magnetic
  skyrmions as global minimizers of the simplest local micromagnetic
  energy. The strategy is to show that any radial critical point with
  strictly decreasing out-of-plane component is the unique minimizer
  in the class of general degree-one maps with the prescribed limit at
  infinity. To this end, we identify a class of null Lagrangians that
  is sufficiently flexible to contain a calibration, giving a uniform
  lower bound for the energy that is uniquely saturated on the
  critical point. Our arguments provide a blueprint for proofs of
  symmetry and uniqueness of minimizers in vectorial variational
  problems under topological constraints.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Unified Space-Time Variational Framework for Wave Equations on Differential Forms
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We revisit a standard space--time variational formulation of the scalar wave equation in the setting of differential forms. For this, we use as spatial operator the nonnegative, self-adjoint (relative) \emph{Hodge--Laplacian} on a bounded Lipschitz domain. Its spectral decomposition reduces the wave problem in any form degree to the same family of scalar ordinary differential equations that underlies existing space-time analysis. We illustrate how this can be used to transfer results from the scalar wave equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions to other wave-type problems. In particular, we connect the framework to perfectly electrically conducting Maxwell problems.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Liouville theorem for monotone solutions of the Lane-Emden system in a half-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
The Lane-Emden system is an important model case of Hamitonian elliptic systems. We here consider the zero-Dirichlet problem in a half-space for arbitrary powers $p,q\ge1$. We prove that any nonnegative classical solution that is nondecreasing in the normal direction is necessarily trivial. No bound at infinity of any kind is assumed and this extends the known scalar monotonicity theorem.
  We also obtain the same conclusion for the scalar equation $-Δu=f(u)$ when $f\in C^1([0,\infty))$ is nonnegative, $f(0)=0$, $f\not\equiv0$, and $f(s)/s$ is nondecreasing for $s>0$. This relaxes the convexity and $C^2$ regularity requirements on $f$ in previous works.
  To prove these results we introduce a new method, completely different from the normal convexity approach from previous works, which relies on a delicate combination of techniques and could be applied to more general systems. Our basic tool is a suitable average of the linear interpolant between the solution and its normal limit on each finite strip. We next use stability estimates, combined with an energy argument for the scalar equation, or a contraction argument relying on Bessel potentials and the Schur test for the system. Increasing the strip height then forces the solution to vanish.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The partial data Calderón problem in dimension three
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider an inverse boundary value problem for the time-independent Schrödinger equation in dimension three. We prove that the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map defined near a boundary point uniquely determines the potential in a neighborhood of the boundary point in the interior. In particular, we show that the uniqueness question can be reduced to the injectivity of a weighted X-ray transform, which links inverse boundary value problems to integral geometry.
