Analysis of PDEs.title: On the dimension drop for harmonic measure on uniformly non-flat Ahlfors-David regular boundaries
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We extend earlier results of Azzam on the dimension drop of the harmonic measure for a domain $Ω\subset \R^{n}$ with $n\geq 3$, with dimensional Ahlfors regular boundary $\partialΩ$ of dimension $s$ with $n-1-δ_0 \leq s\leq n-1$, that is uniformly non flat. Here $δ_0$ is a small positive constant dependent on the parameters of the problem. Our novel construction relies on elementary geometric and potential theoretic considerations. We avoid the use of Riesz transforms and compactness arguments, and also give quantitative bounds on the $δ_0$ parameter.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Calderón problem for near-Euclidean metrics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this article, we consider the anisotropic Calderón problem of determining the potential from boundary measurements of the time-independent Schrödinger equation on compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary. We prove a global uniqueness theorem for small perturbations of the Euclidean metric.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Time-Decay Rates toward Rarefaction Waves for the One-Dimensional Isentropic Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: While the asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations has been well established since the pioneering works of Matsumura--Nishihara \cite{MatsumuraNishihara1986} and Liu--Xin \cite{LiuXin1988}, the classical $L^2$ energy method yields only qualitative convergence in $L^\infty(\R)$ as $t\to\infty$ without any explicit decay rate. In this paper, we establish for the first time a standalone \(L^4\) energy estimate for perturbations of a weak rarefaction wave in the one-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes system, thereby obtaining the first explicit algebraic time-decay rates for this model. Specifically, for small initial perturbations in $H^2(\R)$ and small wave strength $δ$, we prove that $(v-V,u-U)$ decays in $L^4(\R)$ at the rate \[ \|(v-V,u-U)(t)\|_{L^4}\le C\bigl(\|(v_0-V(0),u_0-U(0))\|_{H^2}+\sqrtδ\bigr)(1+t)^{-1/8}, \] where \((V,U)\) denotes the smooth rarefaction wave, while the relative Riemann invariants \(z_\pm\) of the perturbed system decay in \(L^\infty(\R)\) at the rate \((1+t)^{-1/6}\). The proof relies on a new local quartic energy estimate for \(z_\pm\) and \(z_\pm-Q\), where \(Q=μ(v)v_x-μ(V)V_x\), as well as a nonlocal half-space wave-interaction functional for corrected characteristic modes and a weighted higher-order derivative energy estimate coupled at the scale of the one-dimensional Nash inequality.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global existence and decay estimates of solutions for the compressible Prandtl type equations in Sobolev spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper addresses the global existence and large-time decay of solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces. We study small perturbations around a monotone shear flow and establish global weighted Sobolev estimates together with precise time-decay rates for the solutions. The main difficulties are that the normal velocity causes a loss of one tangential derivative, the variable density gives rise to nonstandard boundary and shear-flow coupling terms, and the global-in-time argument requires sufficiently strong decay to close the time-weighted energy estimates. To overcome these difficulties, we combine the cancellation method introduced by Masmoudi and Wong~\cite{MW2015} with the good-quantity approach developed by Paicu and Zhang~\cite{PZ2021}, together with weighted shear-flow estimates and a careful treatment of the natural boundary structure. Under suitable assumptions on the density perturbation, the shear flow, and the function $f(t)$ describing the outer tangential flow, we prove the global-in-time well-posedness of solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces. In this sense, the present result may be viewed as a Sobolev-space counterpart of the recent analytic-framework result obtained by Chen, Huang and Li (J. Funct. Anal. 286 (2024), 110322)~\cite{CHL2024} for the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl-type equations, while requiring a weaker time-decay assumption on the density perturbation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Generalized Hamiltonian gradient flow of contact type II: singularities, cut locus, and controllability
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study singularities, cut loci and controllability for time-dependent contact Hamilton--Jacobi equations. A contact version of Arnaud's theorem identifies the superdifferential graph of an evolved profile with the contact Hamiltonian image of the differential graph of its positive Lax--Oleinik regularization. This representation defines intrinsic singular characteristics and determines their initial velocity through a minimum-energy selection on the space-time superdifferential. The curves are continuous and locally $1/2$-Hölder, but they need not be locally Lipschitz. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal even for a quadratic Hamiltonian. The intrinsic characteristic issued from a cut point is singular at every later time in the short-time interval. We also establish the contact Lax--Oleinik commutator identities, which identify the superlevel and sublevel sets of the cut time with the corresponding terminal momentum graphs through bi-Lipschitz maps. For reachable terminal data we characterize the associated calibrated sets, and we describe all continuous initial data that reach a prescribed semiconcave profile. The proofs use Herglotz' variational principle and short-time estimates for contact fundamental solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Negatively Curved Minimal Surfaces in the Round Four-Sphere
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct smooth closed embedded minimal surfaces with everywhere negative Gaussian curvature in the unit round four-sphere. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $m$, our construction gives a minimal surface $Σ_m$ of genus $m^2+1$ such that $\operatorname{Area}(Σ_m)\to 4π^2$ as $m\to+\infty$. This result yields a complete solution to Problem 101 in Yau's 1982 list of open problems.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 65 pages, 7 figures. v2: Substantially revised exposition; routine computations in Riemannian geometry moved to the appendices. All comments are welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: On $W^{2,1}$-Regularity for Rivière's System with a Local Hardy Drift
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the endpoint regularity of weak solutions to the inhomogeneous Rivière system $$ -Δu=Ω\cdot\nabla u+f \qquad\text{in }B_1\subset\mathbb R^2, $$ with an antisymmetric potential $Ω\in L^2$ and a local Hardy drift term $f\in h^1$. We construct a continuous solution in $W_0^{1,2}$, which fails to belong to $W^{2,1}$ in every neighborhood of the origin, even when $\|Ω\|_{L^2}$ is arbitrarily small. Smooth truncations further show that the corresponding uniform interior $W^{2,1}$ estimate fails even for smooth solutions and coefficients. Thus, the $L\log L$ assumption ensuring local $W^{2,1}$ regularity cannot in general be replaced by componentwise local Hardy data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dynamics of solutions to the Korteweg--de Vries equation on a $\mathcal{Y}$-junction
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the long-time behavior of solutions to the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a Y-junction, a metric graph consisting of one incoming and two outgoing half-lines joined at a vertex. We first identify vertex conditions of separating-derivative type, together with a balance between the nonlinear coefficients and the coupling parameters, under which the problem is globally well-posed in $L^2$ for arbitrarily large data. This regime coincides with the one in which the explicit solitary waves of the junction, recently constructed by Mugnolo, Noja and Seifert (2025), exist. Using virial inequalities in the spirit of Muñoz and Ponce (2019), we then establish decay, in the sense of liminf, of the $L^2$ norm of the solution in time-dependent regions far from the solitons. In the strongly dominated linear region, which moves away from the vertex, the three edges decouple and the decay holds for every admissible choice of parameters. In the weakly dominated linear region, which stays close to the vertex, the topology of the graph produces boundary contributions at the vertex, and the decay is obtained under an algebraic condition on the coupling parameters that makes these contributions cancel. Finally, we discuss adaptations to general star graphs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Chemotaxis-Stokes system with $p$-Laplacian slow diffusion: global boundedness across the full $p>2$ range
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
The global boundedness problem for three-dimensional chemotaxis-fluid systems with nonlinear diffusion presents substantial analytical challenges, particularly in the near-linear diffusion regime. Indeed, the porous-medium and p-Laplacian diffusion operators approach the classical Laplacian as $m\searrow1$ and $p\searrow2$, and the extra a priori control afforded by nonlinear structures becomes increasingly difficult to exploit. This difficulty is reflected in the porous-medium setting, where establishing boundedness throughout $m>1$ required a sequence of substantial developments spanning more than a decade (2010-2024). For the p-Laplacian case, despite significant progress, the problem remained open in the near-linear range $2<p\le p^*(\approx2.01)$, due to the saturation of classical Moser-type iterations as $p\searrow2$.
  In this paper, we establish global bounded strong solutions for a three-dimensional chemotaxis-Stokes system with p-Laplacian slow diffusion and signal consumption. Our approach departs from the conventional $L^q$-iteration framework and develops a weighted energy method that directly exploits the coercive structure of the nonlinear diffusion operator. A weighted Rellich identity yields density estimates. To control the resulting boundary contribution on general smooth domains, we first use tangential differentiation along the boundary to lower its order, and then apply a trace-embedding estimate. Combined with a high-gradient/low-gradient decomposition, these estimates allow us to control the mixed chemotactic terms and close the coupled estimates for the density, signal, and fluid. The resulting estimates hold throughout $2<p\le 3$, thereby resolving the previously open range $2<p\le p^*$. Together with existing results for $p>p^*$, our work establishes boundedness throughout the entire slow-diffusion range $p>2$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Periodic Fisher-KPP equations on a regular tree
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study Fisher-KPP equations on regular trees with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate or in distance from a vertex or a bi-infinite geodesic. For nonzero finitely supported data, we characterize the spectral threshold between uniform extinction and persistence, including critical extinction. We establish Bramson corrections for Busemann step data at positive, zero and negative speeds and, above the periodic extinction threshold, for the largest Busemann coordinate and radial level positions of finitely supported solutions. When the periodic spectral minimum is nonpositive but the geodesic spectral threshold is positive, we construct a smallest positive stationary solution with exponential transverse decay, prove uniqueness under an exponential bound, and determine longitudinal spreading with its logarithmic correction. We also classify positive stationary solutions depending only on distance from the geodesic and prove existence and stability results for moving and stationary fronts.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Second order regularity of solutions of elliptic equations in divergence form with Sobolev coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We give $L^p$ estimates for the second derivatives of weak solutions to the Dirichlet problem for equation $\operatorname{div}(\mathbf{A}
abla u) = f$ in $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with Sobolev coefficients. In particular, for $f\in L^2(Ω)  igcap L^s(Ω)$ $$\|Δu\|_{2} \leq  egin{cases} c_1\|f\|_2 + c_2 \|
abla \mathbf{A}\|_q^2\|f\|_s, & 	ext{if } 1 < s < d/2,  rac{1}{2}= rac{2}{q}+  rac{1}{s} -  rac{2}{d}\ c_1\|f\|_2 + c_2 \|
abla \mathbf{A}\|_4^2\|f\|_s, & 	ext{if } s > d/2 \end{cases}.$$

Analysis of PDEs.title: Derivation of a nonlinear, history-dependent tissue-level current law for an electropermeabilization model via homogenization
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a phenomenological electropermeabilization model in a periodic medium representing biological tissue. Starting from a cell-level model describing the electric potential and the degree of poration, we perform dimensional analysis to identify a relevant scaling in terms of a small parameter $\varepsilon$ - the ratio between the cell and the tissue size. The electric potential satisfies electrostatic equations in the extra- and intracellular domains, while its jump across the cell membrane evolves according to a nonlinear law coupled with an ordinary differential equation for the poration degree. We prove the well-posedness of the microscopic problem, derive a priori estimates, obtain formal asymptotics, and rigorously justify the expansion by combining two-scale convergence with monotonicity arguments. The resulting macroscopic model exhibits memory effects and a nonlinear, time-dependent effective current. It captures the nontrivial evolution of effective conductivity, including a characteristic drop reflecting the capacitive behavior of the lipid bilayer, in agreement with experimental data. Numerical computations of the effective conductivity confirm that, although the intracellular and extracellular bulk conductivities are constant, tissue conductivity varies nonlinearly with electric field strength, showing a sigmoid trend.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global weak solutions with vacuum for isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the unit disk under Dirichlet boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct global weak solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson systems in the unit disk under no-slip boundary conditions, allowing vacuum and unbounded densities for sufficiently small initial energy. Such solutions particularly possess uniform $L^{q_0}$ density bounds for some $q_0>4γ$, beyond the natural energy class. Our analysis combines Green function representations with the mean-value property of harmonic functions to isolate a pressure-generated harmonic component of the effective viscous flux and obtain a purely interior potential representation valid for both systems. These results complement Perepelitsa's half-space theory (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 212 (2014), pp. 709-726) and our recent half-plane work (arXiv:2601.11852, 2026), treating bounded-domain geometry and Poisson coupling with nonnegative initial density.

Functional Analysis.title: An affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality via information decay
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ admits $S\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that $λ_1(SK)|K|^{2/n}\le Cn$, where $C$ is universal. For origin-symmetric bodies of volume one, the bound holds in maximal Gaussian measure position. The main step is the spectral estimate \[ λ_1(D)\le C(P)\bigl(n+\sqrt{n I(ν\midγ_n)}\bigr) \] for an even isotropic log-concave probability measure $ν$ supported on a symmetric convex body $D$, with Poincaré constant at most $P$ and finite relative Fisher information. A second-order Stein estimate and an information jump under convolution give entropy decay faster than $m^{-1}$ for normalised sums. Their supports control the Gaussian measure of dilates, and a Brownian bridge expansion gives the spectral estimate. A Gaussian-weighted ground state supplies a measure whose Fisher information is bounded in terms of $λ_1(K)$. The square-root dependence then gives the bound of order $n$.

Functional Analysis.title: Convexity of Radial Mean Bodies via an Extension of Ball's Bodies
Functional Analysis.summary:
In this work, we extend a classical theorem of Keith Ball on integrals of log-concave functions along rays against the weight $r^{p-1}$ to the previously inaccessible regime $p\in (-1,0)$: if $g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+$ is an integrable, upper semi-continuous, log-concave function which attains its maximum at the origin and has the origin in the interior of its support, then \[ x\mapsto \left(\frac{p}{g(o)}\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{p-1}(g(rx)-g(o))\mathrm{d}\,r\right)^{-\frac{1}{p}} \] is a gauge on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Our approach also provides a new proof of the original regime $p> 0$. The argument is based on a reduction to a two-dimensional inequality derived from Prékopa's theorem, which may be of independent interest.
  As a consequence of this extension, we resolve a nearly 30-year-old question of Richard Gardner and Gaoyong Zhang in the affirmative. In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_p K$ of a convex body $K\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ for $p>-1$. Furthermore, they established that $R_p K$ is convex for $p\geq 0$, but the convexity of $R_p K$ for $p\in (-1,0)$ remained open. We prove that $R_p K$ is convex for all $p>-1$.
Functional Analysis.comment: 23 pages. Substantially simplified presentation by assuming g in LC satisfies max g = g(0) and the origin lies in the interior of its support. Earlier versions treated the boundary case with lengthy proofs and approximation arguments that diluted the main results and proof ideas. These cases will be revisited in future work. Minor technical improvements throughout

Functional Analysis.title: Hardy transitions on product lattices
Functional Analysis.summary: Boundary conditions can change the dimensional scale of a sharp functional inequality. We determine this change for inverse-square Hardy inequalities on the product lattices $\mathbb N^k\times\mathbb Z^{N-k}$. Their sharp constants satisfy $C_{N,k}\sim N^2Ψ(k/N)$ uniformly for $1\le k\le N$, where $Ψ(α)\sim2α$ at zero. The law gives linear growth for a fixed number of positive coordinates, every intermediate power for suitable sublinear choices, and quadratic growth for a positive proportion. We develop a method that connects exact uncertainty inequalities with Hardy inequalities through logarithmic localization, and combines this transfer with a block decomposition to cover all proportions. The transfer holds on weighted graphs with an explicit geometric error and controls the variational problem over arbitrary functions. A mixture of two Mathieu ground energies determines $Ψ$. At the fully positive endpoint, the variational problem defining $κ=Ψ(1)$ has a unique nondegenerate minimum and a unique positive energy--moment minimizing profile. We also prove strict comparison with the continuum coefficient in every sector for $N\ge9$, the optimal uniform dimension.

Functional Analysis.title: Homotopy lifting, asymptotic homomorphisms, and traces
Functional Analysis.summary:
The following homotopy lifting theorem is proved: Let $φ, ψ: B \to D/I$ be homotopic $\ast$-homomorphisms and suppose $ψ$ lifts to a (discrete) asymptotic homomorphism. Then $φ$ lifts to a (discrete) asymptotic homomorphism. Moreover the whole homotopy lifts.
  \noindent We also prove a completely positive version of this theorem and a version where $φ$ is replaced by an asymptotic homomorphism. These are the first homotopy lifting theorems that hold for all separable C*-algebras.
  We obtain a lifting characterization of several important properties of C*-algebras and use them together with our homotopy lifting theorems to get the following applications:
  MF-property is homotopy invariant;
  If either $A$ or $B$ is exact, $A$ is homotopy dominated by $B$ and all amenable traces on $B$ are quasidiagonal, then all amenable traces on $A$ are quasidiagonal;
  If a C*-algebra $A$ is homotopy dominated by a nuclear C*-algebra $B$ and all (hyperlinear) traces on $B$ are MF, then all hyperlinear traces on $A$ are MF.
  Some of the extension groups introduced by Manuilov and Thomsen coincide.
  The C*-algebra $qA$ from Cuntz's picture of KK-theory is always quasidiagonal.
  Every homotopy symmetric C*-algebra is MF.
Functional Analysis.comment: New results are added. They state that every homotopy symmetric C*-algebra is MF and that the C*-algebra qA is always quasidiagonal. Also some new statements on extension groups are added

Functional Analysis.title: Sobolev spaces arising from the Stockwell transform on Gelfand pairs
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce a family of Sobolev-type spaces on Gelfand pairs, built from the Stockwell transform: a function belongs to the space of a given smoothness when its Stockwell transform, multiplied by a weight that grows with the smoothness, is square integrable. We prove that these spaces are Hilbert spaces, that they form a decreasing scale under continuous embeddings, and that an interpolation inequality controls the norm at an intermediate smoothness by the norms at the two endpoints. Under integrability conditions on the weight and on the family of analysing windows, they embed continuously into Lebesgue spaces. Under a local domination condition on the window, we show that their elements have bounded continuous representatives. On the Euclidean motion group, where the Stockwell transform reduces to a windowed Hankel transform, this gives boundedness and continuity as soon as the smoothness exceeds half the dimension, which is the classical threshold for Euclidean spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Tensor Products and the Isomorphic Theory of Daugavet Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct two separable Banach spaces with the Daugavet property whose injective and projective tensor squares, respectively, fail the Daugavet property. Both examples arise from one sequence of finite-dimensional extensions. The first space is the completion of the increasing union of the extensions, whereas the second is the closed span of their coordinate functionals. We will also investigate the operator Daugavet properties of these spaces later in the paper, also highlighting natural examples of metric spaces \(M\) for which \(\operatorname{Lip}_0(M)\) has the Daugavet property but fails to have the weak operator Daugavet property. Independently of this, we will also prove that every Banach space admits a linear isometric embedding into a Banach space which is not isomorphic to any Banach space with the Daugavet property.

Functional Analysis.title: Taylor-Accelerated Neural Network Interpolation Operators on Irregular Grids: Higher-Order Approximation and Derivative-Informed Field Reconstruction
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, a new class of Taylor-accelerated neural-network interpolation operators is introduced for quasi-uniform, irregularly distributed grids to reconstruct derivative-informed physical fields in both univariate and multivariate settings. The framework incorporates Taylor expansions within the neural network operators framework, allowing operators to efficiently utilize the smoothness of the target function. We determine the analytical properties of the proposed operators, including well-posedness, uniform boundedness, and exact interpolation at the sampling nodes. Additionally, we establish polynomial reproduction to a specified degree and provide Jackson-type error estimates based on higher-order moduli of smoothness, thereby improving convergence rates on quasi-uniform, irregular grids. The applicability of the method is demonstrated by reconstructing physical fields such as temperature, electromagnetic fields, and fluid properties, including pressure and velocity. The numerical results show that the proposed operators provide reliable, accurate estimates in the presence of noise and irregular sampling. The enhanced accuracy of the proposed method is validated by comparing it with current interpolation systems on irregular grids, including Lagrange-type methods.

Functional Analysis.title: Carleson Measures and Integral Operators on Fock--Sobolev Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
For integers $n\ge1$ and $N\ge0$, let $\mathbf g=(g_0,\ldots,g_N)$ be a vector of entire functions. We consider the generalized integral operator \ [T_{\mathbf g}^{(n,N)}f
  =I^n\!\left(\sum_{j=0}^N g_jf^{(j)}\right),
  \qquad (Ih)(z)=\int_0^z h(w)\dd w. \] We characterize its boundedness and compactness between Fock--Sobolev spaces $\F_m^p$ and $\F_\ell^q$, where $0<p,q<\infty$ and $m,\ell\ge0$ are integers. The coefficients of critical total degree determine the operator modulo compact operators and yield essential-norm estimates. In the Hilbert case, a Laurent Toeplitz representation gives the exact essential norm, a Fredholm criterion and an index formula. As an application, we obtain conditions for solutions of linear differential equations to belong to Fock--Sobolev spaces, including a necessary and sufficient polynomial zero condition in the Hilbert case. For entire functions $u_0,\ldots,u_N$ and $\varphi$, we also characterize boundedness, compactness and essential norms of the operators \[
  L_{\mathbf u,\varphi}^{(N)}f
  =\sum_{j=0}^N u_j\,f^{(j)}\circ\varphi. \] The proofs use Carleson measure characterizations for finite sums of weighted differentiation operators on Fock--Sobolev spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal Condition Numbers in Low-Rank Positive Semidefinite Matrix Sensing
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper we focus on the stability of positive semidefinite matrix sensing maps $Φ_{\mathcal{A}}=(\langle A_i,X\rangle)_{i=1}^m$ where $A_i\succeq 0$, $X\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r$. We introduce the bi-Lipschitz constants of $Φ_{\mathcal{A}}$ and define the global condition numbers as the ratio of upper and lower Lipschitz constants. We give deterministic universal lower bounds for these condition numbers that depend only on the rank $r$ and on the underlying field. We then show that rank-one Gaussian measurements asymptotically attain these bounds, except for the operator-norm condition number over $\mathbb R$ when $r=1$. For this exceptional case, we establish a sharper universal lower bound and prove its asymptotic sharpness. As an application, we derive stability guarantees for an $\ell_1$-residual PhaseLift-type estimator at the optimal sampling scale. These results identify the intrinsic limits of conditioning in positive semidefinite matrix sensing and connect these limits to stable low-rank recovery.

Functional Analysis.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
Functional Analysis.summary: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.

Functional Analysis.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $0<λ_1\leqλ_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ λ_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^kλ_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω) \frac{n}{n+2}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{ω_{n-1}}{ω_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

Functional Analysis.title: Linear Preservers of Semipositivity and Minimal Semipositivity
Functional Analysis.summary: We classify all real linear into preservers of semipositivity on $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$, $m,n\ge2$, relative to arbitrary source and target pairs of proper cones, without assuming invertibility or a prescribed form. The classification consists of product maps $L(A)=XAY$ and rank-$n$ degenerate maps $L(A)=Ψ(u^TA)$, subject to explicit cone and matrix-pencil conditions. For square minimal semipositivity with respect to the standard nonnegative orthant, preservation forces the operator to be invertible: for $n\ge2$, the linear into preservers are precisely the maps $L(A)=XAY$ and $L(A)=XA^TY$ with $X,Y\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ satisfying $X^{-1},Y^{-1}\ge0$. We also classify all linear preservers of orthant semipositivity from $M_{2,2}(\mathbb{R})$ to $M_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ into three disjoint classes, two of which consist of maps of rank three outside product form.

Functional Analysis.title: Algebraic properties of Toeplitz operators on annulus and multiply connected domains
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over the annulus and provide a complete characterization of them. Based on that, we single out a certain class of Toeplitz operators that satisfy the multiplicativity property and lead to a zero product theorem. We further extend the results for the general multiply-connected domain and prove the zero product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over such a domain.

Functional Analysis.title: Transfer of similarity to Hilbert space contractions through inner functions: a proof of Douglas's conjecture
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded operator on a Hilbert space and let $u$ be a non-constant Blaschke product, finite or infinite. We prove that if the spectrum of $A$ does not meet the closure of the set of poles of $u$, then $u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is. This settles a conjecture of R.G. Douglas. For infinite products $u$, no additional condition on the zeros beyond the Blaschke condition is required. We also show that '$u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is' for all non-constant inner functions $u$ whose reflected singularity set, the closure of the set of poles together with the singular support, avoids the spectrum of $A$. We also prove a weighted resolvent version of the theorem, which allows the poles to accumulate on the spectrum to a limited extent; a column criterion for partial products, which is shown to force their norm convergence; and a simultaneous version for commuting tuples of operators tested by separated inner functions sharing one Lyapunov operator. For finite Blaschke products we obtain a polynomial form of the Lyapunov operator, which gives an estimate for the similarity constants. We also characterise the tuples of finite Blaschke products that form a uniform strong test collection: they are exactly the tuples that are injective, with non-vanishing joint derivative, on the closed disc. Finally, we show by examples that the separation hypothesis cannot be replaced by the existence of a bounded $H^\infty$ calculus, by the existence of a norm radial limit, or by the strong convergence of the partial products, even for Ritt operators.

Functional Analysis.title: A Banach--Stone-like Theorem for Slowly Oscillating Functions
Functional Analysis.summary:
We prove that every lattice isomorphism between the lattices of slowly oscillating real-valued functions
  on proper metric spaces induces a coarse homeomorphism. This yields a Banach--Stone-like theorem for slowly oscillating functions,
  as well as a representation theorem for linear lattice isomorphisms between these function lattices. Both theorems were previously established by the author under the assumption of chain-connectedness. The present paper establishes both results for arbitrary proper metric spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Bound states at Trudinger--Moser growth: obstructions, pairing and bubbling
Functional Analysis.summary: We study radial solutions of the planar scalar field equation $$ -Δu+u=λu\,e^{u^2}, \qquad 0<λ<1, $$ whose nonlinearity has critical Trudinger--Moser growth. These solutions describe standing waves of the two-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations. Motivated by Tang's recent uniqueness result for radial bound states with power nonlinearities in higher dimensions, we investigate the validity of the corresponding uniqueness theory at critical exponential growth. We show that the Serrin--Tang criterion and two structural hypotheses in Tang's analysis fail in this setting. We establish a pairing principle for the shooting problem, prove that Tang's variation conditions force the nodal count to be non-decreasing, and show that any two radial ground states intersect. We also derive a second-order expansion of the Liouville bubble arising at large initial heights and compute the corresponding flux correction. These asymptotics yield formal predictions for the first zero and the nodal structure at large heights. Our results suggest that the ground state is unique, whereas nodal radial bound states, if they exist, occur in pairs, contrary to the uniqueness phenomenon for power nonlinearities.

Functional Analysis.title: Alternating chains and lattice strict singularity
Functional Analysis.summary: We present an alternating-chain argument intended to show that every lattice strictly singular operator from a real Banach lattice to a real Banach space is disjointly strictly singular. A hypothetical counterexample yields two LSS operators on a reflexive sequence lattice whose difference is bounded below. Quotienting by the range of that difference gives a common map bounded below on a positive tail cone. Finite chains of positive disjoint vectors, with alternating small differences, then lead to incompatible length estimates. We record the resulting operator and sequence consequences and extend the construction to common postcompositions with DSS errors. Independently of the proposed equality, we prove simultaneous nuclear restriction results for countable DSS families and uniform nuclear tails for norm-compact DSS families, together with common Hilbert-space factors and arbitrarily small nuclear corrections having a common infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples identify limits of these selection statements. The main equality is a candidate real-field proof; no complex-field equality is asserted.

Functional Analysis.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain a complete bound independent of the two disks, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.

Functional Analysis.title: The ball fixed point property for continuous functions on locally compact spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and $p\in K$. We prove that the Banach space $C(K,p)=\{f\in C(K,\mathbb R):f(p)=0\}$ fails the ball fixed point property (BFPP) whenever $p$ is non-isolated, answering a question of Avilés, Japón, Lennard, Martínez-Cervantes and Stawski. Consequently, $C_0(L)$ fails the BFPP for every noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space $L$. Together with Barroso's characterization for $C(K)$, this yields complete topological classifications of the BFPP for $C_0(L)$ and $C(K,p)$. We also resolve a second question of Avilés et al., showing that the BFPP of $C(K)$ implies that of $C(K,p)$ for every compact Hausdorff space $K$ and every $P$-point $p\in K$ if and only if there are no measurable cardinals.

Functional Analysis.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: KPZ universality
Functional Analysis.summary: We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and positive representing measure, together with joint profile convergence at every prescribed finite parameter list. We also prove convergence of the height evolution from general upper-semicontinuous initial profiles to the half-space KPZ fixed point. The associated passage field converges locally uniformly to the half-space directed landscape, jointly with evolutions from finitely many initial profiles driven by the same environment. The convergence results cover the critical boundary window and every fixed subcritical boundary rate, including zero. All fixed subcritical rates produce the same limiting laws.

Functional Analysis.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
Functional Analysis.summary: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.

Functional Analysis.title: A short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality in dimension three
Functional Analysis.summary: We give a short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality with sharp constant $2$ for matrices of dimension at most three.

Functional Analysis.title: Decay of Correlations for Multiplicative Functionals of Determinantal Point Processes
Functional Analysis.summary: The main result of this paper is an upper bound on the correlations of multiplicative functionals of determinantal point processes. In particular, for the sine process, the correlations of a multiplicative functional associated with a rapidly decaying function decay quadratically. It follows that the spectral density of such functionals belongs to the Sobolev space $H_1$.

Functional Analysis.title: Stochastic Euler Products in the Paley-Wiener Space
Functional Analysis.summary: General sufficient conditions, in terms of stochastic Euler products, are given for a realization of a point process to have finite excess or finite deficiency in the Paley-Wiener space.

Functional Analysis.title: The sharp Stein-Tomas inequality on the circle
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that constant functions are global maximizers for the endpoint Stein--Tomas inequality on $\mathbb{S}^1$, thereby determining its sharp constant. By the known characterization of the phases of maximizers, every nonzero maximizer then has the form $f(ω)=c e^{ix_0\cdotω}$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$.

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal lengths of commutators of idempotents and similarity of nilpotent operators to their negatives
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\HH$ be a complex separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We prove that every operator in $\BH$ is a sum of three commutators of idempotents and a product of two such commutators. Both numbers are best possible. The same is true for differences of idempotents, for operators similar to their negatives, and for operators anticommuting with an involution. Each of these four classes therefore has additive length three and multiplicative length two. We also construct nilpotent operators of order three that are similar to their negatives but cannot be conjugated to their negatives by any bounded involution. These results answer Question~7.22(a)--(c), the question in Remark~7.17, and the question about involutions in Section~2.9 of Marcoux, Radjavi and Zhang, \emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{284} (2023), 109854.

Functional Analysis.title: Similarity cancellation and primitive operator roots
Functional Analysis.summary: Kaplansky's second test problem for similarity asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$ for bounded operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We answer this question in the negative, even for compact operators whose singular values satisfy any prescribed positive upper bounds tending to zero. We also show that cancellation can fail under the stronger hypothesis $J_2(T)\sim J_2(S)$ considered by Marcoux, Radjavi, Troscheit, and Zhang \cite{MRTZ}. For these operators, finite amplifications and primitive roots are similar exactly at even multiplicities and even orders, respectively. In contrast, cancellation in fixed matrix size admits a uniform bound on the condition number. This extends the finite type~$I$ results of Jiang, Ma, Shi, and Zhang \cite{JMSZ}. The bound also holds for simultaneous similarity of arbitrary families of matrices and can be chosen to tend to one as the amplified bound tends to one. We conclude that, in a finite type~$I$ von Neumann algebra, cancellation of doubles and cancellation of primitive square roots are each equivalent to boundedness of the orders of its nonzero homogeneous summands.

Functional Analysis.title: Counterexamples to uniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform under quadratic decay
Functional Analysis.summary: We show nonuniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform on $\mathbb Z^2$ under quadratic decay. We construct an explicit nonzero function in $\ell^1(\mathbb Z^2)$ with pointwise decay $O(|z|^{-2})$ whose sums over integer lines vanish. We also obtain an infinite-dimensional null space with the same decay assumption. Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.

Functional Analysis.title: Construction of a Natural Transformation from a Classical to a Quantum 0-Species
Functional Analysis.summary: A natural transformation $\mathfrak{J}$ between functors valued in the category $\mathfrak{Chdv}_{0}$ is assembled. $\mathfrak{Chdv}_{0}$ is obtained by replacing both the categories $\mathrm{ptls}$ and $\mathrm{ptsa}$ with the category of topological linear spaces in the defining properties of the category $\mathfrak{Chdv}$ introduced in one of our previous papers. By letting a $\mathfrak{dp}$-valued functor be (classical) quantum whenever every its value is a dynamical pattern whose set map takes values in the set of (commutative) noncommutative topological unital $\ast-$algebras, and letting a (classical) quantum $0$-species be a $\mathfrak{Chdv}_{0}$-valued functor factorizing through the canonical functor from $\mathfrak{dp}$ to $\mathfrak{Chdv}_{0}$ into a (classical) quantum $\mathfrak{dp}$-valued functor, we have that the domain and codomain of $\mathfrak{J}$ are a classical and a quantum $0$-species respectively.
Functional Analysis.comment: Added in front-page address, email, URLs

Functional Analysis.title: Stokes-type Integral Equalities for Scalarly Essentially Integrable Locally Convex Vector Valued Forms which are Functions of an Unbounded Spectral Operator
Functional Analysis.summary: In this work we establish a Stokes-type integral equality for scalarly essentially integrable forms on an orientable smooth manifold with values in the locally convex linear space $\langle B(G),σ(B(G),\mathcal{N})\rangle$, where $G$ is a complex Banach space and $\mathcal{N}$ is a suitable linear subspace of the norm dual of $B(G)$. This result widely extends the Newton-Leibnitz-type equality stated in one of our previous articles. To obtain our equality we generalize the main result of that article, and employ the Stokes theorem for smooth locally convex vector valued forms established in a prodromic paper. Two facts are remarkable. Firstly the forms integrated involved in the equality are functions of a possibly unbounded scalar type spectral operator in $G$. Secondly these forms need not be smooth nor even continuously differentiable.
Functional Analysis.comment: Added in front-page address, email, URLs

Functional Analysis.title: Frechet differential of a power series in Banach algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We present two new forms in which the Frechet differential of a power series in a Banach algebra can be expressed in terms of absolutely convergent series involving the commutant $C(T):A\mapsto [A,T]$.Then we apply the results to the analytic functional calculus in a complex Banach space.
Functional Analysis.comment: Added in front-page address, email, URLs

Functional Analysis.title: Use of bundles of locally convex spaces in problems of convergence of semigroups of operators defined on different Banach spaces. Applications to spectral stability problems
Functional Analysis.summary: In this work we construct certain general bundles $<\mathfrak{M},ρ,X>$ and $<\mathfrak{B},η,X>$ of Hausdorff locally convex spaces associated with a given Banach bundle $<\mathfrak{E},π,X>$. Then we present conditions ensuring the existence of bounded sections $\mathcal{U}\in Γ^{x_{\infty}}(ρ)$ and $\mathcal{P}\in Γ^{x_{\infty}}(η)$ both continuous at a point $x_{\infty}\in X$, such that $\mathcal{U}(x)$ is a $C_{0}-$semigroup of contractions on $\mathfrak{E}_{x}$ and $\mathcal{P}(x)$ is a spectral projector of the infinitesimal generator of the semigroup $\mathcal{U}(x)$, for every $x\in X$.
Functional Analysis.comment: Added in front-page address, email, URLs

Functional Analysis.title: Integral equalities for functions of unbounded spectral operators in Banach spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate a limiting procedure for extending local integral operator equalities to the global ones and to applying it to obtaining generalizations of the Newton-Leibnitz formula for operator-valued maps for a wide class of unbounded operators.
Functional Analysis.comment: Added in front-page address, email, urls

Functional Analysis.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. III
Functional Analysis.summary:
This paper is the third in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices of size $n\times k$ with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough.
  In this part we study the remaining case where $k = 3$ and $n \ge k + 2 = 5$ and prove that every linear map preserving the Cullis' determinant admits the same description as for the case where $k \ge 4$ and $n \ge k + 2$ obtained previously.

Functional Analysis.title: Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.

Functional Analysis.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part II: Abstract Integration in Net Convergence Structures
Functional Analysis.summary: The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.

Functional Analysis.title: Two-scale criteria for Poincaré and log-Sobolev inequalities with applications to Markov chain Monte Carlo
Functional Analysis.summary: Given a collection of distributions $\{P_{y}\}$ and a mixing distribution $ρ$ supported over $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, we propose new sufficient conditions under which the mixture / joint distribution satisfies a Poincaré or log-Sobolev inequality. We develop these sufficient conditions in a unified manner using the framework of $Φ$-Sobolev inequalities (Chafaï, 2004). The conditions that we develop in this work are satisfied by a variety of Markov chains, and consequently allows us to characterise the evolution of these functional inequalities for iterates generated by simulating these Markov chains. As a result, we obtain an clean error analysis for estimating a broad class of functionals using Markov chain Monte Carlo strategies along these Markov chains.
Functional Analysis.comment: v3: establish stronger W2 mixing with condition on kernel

Functional Analysis.title: Convergence of non-symmetric forms with changing reference measures
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop a functional-analytic theory of convergence for non-symmetric generalized Dirichlet forms defined on a sequence of Hilbert spaces $H_n$ converging to a limit space $H$ in the sense of Kuwae-Shioya, with the principal applications concerning $L^2$-spaces over varying reference measures $μ_n \to μ$. Extending Mosco's variational convergence for Dirichlet forms to the non-symmetric setting via a functional controlling the off diagonal values of the forms, we introduce a notion of generalized convergence of non-symmetric Dirichlet forms and show it to be equivalent to strong convergence of the associated resolvents, to weak convergence of the co-resolvents, and to strong graph convergence of the infinitesimal generators. A version of the Trotter-Kato theorem in the Kuwae-Shioya framework yields the corresponding equivalence for $C_0$-contraction semigroups. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for the generalized convergence of elliptic and sectorial $a_{i,j}$-forms with changing speed measures, both on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and in infinite dimensions over a Gelfand triple, and deduce weak convergence of the laws of the associated right processes under tightness of the path measures.

Functional Analysis.title: A new perspective on Riemann surfaces and von Neumann algebras via thin Blaschke products
Functional Analysis.summary:
In 2014, K.Guo and the second author constructed the first example of an infinite Blaschke product
  $B$ (a thin Blaschke product), for which the associated multiplication operator $M_B$ is irreducible
  on the Bergman space $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$ over the unit disk $\mathbb D$. We take a substantial step forward toward characterizing
  the irreducibility of the operator $M_B$ on
  $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, the trivialness of the von Neumann algebra
  $\{M_B,M_B^*\}'$. This characterization indicates a close connection with the primeness of $B$ and with
  the two-component property of the Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}_B$ associated with $B$. The approach is built upon
  a nested family of connected components of the sublevel set
  $\{z\in \mathbb{D}:|B(z)|<t\}$ for $0<t<1$, which captures the function-theoretic and geometric feature of $B$.

Functional Analysis.title: Additive preservers of mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with $\dim H\ge 2$. We characterize the nonzero additive maps on $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and on its self-adjoint part $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$ that preserve mutual strong numerical-radius orthogonality in one direction, assuming surjectivity only in infinite dimension. These maps are precisely those of the form $A\mapsto cUAU^*$, where $U$ is unitary or antiunitary, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar for $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and a nonzero real scalar for $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$.
Functional Analysis.comment: 16 pages. The surjectivity assumption has been removed in the finite-dimensional case

Functional Analysis.title: Banach Gelfand Triples with Kernel Theorems via Equivalence Bimodules
Functional Analysis.summary: Hilbert C*-modules whose coefficient C*-algebra is equipped with a finite faithful trace generate Banach Gelfand triples. This provides a natural setting for the interpretation of Hilbert C*-modules as function spaces. In particular, when the modules are finitely generated and projective, their external tensor products interact well with projective tensor products. This allowed us to derive abstract kernel theorems for Hilbert C*-modules. As an application, we apply our results to Heisenberg modules and obtain new kernel theorems for time-frequency analysis.
Functional Analysis.comment: Updated reference list. Added concluding examples. 43 Pages

Functional Analysis.title: Continuous, locally Lipschitz and Lipschitz selections for intuitionistic fuzzy sets, with applications to expert voting
Functional Analysis.summary: This paper studies continuous selections in the framework of intuitionistic fuzzy sets. To each intuitionistic fuzzy set $A=(μ,ν)$ on a topological space $X$ we associate the interval-valued map $F_{A}(x)=[μ(x),1-ν(x)]$, whose width is the hesitation degree. Hence, in this setting, a selection of $F_{A}$ is an ordinary fuzzy membership function compatible with the intuitionistic information, and every selection is the membership function of Atanassov's operator $D_{\vartheta}$ for a suitable pointwise parameter $\vartheta$. When $X$ is normal and $μ$, $ν$ are upper semi-continuous, a continuous selection exists by the Katětov--Tong insertion theorem. We show that upper semi-continuity arises naturally in a voting model, in which a panel of experts divides a metric universe into closed regions of acceptance and rejection, and for this model we construct an explicit continuous selection, the consensus selection, illustrated by a non-compact example in the plane. On metric spaces we characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets that admit an $L$-Lipschitz selection through a non-local version of the condition $μ+ν\leq 1$, and we give the largest and the smallest such selections in closed form. Finally, we prove that the set of continuous selections depends in a $1$-Lipschitz way on the intuitionistic fuzzy set, with respect to the Hausdorff-type distance of Grzegorzewski. We also characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets admitting locally Lipschitz selections.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral Theory and Continuum Norm Resolvent Convergence of a One-Sided Discrete Dirac-Type Operator
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate a one-dimensional discrete Dirac-type operator $D_d$ acting on the Hilbert space $\big(\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$, obtained from the classical continuous free Dirac operator by replacing the spatial derivative with the one-sided backward difference operator $I - S_1$, where $S_1$ denotes the right shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})$. We establish the fundamental operator-theoretic and spectral properties of $D_d$: unlike symmetric or supersymmetric lattice discretizations, $D_d$ is bounded and non-normal for every non-zero rest mass $m > 0$, with self-commutator $[D_d, D_d^†] = -2mc^3(-Δ_{\mathrm{disc}})σ_2$, yet it is quadratically normal. We compute the exact operator norm, determine the exact spectral radius in two mass regimes, and show via Fourier--Laurent analysis that the spectrum $σ(D_d)$ is purely continuous and lies on a two-component algebraic curve in the complex plane undergoing a topological transition at $mc^2 = 2c$. Finally, introducing a lattice spacing $h > 0$ and embedding $\big(\ell^2(h\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ isometrically into $\big(L^2(\mathbb{R};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ via Whittaker--Shannon band-limited interpolation, we prove that the scaled non-normal discrete Dirac-type operator $D_{d,h}$ converges to the continuous self-adjoint Dirac operator $D$ in the norm resolvent sense at the optimal rate $\mathcal{O}(h)$ as $h \to 0^+$, without requiring frequency cutoffs.

Functional Analysis.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
Functional Analysis.summary:
This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $κ$-barrelled and $ω$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $ω$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets.
  Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $σ$-compact, $ω$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_κ$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $ω$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.

Functional Analysis.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $(\mathcal T_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal A$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Cesàro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Cesàro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.

Functional Analysis.title: Polish spaces of separable Banach lattices
Functional Analysis.summary: We compare two Polish presentations of separable real Banach lattices: closed sublattices of a universal lattice and closed ideals of $\operatorname{FBL}[\ell_1]$. We construct translations preserving lattice isometry in both directions, continuous and injective from sublattices to ideals and Borel in the reverse direction. Natural generation and Fremlin tensor operations are $\boldsymbolΣ^0_2$-measurable with $G_δ$ graphs. Isometric lattice isomorphism in either universal coding is Borel bireducible with a complete orbit equivalence relation of Polish-group actions. Uniform monotonicity and order uniform smoothness are $\boldsymbolΠ^0_3$-complete in both codings, whereas strict monotonicity, order smoothness, and order continuity are coanalytic. Abstract $L_p$ and AM-spaces form closed classes of sublattice codes. We also give explicit Borel bounds for atom counts, compact order intervals, and the lattice-isometry classes of $L_p[0,1]$, $\ell_p$, and $c_0$.

Functional Analysis.title: Semiprojective Banach lattices
Functional Analysis.summary: We study a norm-controlled notion of semiprojectivity for Banach lattices, testing sequential quotient towers in separable ambient lattices and requiring arbitrarily small norm loss at a fixed stage. For a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff space $X$, we prove that $C_0(X)$ is semiprojective if and only if $X$ is compact and an absolute neighbourhood retract. Finite $\ell_1$-sums preserve semiprojectivity, and arbitrary $\ell_1$-sums of $1^+$-projective lattices are semiprojective without any order-unit assumption. By contrast, $\mathbb{R} \oplus_\infty \ell_1$ fails to be semiprojective, showing that neither semiprojectivity nor $1^+$-projectivity is preserved by finite $\ell_\infty$-sums, extensions, or pullbacks over a projective base. Every separable semiprojective lattice is $λ$-projective for some finite $λ$, and its scalar-valued lattice homomorphisms separate points. Consequently, a separable reflexive Banach lattice is semiprojective precisely when it is finite-dimensional, and no nonzero separable atomless order-continuous lattice is semiprojective. We also characterise $\ell$-openness as $1^+$-projectivity relative to separable ambient lattices; for separable domains this is ordinary $1^+$-projectivity. The restriction to separable ambient lattices is redundant for separable domains but affects the nonseparable examples.

Functional Analysis.title: Stable Initial-State Recovery from Dynamical Samples using Nagy-Type and Pollard-Hilding-Type Frame Perturbations
Functional Analysis.summary: Stimulated by Aldroubi and his collaborator's recent work on dynamical sampling, we consider a homogeneous discrete dynamical system of the form $f_n = A f_{n-1}= A^{n}f, \quad f_0 = f$, where A is a bounded linear operator on a separable Hilbert space H, which is known as the evolution operator, and $f_0 \in \mathcal{H}$ is the unknown initial state. The associated dynamical samples are given by the collection $\{\langle A^n f, g\rangle: g \in \mathcal{G, 0 \leq n < n < L(g)}\}$, where $\mathcal{G} \subset H$, is a finite or countable sampling set and $L$ is a function $L: G \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \bigcup \{\infty\}$. We analyze the stability of perturbed dynamical sampling systems in the sense of Nagy and Pollard-Hilding. More precisely, we establish sufficient conditions for the stable recovery of an initial state from perturbed dynamical samples obtained by changing the sampling vector, the evolution operator, ro simultaneously both, within the framework of Nagy-type and Pollard-Hilding-type perturbation of frames.

Functional Analysis.title: Estimates for convolution operators on Hardy spaces associated with ball quasi-Banach function spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $0 \leq α< n$, $N \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $X$ and $Y$ be ball quasi-Banach function spaces on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We consider operators $T_α$ defined by convolution with kernels of type $(α, N)$. Assuming that the powered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator satisfies a Fefferman-Stein vector-valued maximal inequality on $X$ and is bounded on the associated space, we prove that, for $α= 0$, $T_0$ extends to a bounded operator $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to X$ and $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n)$; and for $0 < α< n$, under certain additional assumptions on $X$ and $Y$, $T_α$ extends to a bounded operator $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to Y$ and $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to H_{Y}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. In particular, these results yield the corresponding estimates for singular integral operators and Riesz potentials. We also provide an off-diagonal Fefferman-Stein vector-valued inequality for the fractional maximal operator on the $p$-convexification of ball quasi-Banach function spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Hyperrigidity and convexity in two variables
Functional Analysis.summary: We extend Brown's one-variable rigidity theorem to strictly convex functions of two variables under a regularity assumption. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let $f$ be real-valued, strictly convex on $K$, and of class $C^2$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. We prove that the generating set $\{x_1,x_2,f\}$ is hyperrigid in $C(K)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stable soliton resolution for the corotational Skyrme model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the classical Skyrme model. Under corotational symmetry, we prove that (i) stationary solutions, or Skyrmions, are unique in every topological degree; (ii) the Cauchy problem is globally well-posed in a nonlinear energy space; and (iii) stable soliton resolution holds: every finite-energy solution scatters to the Skyrmion of the same degree. Our key observation is that subcritical equivariant Yang--Mills dynamics emerge near the origin and suppress concentration.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Rellich-Poincaré inequalities and improved Rellich inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study linear variational problems on bounded domains $Ω\subset \mathbb R^d$ involving the Dirichlet biharmonic operator $Δ^{2}$ and the Rellich potential $|x|^{-4}$, under the assumption $0\in\overlineΩ$. The case $0\in\partialΩ$ is particularly noteworthy and subtle.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform local smoothing for the derivative NLS and the soliton mass threshold
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Harrop-Griffiths, Killip, Ntekoume and Vişan proved that the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation (DNLS) is globally well-posed in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. A key ingredient of their proof is a local smoothing estimate. It holds on $L^2$-equicontinuous sets of initial data, but it cannot hold on $L^2$-balls, because rescaled stationary solitons, all of mass $2π$, violate it. This raises a natural question: for which masses $m$ does local smoothing hold uniformly on the ball $\{M(q_0)\le m\}$? We prove three results. First, we give a quantitative version of the local smoothing estimate in which the data enter only through the mass and an explicit frequency scale $κ(q_0)$. On time intervals of length $2T$ the bound grows like $1+κ(q_0)^2T$, and the stationary soliton shows that the power of $κ$ cannot be lowered below one. Second, we prove uniform local smoothing on balls of small mass, together with a scale-invariant Morrey-type form and a localized $L^4_{t,x}$ bound. Third, we analyse the soliton family from both sides. The uniform constant must blow up at least like $(2π-m)^{-1}$ as $m\uparrow 2π$, while every soliton of mass $m<2π$ satisfies local smoothing with a constant $O((2π-m)^{-1})$. These facts single out the stationary-soliton mass $2π$, which is also the Hayashi--Ozawa coercivity threshold, as the natural candidate for the sharp threshold. We formulate this as a conjecture, give a spectral reformulation in terms of the Kaup--Newell scattering data, and discuss the obstacles to a proof.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $ρ$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2πρ(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ))$ as $ρ\to 0$, and the condensate fraction $η$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $η= 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ)$ as $ρ\to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case.
  The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,χ_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Existence for a Drift-Diffusion Model of Electrical Discharge in MEMS
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a coupled elliptic-parabolic system modelling electrical discharge in a micro-electro-mechanical (MEMS) capacitor: a Poisson equation for the electrostatic potential, coupled to drift-diffusion equations for the ion and electron densities with a Townsend ionization source whose rate per electron grows linearly in the electric field. Gimperlein, He and Lacey proved local well-posedness and left open whether the densities blow up in finite time. We first prove a continuation criterion in a weak norm: a finite-time singularity forces the space charge to be unbounded in H^1_D, the dual of the space of H^1 functions vanishing on the electrodes, so blow-up cannot be quasi-neutral. We then exclude it altogether when the two diffusivities coincide and the vacuum field is bounded: the weak solution is then global in time. To our knowledge this is the first global existence result without smallness assumptions for a drift-diffusion-Poisson model of gas discharge whose ionization rate is unbounded in the field. The proof uses the electrostatic energy and the number of carriers in place of the usual free energy: the ionization source cancels in the energy balance, the Joule heating is dissipative, and the two quantities close through a linear Gronwall inequality. Numerical experiments on a discharge in a micrometre gap, with the Townsend constants and the mobilities of air, provide evidence for the extension to unequal diffusivities and bear on the existence of a breakdown threshold.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Anisotropic Minkowski flows: well-posedness and asymptotic behaviour
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study anisotropic Minkowski-type curvature flows associated with a perimeter defined through oscillations on Wulff neighbourhoods. The anisotropy may be non-smooth, and in particular crystalline, while the mobility may differ from the anisotropy, provided a natural compatibility condition is satisfied. We compute the first variation of the perimeter and introduce a weak formulation in terms of distance functions and measure-valued nonlocal Cahn-Hoffman fields. By means of a nonlocal minimising movement scheme and suitable estimates for the evolution of Wulff shapes, we prove existence of weak superflows and subflows starting from arbitrary closed sets. Under the additional assumption that the initial level sets have compact boundary, a comparison principle yields existence and uniqueness of the level set flow. Finally, we prove that variational weak flows converge, up to fattening, as $r\searrow 0$ to the weak flow of the local anisotropic, possibly crystalline, curvature motion. The main step in the proof consists in averaging the nonlocal Cahn-Hoffman measures to obtain vector fields converging to a local Cahn-Hoffman field.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Modulational stability of finite-depth Stokes waves with constant vorticity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the effect of constant vorticity on the modulational spectral stability of small-amplitude periodic gravity waves for the two-dimensional finite-depth water-wave system. We derive an explicit stability criterion that agrees with the prediction obtained by Thomas, Kharif and Manna [43] through a nonlinear Schrödinger approximation. For waves propagating to the right, we identify a sharp range of dimensionless positive (counterclockwise) vorticity, for which modulational instability is suppressed at every depth, while at any fixed depth sufficiently strong negative (clockwise) vorticity also restores modulational stability. We give a complete description of the spectrum near the origin and identify a figure-eight spectral curve in the unstable regime. A key distinction from the irrotational case is that the usual Hamiltonian factorization of the linearized operator fails at zero Floquet exponent on the full periodic Sobolev space. We therefore carry out a spectral reduction based on reversibility, without relying on Hamiltonian factorization.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Landau equation: Well-posedness and singularities of homoenergetic solutions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the inhomogeneous Landau equation and focus on solutions whose density and temperature evolve in time but remain spatially homogeneous. Such solutions are called homoenergetic. We identify one class of initial data for which homoenergetic solutions exist globally in time, and another class for which they develop finite-time hydrodynamic singularities. The initial data are spatially inhomogeneous, neither close to vacuum nor close to equilibrium; both the well-posedness and the finite-time blow-up results hold for all soft and hard potentials.

Analysis of PDEs.title: 2D Navier-Stokes with viscosity-dependent Navier slip: strong convergence for unbounded initial velocity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with Navier friction on a smooth, bounded, simply connected domain, we establish strong vorticity convergence along a subsequence in the vanishing viscosity limit for initial vorticity in $L^p$ with $p>1$. The friction coefficients may grow as viscosity vanishes under an explicit growth restriction depending on $p$, which includes regimes of vanishing slip length. The main challenge, even for viscosity-independent friction, is to control the vorticity generated at the boundary. We split the vorticity into contributions from the initial data and the boundary. By combining renormalization and estimates for the normal velocity near the boundary, we show that the boundary contribution vanishes in the inviscid limit. As a consequence, the limiting Euler solutions conserve kinetic energy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Positive solutions to the nonlinear Choquard equation: symmetry, uniqueness, and nondegeneracy
