At each finite cutoff, a prescribed terminal coordinate selects an initial perturbation whose physical $L^2$ norm tends to zero as the cutoff is removed. Uniform energy, moment, and transfer estimates yield the common strong initial trace while preserving a nonzero observable at a fixed positive time.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Reconstruction and well-posedness of an inverse coefficient problem for a diffusion equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we investigate the inverse coefficient problem of determining an unknown coefficient in a diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement. More precisely, assuming that the domain is cylindrical, we develop a unified theoretical and numerical framework for the stable reconstruction of a space-time-dependent coefficient, by reformulating the inverse problem as a nonlinear equation. The inherent nonlinearity of the problem is transferred to an auxiliary nonlinear equation, enabling the application of techniques and concepts from nonlinear analysis. By combining representation formulas with regularity properties of solutions to diffusion equations, we extend to nonlinear inverse problems an approach that has so far been restricted to linear ones. The theoretical reconstruction procedure is complemented by a numerical analysis of the proposed method, including convergence and error estimates, as well as numerical experiments. The proposed reconstruction algorithm is directly inspired by the theoretical framework.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Semiclassical resonances under local magnetic fields
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study resonances for the semiclassical magnetic Laplacian in the full plane with a compactly supported magnetic field in the framework of semiclassical complex scaling and black box scattering theory. Assuming that the magnetic field is locally constant, we prove the existence of semiclassical resonances near the Landau levels with exponentially small imaginary parts. We also prove that resonances emerge from a magnetic step discontinuity along a curved interface or a non-degenerate magnetic well, and in the vicinity of anharmonic Landau levels if the field has an isolated zero.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 26 pages, two figures. Amended: the main theorems and body of the paper remain unchanged; the revision added estimates, in the appendix, on the Tang-Zworski Theorem for energies near the threshold

Analysis of PDEs.title: Constrained minimization problem and unbounded dynamics for the four-dimensional Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger System
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the Klein-Gordon-Schrodinger system in four spatial dimensions. We consider a constrained minimization problem associated with the corresponding stationary system and establish the existence of a positive radial minimizer. We further investigate the asymptotic behavior and qualitative properties of minimizers. As an application, we analyze the dynamics of solutions with initial data in a potential well and prove that such solutions either blow up in finite time or exhibit unbounded growth in the energy norm as time tends to infinity. Since the minimizers lie on the boundary of the potential well, we also establish the strong instability of the associated standing waves.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Maximum Principle and Optimal Gradient Estimates of Solutions to the Insulated Conductivity Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the insulated conductivity problem with two unit spherical inclusions embedded in a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge3$. The gradient of solutions may blow up as the distance between the two inclusions goes to zero. We introduce bispherical coordinates and expand the solution in spherical harmonics. Then we use the maximum principle to give a new proof of the optimal gradient estimate obtained by Dong-Li-Yang.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Failure of superharmonicity near an isolated singularity of the critical biharmonic equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $n\ge5$ and $u$ be a positive singular solution of $Δ^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball. A long-standing question is where or not $ -Δu>0$ in the punctured ball. In this paper we show that the answer is negative. More precisely we construct a positive singular solution whose singularity at the origin is nonremovable, while its lower limit there is zero. On a normal subspace, $-Δu$ converges to a strictly negative constant. The spherical minimum has order $r^β$, where $2<β<4$, and the spherical Harnack ratio is unbounded. The proof uses balanced planar polygons, finitely many exterior parameters and a countable gluing construction.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Existence, Smoothness, and Order-Two Entire Extension of the Navier-Stokes Equations in Critical Fourier-Besov Spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish global existence, smoothness, and physical energy bounds for solutions to the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \ge 3$) under a scaling-critical smallness condition in the homogeneous Fourier-Besov spaces $\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, defined as the weak space $F \dot{B}^{\frac{d}{p'}-1}_{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$ and $F \dot{B}^{-1}_{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ at the endpoint $p = 1$. By combining the nonassociative algebra of Riesz convolutions and spaces of functions dominated by Fourier-Caloric flows $\mathscr{V}(λ)$ with a Littlewood-Paley dyadic atomic decomposition, we prove that the Catalan Picard series converges globally whenever $\|\widehat{u^0}\|_{\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)} < Cν$. This threshold reaches the sharp boundary of well-posedness prior to norm inflation, strictly improves upon the classical Fujita-Kato $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ condition, and admits explicit multiscale Schwartz initial data with arbitrarily large $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $H^k(\mathbb{R}^d)$ norms. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for positive times, the velocity and pressure fields admit an analytic extension to the complex domain $\mathbb{C}^d$, forming a smooth curve of entire vector fields of order two. Finally, for arbitrary initial data outside the critical ball, we employ fractional Riesz convolutions $*_α$ ($0 < α< 1$) to derive an explicit lower bound $T_{\max}(u^0) > 0$ on the lifespan of smooth, order-two entire solutions, establishing a sharp dichotomy between global continuation via viscous re-entry into the critical ball and a scaling-invariant lower blow-up rate.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_α^{γ+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(ω^r)$ to $L^q(ω^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=α\in(0,1)$, and $ω\in A_{r,q}^+(γ)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_α^{γ+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for $[b,I_α^{γ+}]_k$, and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with $\inf_T\{\|[\cdot,I_α^{γ+}]_k-T\|_{L^r\to L^q}^\frac{1}{k}\}$ of $\mathrm{dist}_{\mathrm{PBMO}}(\cdot,\mathrm{PCMO})$, where the infimum is taken over all compact operators $T:L^r\to L^q$. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Compact toric Einstein four-manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This is a continuation of our previous paper on toric gravitational instantons. We develop a systematic theory of compact simply-connected Einstein four-manifolds with toric symmetry. Applications include
  (1) The construction of simply-connected positive Einstein four-manifolds with arbitrarily large $b_2$. Our method is based on local gluing combined with a global virtual counting argument. The key idea involves a particular design of rod structures to enable a gluing construction and restrict possible degenerations.
  (2) A topological characterization of algebraically special toric Einstein metrics in terms of $b^+_2 \leq1$. This uses special curvature identities for $W^+$ in the toric setting.
  (3) Uniqueness, up to scaling and isometry, of toric Einstein metrics on four-manifolds admitting an algebraically special Einstein metric.
  (4) Diffeomorphism classification of compact toric Einstein four-manifolds in terms of an improved Hitchin-Thorpe inequality $χ\geq3|τ|$.
  (5) Smooth compactness of simply connected toric Einstein four-manifolds with bounded Euler number.
  In particular, our construction recovers all the classical toric Einstein metrics, including the Page and Chen-LeBrun-Weber metrics, starting from the round sphere through moduli spaces of conical Einstein metrics.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 152 pages. Exposition improved and some arguments clarified. Moved Appendix C to the main text. Added a new Appendix C on a general compactness theorem for toric Einstein metrics. Removed the Appendix D on the discussion on the variational framework since it is not relevant to the main results

Analysis of PDEs.title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Critical Value for the Viscosity Coefficient: Triggering Oscillatory Traveling Waves in the Pseudo-parabolic Fisher-KPP Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The pseudo-parabolic term $u_{xxt}$ serves as a canonical example of higher-order viscosity that provides effective regularization while capturing the refined physical mechanism. How it alters the dynamics of prototype equations remains a fundamental issue, which is not yet fully understood. The goal of this paper is to show that this term induces a sharp transition in traveling wave structure, via studying the pseudo-parabolic Fisher-KPP equation $$ u_t - τu_{xxt} = D u_{xx} + u(1-u). $$ We completely characterize how the parameter ratio $τ/D$ acts as a critical switch: it preserves the monotonic structure of classical traveling waves when $τ/D \leq 1$, yet it triggers a qualitative shift to oscillatory traveling waves when $τ/D > 1$. Numerical simulations support these findings. The threshold $τ/D=1$ thus captures the dual role of the pseudo-parabolic term: it acts as a structure-preserving viscosity when small, but when large it reflects dominant capillary hysteresis, generating the oscillations that explain the saturation overshoot, a phenomenon that contradicts classical diffusion models yet is widely observed in two-phase flow.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The authors request withdrawal due to critical errors in Sections 6 and 7. Specifically, the proof regarding non-monotonic traveling waves is flawed and the corresponding numerical simulations are incorrect, which invalidates the main conclusions

Analysis of PDEs.title: Effect of a fourth-order diffusion term on the robustness of the transfer function stability for hyperbolic systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system with anti-located control and observation. It is well known that the system can be stabilized with a delayed output-feedback control and that, unfortunately, this design is arbitrarily sensitive to small errors in the transport velocity. It was recently proved that adding a second-order diffusion term to the system restores robustness. We show that the same phenomenon occurs with a fourth-order diffusion term: the maximal spectral abscissa of the closed-loop system converges, as the diffusion parameter goes to zero, to the explicit value $-\ln(2)$, and the resulting stability margin is robust to small perturbations of the transport velocity. This additional term leads to a quartic characteristic equation whose roots have no tractable closed-form expression. We develop an asymptotic classification of its four roots and use it to obtain a first-order expansion of the transfer function with an explicit error bound. Combining this expansion with a topological degree argument, we show that $-\ln(2)$ is in fact the exact limiting value of the spectral abscissa, extending to the fourth-order case the sharpness result previously available only for second-order diffusive terms.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Whole-space eventual log-concavity and level-set geometry for the multidimensional Fisher-KPP equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish eventual strict log-concavity and quantitative level-set curvature bounds for the Fisher-KPP equation $u_t=Δu+u-u^2$ in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\geq2$, with nontrivial, nonnegative, smooth compactly supported initial data. Specifically, there exist $T>1$ and $c>0$ such that $D_x^2\log u(t,x)\leq-(c/t)e^{-2(\sqrt2-1)t}\mathrm{Id}$ for all $t\geq T$ and $x\in\mathbb R^N$. Consequently, after a single waiting time, the solution has exactly one critical point, which is a nondegenerate global maximizer, and every positive level set below the maximum is smooth, closed, and strictly convex with positive principal curvatures. Moreover, for levels in any fixed closed interval $K\subset(0,1)$, the principal curvatures are uniformly bounded below by $(1-C\log t/t)/(2t)$ for all sufficiently large $t$. The proof combines one-sided second angular derivative estimates for the fixed-front region, absorptive comparison in the invaded interior, leading-edge barriers and blow-up arguments through the diffusive scale, and uniform Gaussian amplitude estimates in the exterior.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 44 pages, 1 figure. Revised and shortened version

Analysis of PDEs.title: Variational exponential estimates and stationary large deviations for SPDEs
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We establish an abstract criterion for large deviations of invariant measures when the deterministic dynamics has a single globally attracting equilibrium. Deterministic regularisation and attraction yield an endpoint estimate for long controlled paths of bounded action, uniformly over each fixed bounded initial set. This allows the finite time Freidlin-Wentzell uniform LDP on bounded initial sets to be combined directly with stationary exponential norm estimates. The proof requires neither a separate exponential tightness argument nor a Dembo-Zeitouni uniform LDP, and imposes no decay condition on differences between controlled trajectories. Finite path approximation identifies the quasipotential as the good rate function. We also establish a variational criterion based on the Boué-Dupuis representation that derives exponential estimates from bounds for controlled outputs, without requiring their convergence. Uniform controlled terminal moments yield estimates uniform in time, which pass to Krylov-Bogoliubov invariant measures.
  Together, these results establish stationary LDPs in four regimes: two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with possibly unbounded, globally Lipschitz, uniformly positive scalar amplitudes and vanishing noise correlation; reaction-diffusion systems without the additional restriction linking noise growth to reaction strength; Allen-Cahn equations with opposite boundary values and globally Lipschitz, uniformly nondegenerate multiplicative space-time white noise on intervals of arbitrary length; and Burgers equations with fixed covariance $(-Δ)^α$, $0\leqα<1/2$. For Burgers, we also obtain Gaussian norm estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Observability and stabilizability for Grushin-Type parabolic equations in the whole space
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study observability and stabilization for the whole-space Grushin heat equation $$ \partial_t u-Δ_γu=0,\qquad Δ_γ:=Δ_x+|x|^{2γ}Δ_y,\qquad (t,x,y)\in(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m,\quad γ>0. $$ For product sets $E=E_1\times E_2$, we identify three observability regimes in which thickness, distance from the degeneracy set $\{x=0\}$, and local density near that set play different roles.
  (i) In the subcritical regime $0<γ<1$, the observability inequality holds for every $T>0$ if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick; hence $T_{\min}(E)=0$.
  (ii) At the critical exponent $γ=1$, if $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is thick, we determine the exact minimal observable time: $$ T_{\min}(E)=\frac{a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)^2}{2n},\qquad a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1):=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{x\in E_1}|x|. $$ Thus, the threshold depends on the essential distance of $E_1$ from the degeneracy set.
  (iii) In the supercritical regime $γ>1$, we consider $n=1$, $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and thick sets $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)>0$, observability fails for every $T>0$, so that $T_{\min}(E)=+\infty$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)=0$, observability depends on the density of $E_1$ near $0$, measured by $$ D_{E_1}(r):=\log\!\left(\frac{2r}{|E_1\cap(-r,r)|}\right),\qquad L_{E_1}:=\limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^2D_{E_1}(r). $$ If $L_{E_1}=0$, then $T_{\min}(E)=0$; if $0<L_{E_1}<\infty$, a finite sufficient observation time exists. Moreover, observability at time $T$ requires $$ \limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^{2(1+γ)/(γ-1)}D_{E_1}(r)\le C_{T,γ}. $$
  In contrast, for every $γ>0$, exponential and complete stabilizability hold if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick. The stabilization criterion is therefore independent of $γ$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Analysis of a Two Membrane Thermoelastic Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We formulate and study a mathematical model of a thermoforming process involving two interdependent thermoelastic membranes coupled with equations governing heat transfer. These membranes interact with each other through means of elastic forces and thermal transfer which determines changes in elastic properties and further deform the membranes. The two thermoelastic membranes lead to a pair of implicit obstacle problems which are modeled both as a 2-membrane problem or a pair of quasi-variational inequalities. Mathematically, the primary model couples an elliptic two membrane problem with associated nonlinear elliptic equations describing temperature distribution. We show, under physically relevant conditions, the existence of solutions via a fixed point approach that involves reformulation of the problem to improve regularity of solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence of a Normalized Mountain Pass Solution for a Coupled Cubic Schrödinger System with Partial Confinement
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper studies a mass supercritical Schrödinger system with partial confinement: $$ \begin{cases} -Δu_1+|y|^2u_1 =λ_1u_1+μ_1u_1^3+2βu_1u_2^2,\qquad x\in\R^3,\\ -Δu_2+|y|^2u_2 =λ_2u_2+μ_2u_2^3+2βu_1^2u_2,\qquad x\in\R^3, \end{cases} $$ subject to the mass constraints $ \int_{\R^3}u_1^2\dd x=a_1$, $\int_{\R^3}u_2^2\dd x=a_2,$ where $x=(y,z)\in\R^2\times\R$, the parameters $μ_1,μ_2,β$ are positive, and $λ_1,λ_2\in\R$ are unknown Lagrange multipliers. The masses satisfy $(a_1,a_2)=\eps(ρ_1,ρ_2)$ for a fixed vector $ρ=(ρ_1,ρ_2)\in (0,\infty)^2$. For all sufficiently small $\eps>0$, we establish the existence of a positive normalized solution $u_\eps^-$ at a mountain pass level on the full product mass sphere. This level coincides with the infimum of the energy over the negative part of the Pohozaev set. The main difficulty arises from the lack of compactness due to partial confinement. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness argument that preserves the two independent mass constraints and show that every minimizing sequence for this infimum admits a strongly convergent subsequence after suitable common translations along the unconfined axial direction. We further establish the asymptotic relation $\eps E(u_\eps^-)\to m_0(ρ)$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, where $m_0(ρ)>0$ denotes the infimum of the free energy under the corresponding Pohozaev constraint. In addition, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the kinetic and potential energies. The solution obtained here is distinct from the normalized ground states constructed by Jia et al. [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst., 40(2020), 2739-2766] through local minimization for sufficiently small masses.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Continuity and Stability of the FitzHugh Nagumo System with Respect to the Diffusion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Spatial heterogeneity in diffusion is a fundamental feature of excitable media, yet its effect on FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics remains mathematically challenging. We establish stability of solutions with respect to perturbations of the diffusion coefficient, providing a rigorous account of how changes in the medium affect the evolution of the system. Specifically, we prove a continuous dependence result ensuring that small perturbations in diffusion produce small variations in the corresponding solutions. The proof adapts the method of contracting rectangles to variable diffusion, yielding a framework for controlling and comparing solutions associated with different diffusion profiles. This result provides a rigorous link between heterogeneous and homogeneous FitzHugh Nagumo systems and justifies constant-diffusion approximations when the diffusion coefficient is close to a constant. Our analysis advances the understanding of FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics in heterogeneous media by establishing robustness with respect to spatial variations in diffusion.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-migration for planar elastic flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a closed planar curve evolving by the free or the length-preserving elastic flow. We prove that the scale-invariant bound $L\int k^2\,ds\le 4π^2+8/3$ at the initial time prevents the entire curve from crossing any line between two times. For the free flow, the proof combines a monotonicity estimate for the normalized bending energy with a barrier that compares centroid motion to an expanding energy radius. For the length-preserving flow, a quantitative gradient estimate controls the total centroid displacement.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Multiplicity and least energy sign-changing normalized solutions for a Kirchhoff equation on bounded domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we study sign-changing normalized solutions of the Kirchhoff problem \[ \begin{cases} -\left(a+b\displaystyle\int_Ω|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)Δu =|u|^{p-2}u+μu &\text{in }Ω,\\ u=0 &\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{cases} \] subject to the constraint \[ \int_Ω|u|^2\,dx=c, \] where $a,b>0$, $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$ is a smooth bounded connected domain, $1\le N\le3$, $c>0$ is prescribed, and $μ\in\mathbb R$ is a Lagrange multiplier. We assume $2<p<\infty$ for $N=1,2$ and $2<p\le6$ for $N=3$. For every integer $k\ge1$, we obtain at least $k$ distinct pairs of sign-changing normalized solutions for sufficiently small $c>0$. We determine the small mass asymptotics of their energies, Lagrange multipliers, and rescaled profiles in terms of the distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues and their eigenspaces. When $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$, we obtain infinitely many such pairs for every prescribed mass $c>0$, with energies tending to $+\infty$. At $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$, this conclusion holds for every sufficiently small fixed mass.
  We also establish the existence of a least energy sign-changing normalized solution on general bounded domains for every prescribed mass when $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$. For sufficiently small mass, such a solution exists on general bounded domains when $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$ and on star-shaped domains when $p>2+\frac{8}{N}$. For any family of such least energy solutions, the rescaled profiles approach the $L^2$-unit sphere of the second Dirichlet eigenspace in $H_0^1(Ω)$ as $c\to0^+$. The finite multiplicity and least energy results include the Sobolev critical case $N=3$, $p=6$. The proofs combine a localized symmetric minimax construction, energy comparisons with one-signed critical points, and compactness arguments that preserve the sign-changing property.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Energy methods and optimal decay for time-fractional equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study energy methods for the time-fractional equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-(a(t,x)u_x)_x+(F(t,x,u))_x=Q(t,x,u)$ on the real line, where $0<α<1$, the coefficient $a$ is measurable and bounded from above and from below by positive constants, $σ\partial_xF\ge0$, $σQ\le0$, and the data are in $L^1\cap L^\infty$. Using Yosida approximations of the kernel, an iteration on the $L^{2^m}$ norms gives the parabolic decay $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α/2}$.
  In $L^2$ it gives the rate $t^{-α/4}$, which, already for the linear equation, improves the rate $t^{-α/5}$ obtained before by the classical energy method. For the convection--diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, the parabolic rate is optimal for $q\ge2$, and for $1<q<2$ the convection improves it. An $L^1$ time-regularity estimate of Bénilan--Crandall type gives the pointwise flux bound $|u|^{q-1}u-u_x=O(\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α})$. This bound takes the place of the Oleĭnik estimate and yields the optimal rate $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim t^{-α/q}$ for $1<q<2$. For nonnegative data, matching lower bounds hold for the $L^p$ norms.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Orbital stability and instability of standing waves for an inhomogeneous logarithmic Schrödinger equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the inhomogeneous logarithmic Schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu+Δu+|x|^{-1}u\log|u|^2=0, \qquad (t,x)\in\R\times\R^N,\quad N\ge2. \] For every initial datum in $H^1(\R^N)$, we establish global existence of weak solutions. We also construct explicit positive stationary solutions and solve the associated Nehari minimization problem. For $ω\ge0$, the minimizer is unique up to {a constant} phase and is given by \[ e^{\frac{N-1}{2}(1+\sqrt{1+ω})} e^{-(1+\sqrt{1+ω})|x|}, \] whereas for $ω<0$ the infimum is zero and is not attained. Finally, we prove that the standing waves associated with these profiles are orbitally stable for $ω>0$ by a variational argument, and orbitally unstable for $-1<ω<-1+(N-1)^{-2}$ by combining spectral analysis, localized energy and mass estimates, and phase modulation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Borel Summability for Nonlinear Differential Systems on Characteristic Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate singularly perturbed nonlinear complex differential systems of the form $\hbar \partial_x f = F (x, \hbar, f)$, where $\hbar$ is a small complex perturbation parameter. We give geometric and analytic conditions under which the formal perturbative solution associated with a fixed regular leading-order branch is locally uniformly Borel summable. This leads to an existence and uniqueness theorem of holomorphic solutions with prescribed perturbative expansion. We give an explicit triangular example and a self-contained application to the singularly perturbed Painlevé I equation.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 18 pages. Substantial revision with a new title

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global Hölder regularity
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Let $ C_ω$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $ω\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_ω$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $β^+>0>β^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $β^\pm$.
  As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/β^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-Δ_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_ω$ do not exist for $0<q<q^*$, whereas homogeneous supersolutions exist for $q>q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$.
  The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global Hölder regularity for $(-Δ_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible Hölder exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. The key is a dichotomy: deforming a spectrally localised pattern smears it across scales, whereas pushing its generating centres forward and re-convolving leaves the spectral envelope exactly invariant --- so transporting the eddy centres preserves both cascade and frame. In the field the finite-size Lyapunov exponent obeys $ζ(R)=h(R)-1$ threshold by threshold within the scaling range, with a sweeping deficit $Δ_{\rm sw}=+0.038\pm0.019$, consistent with zero, against $+0.091\pm0.019$ for the frozen field on the same data, a gap that doubles at Navier--Stokes intermittency. Companion papers prove that this family shows Richardson dispersion and a dissipative anomaly (Fefferman and Mayboroda 2026), and that a scalar advected by this flow obeys Yaglom's relation (De Lellis 2026), at small Kubo number. Trajectories forget their starting point as the smallest eddy is removed: the median separation of pairs released from one point with independent Brownian kicks varies as $κ_{p}^{0.0333\pm0.0038}$ over 22 decades of particle diffusivity, against $κ_{p}^{1/2}$ for a smooth control. A scalar in the same field closes the exact scale-by-scale variance budget, four independently measured terms balancing the dissipation to 15\% over 1.2 decades with no adjustable constant, and reaches its inertial--convective asymptote $S_{L}=-χr$ to $0.9995\pm0.0018$ once the measured diffusive transfer is restored, while under an imposed mean gradient $χ$ changes by 14\% over a factor 5.8 in $κ$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The code, the analysis scripts that produce every figure and numbers in the paper, the run configurations, the data behind the figures and the supplementary movies are available at https://github.com/R1967J/kinematic-field. A single self-contained generator of the velocity field kinematic_field.py

Analysis of PDEs.title: An Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom law for a kinematic model of turbulence
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove an Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom-type law for passive scalars advected by a family of random $C^α$ velocity field proposed in \cite{JDEMS} as a kinematic model of turbulent fluids. Up to a technical assumption on one parameter, the expectation of the squared $L^2_t H^γ_x$ norm of solutions to the passive scalar equation is bounded by the squared $L^2$ norm of the deterministic initial datum, uniformly in the viscosity, whenever $α+ 2γ< 1$. The proof is based on a new insight in the theory developed by \cite{FM} to prove Richardson's dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the same model.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp estimates for the Opdam-Cherednik $W$-invariant heat kernel for the root system $A_1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this version of the paper, we note important gaps in the previous version.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity Theory for the Equation $\det(D^2u) = f(u)$ in Two Dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the interior regularity of convex solutions to $$\det D^2u = f(u)$$ in planar domains, with no regularity or monotonicity assumptions on $f$. In particular, when $f$ is bounded between positive constants, we show that $u$ is locally $C^{1,\,1}$, and that its level sets near a critical point are asymptotically ellipses. Our analysis relies on a new monotone quantity for a second-order flow satisfied by the support functions of the level sets of $u$. As a byproduct of our methods, we obtain Liouville theorems that generalize a classical result of Jörgens, and include a complete classification of global solutions in 2D to an obstacle problem studied by Jin-Tu-Xiong. As another application, we obtain regularity and rigidity results for rotating-wave solutions of the semigeostrophic equations from meteorology.

Functional Analysis.title: Independent Backward Preimages and Algebraic Radial Decompositions of Operators
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $T\in\mathcal{B}(X)$, where $X$ is a complex Banach space. We introduce the spaces $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$, defined by independently chosen preimages under the powers of $T$ with exponential growth bounds, and study algebraic radial decompositions involving $\mathcal{H}_r(T)$, $\mathcal{K}_s(T)$, and $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$. We prove that every algebraic decomposition $X=\mathcal{H}_r(T)\oplus\mathcal{I}_s(T)$ is topological and that $\mathcal{I}_s(T)=\mathcal{K}_s(T)$. This removes the closedness assumption in the radial decomposition theorem of Koliha and Poon. We also prove that, for $0\leq a\leq b$, the closedness of $\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ and $\mathcal{H}_a(T)+\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ implies $\mathcal{I}_b(T)=\mathcal{K}_b(T)$. We establish finite-defect and circular spectral criteria and characterize the Cantor--Bendixson derivatives of the spectrum, Browder spectrum, and Drazin spectrum in terms of radial decompositions and quotient restrictions. As applications, we obtain new characterizations of generalized Drazin, generalized Drazin--Riesz, generalized Drazin--meromorphic, and $g_z$-invertible operators in terms of radial subspaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral and mapping properties of the inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate the spectral and boundedness properties of the inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator $\mathcal{A}^{Q,B}$ and its associated semigroup in $L^p$ spaces with respect to the inverse Gaussian measure. We establish strong continuity and contractivity of this semigroup in $L^p$ for $p \in [1, \infty)$, and obtain a complete characterization of the spectrum of $\mathcal{A}^{Q,B}$. For $p \in (1, \infty)$, the spectrum is independent of $p$, consists entirely of eigenvalues and exhibits a spectral gap. For $p=1$, the spectrum is instead the left half-plane. Furthermore, we discuss ultracontractivity and hypercontractivity properties of the semigroup.

Functional Analysis.title: The extension of traces for Sobolev mappings between manifolds
Functional Analysis.summary: The compact Riemannian manifolds $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{N}$ for which the trace operator from the first-order Sobolev space of mappings $\smash{\dot{W}}^{1, p} (\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N})$ to the fractional Sobolev-Slobodeckiĭ space $\smash{\smash{\dot{W}}^{1 - 1/p, p}} (\partial \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N})$ is surjective when $1 < p < \dim \mathcal{M}$ are characterised. The traces are extended using a new construction which can be carried out assuming the absence of the known topological and analytical obstructions. When $p \ge \dim \mathcal{M}$ the same construction provides a Sobolev extension with linear estimates for maps that have a continuous extension, provided that the known analytical obstructions to such a control are not present.

Functional Analysis.title: Near-Riesz and pseudo-Riesz bases of Hilbert C*-modules and semi-C*-Fredholm operators
Functional Analysis.summary: Several useful concepts of almost frames or Riesz bases of Hilbert spaces gave us the motivation to review the theory of C*-module frames and C*-module Riesz bases for Hilbert C*-modules, searching for similar useful structures. We give a survey of the background in C*-module frame theory, summarizing and particularly extending or correcting earlier results. The concepts of near-Riesz bases, pseudo-frames, pseudo-Riesz sequences, and pseudo Riesz bases of Hilbert C*-modules are introduced and equivalently related to (semi-)C*-Fredholm properties of their synthesis operators. The notion of the excess of a C*-module frame is introduced, taking values in related C* algebras. Indicators for possible erasures of frame elements are described with the aim to preserve robustness of frames. Introducing a new notion of pseudo-Riesz-Weyl sequences in the standard Hilbert C*-module $l_2(A)$ we reverse the found correspondence by assuming the associated synthesis operator of a Bessel sequence to be (upper semi-)C*-Weyl. Furthermore, we deduce from the invariance of (upper semi-)C*-Fredholm and C*-Riesz-Weyl properties of synthesis operators with respect to ''compact'' perturbations the perturbation invariance of the respective classes of module Bessel sequences.
Functional Analysis.comment: We joined two further sections from the first version and worked on the presentation of the content, adding explanations, historical remarks and references. [The first two versions are still available on the arxiv.]

Functional Analysis.title: Single commutators in Schatten ideals
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $r>2$ and let $p,q\in(0,\infty)$ satisfy $r^{-1}=p^{-1}+q^{-1}$. We prove that every $T\in \mathcal{S}_r(\mathcal H)$ is a single commutator $T=[A,B]$ with $A\in \mathcal{S}_p(\mathcal H)$ and $B\in \mathcal{S}_q(\mathcal H)$. Combined with L. G. Brown's theorem for $1 \leq r \leq 2$, this completely resolves the Pearcy--Topping problem for Schatten ideals. We also obtain simultaneous operator and Schatten norm bounds for the factors.

Functional Analysis.title: Distance-Weighted Norm Equivalences for Analytic Functions on John Domains
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb C$ be a bounded John domain and set $δ(z)=\text{dist}(z,\partialΩ)$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $α>\text{dim}_A(\partialΩ)-2$, we establish a norm equivalence between $\int_Ω|g|^pδ^α\,dA$ and $\int_Ω|g'|^pδ^{α+p}\,dA$ for analytic functions $g$ on $Ω$, with a point-evaluation term fixing the additive constant. The estimate of the derivative term is local and holds on every proper planar domain, whereas the converse follows from a distance-weighted Poincaré inequality on John domains. Taking $α=mp-2$ yields the corresponding comparison between the $m$-th and $(m+1)$-st derivatives. For $m\ge2$ the boundary-dimension condition is automatic, so the only dimension-sensitive case is the comparison between $\int_Ω|f'|^pδ^{p-2}\,dA$ and $\int_Ω|f''|^pδ^{2p-2}\,dA$ when $1<p<2$. We show that this restriction is sharp within the class of quasidisks by using self-similar Rohde snowflakes. We also construct, for every $s>1$, an inward-cusp $s$-John domain on which the comparison fails, showing that the ordinary John condition cannot in general be weakened.

Functional Analysis.title: Dual Banach spaces with AP but without BAP
Functional Analysis.summary: We give negative answers to the AP-to-BAP and BAP-to-MAP questions for dual Banach spaces. More precisely, there is a separable Banach space $V$ with the metric approximation property (MAP) such that $V^*$ has the approximation property (AP) but no bounded approximation property (BAP). There is also a separable MAP space $X$, isomorphic to $\ell_1$, whose dual has BAP but no MAP. This resolves a longstanding open question explicitly stated in \cite{Oja2010}. The constructions rely on a finitely generated group without Property A and a quantitative estimate for optimal bounded approximation constants of projective tensor products.

Functional Analysis.title: Real alternative Daugavet property without Daugavet property in a separable complex Banach space
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct a separable complex Banach space whose underlying real space has the alternative Daugavet property, although the complex space fails the Daugavet property, thereby answering an open question posed by Kadets, Martin, and Paya in 2006.
Functional Analysis.comment: Submitted for publication. Comments are welcome

Functional Analysis.title: Nonisomorphic separable Banach spaces at Lipschitz distance one
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct nonisomorphic separable real Banach spaces whose multiplicative Lipschitz distance is one. Building on OpenAI's graph-space construction, we arrange two sequences of graph spaces into countably many blocks and form two spaces that differ by a single additional block. This block distinguishes their linear structures: one space contains a complemented copy of $\ell_1(c_0(\ell_2))$, whereas the other does not. By mapping the additional block to increasingly late positions and rearranging the remaining blocks, we obtain homeomorphisms whose Lipschitz constants and those of their inverses tend to one, while both spaces and their norms remain unchanged.

Functional Analysis.title: Szegő quasiforms: a Schottky-scheme construction for vertex operator superalgebras
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study the half weight ($N=\half$) analogue of the Bers quasiform on a Schottky group $Γ$ of genus $g$: the Poincaré series $S_\eps(x,y)=\sum_{\gt\in\Gt}j(\gt,x)/(γx-y)\,(dx\,dy)^{1/2}$ over a lift $\Gt\subset\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)$ of $Γ$. The $\Ng:=2^{g}$ lifts give $\Ng$ trivial $α$-holonomy even spin structures $\Lg$.
  The remaining $2^{2g}-\Ng$ spin structures
  are not treated in this paper.
  We prove, on an open set (H) of Schottky parameters and more generally whenever the critical exponent of $Γ$ is below $\half$ (any genus $g\ge 1$) the following:
  absolute and locally uniform convergence on $Ω_0\timesΩ_0$, where $Ω_0$ is the full region of discontinuity including the point $\infty$ (treated in homogeneous coordinates);
  invariance without Eichler-type defect; skew-symmetry; a simple pole on the diagonal as the only singularity; $H^0(\Sg,\Lg)=0$; and hence identification of $S_\eps$ with the Szegő kernel of $\Lg$. At genus one the kernel is computed explicitly and the relations between lifts and theta characteristics are determined. We further prove that the diagonal coefficient defines a projective connection that differs from the Bergman projective connection by a quadratic differential
  constructed from $θ[δ](0)$, a residue-reconstruction formula for half-differentials with poles of any order, an expansion in the Schottky multipliers, and a formula for the free fermion stress tensor.

Functional Analysis.title: Quasinilpotency of commutators under a weakened Kleinecke--Shirokov condition
Functional Analysis.summary: Kramar and Kramar Fijavž proved that a commutator $Y=AB-BA$ of two complex square matrices is nilpotent whenever $Y$ commutes with an iterated commutator $δ_Y^{k}(A)$, where $δ_Y(T)=YT-TY$, and asked whether this result can be generalized to bounded operators on infinite-dimensional spaces. We show that for $k\geq 2$ such a commutator need not be quasinilpotent. On the other hand, for every $k$ it is quasinilpotent whenever it is compact, or more generally whenever it is a Riesz operator or $AY-YA$ is compact. Moreover, its Riesz projection at any non-zero isolated point of its spectrum always has infinite rank.

Functional Analysis.title: Endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators on quantum Euclidean spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study commutators $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$ involving fractional Laplacians on quantum Euclidean spaces associated with arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices $θ$. For $d\geq2$ and $-\frac d2<ε\neq 0<1$, we characterize critical weak Schatten class membership of $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$ for any $x$ as a tempered distribution by Sobolev spaces, with equivalent corresponding norms. We also establish precise asymptotics of singular values for $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$. For this purpose, we extend the Cwikel estimates and the required asymptotics of singular values to arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices, and we also establish a systematic approximation theory of tempered distributions on quantum Euclidean spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: The Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators in divergence form
Functional Analysis.summary:
We establish the Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators $L = -\operatorname{div}^α(μ
abla^α\cdot)$ of order $2α\in (0,2)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Riesz fractional gradient and divergence, with bounded, measurable and uniformly elliptic complex coefficients $μ$. More precisely, we show that the domain of $L^{1/2}$ coincides with the distributional fractional Sobolev space $\mathrm{S}^{α,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and that $\|L^{1/2} u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2} \simeq \|
abla^αu\|_{\mathrm{L}^2}$, with constants that are locally uniform in $α$. As a consequence, we recover the Kato square root property for elliptic operators $-\operatorname{div}(μ
abla\cdot)$ in the limit $α	o 1$, and we obtain continuity of the square root with respect to the parameter $α$. The proof follows the second-order approach to the Kato problem. Its two new ingredients are nonlocal off-diagonal estimates of polynomial order for the resolvents of $L$, and a construction of $T(b)$-test functions that circumvents the nonlocality of $
abla^α$ by factorizing it through Riesz potentials.

Functional Analysis.title: Quasi-norms on $\mathbb{R}^d$: Characterization and Approximation by Conic Splines
Functional Analysis.summary: We first show that a regularizer on $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is continuous, symmetric, and amplitude-equivariant is of the form $g=q^γ$ with $γ>0$, where $q$ is continuous and absolutely homogeneous; we call the set of such $q$ the CH class, whose convex members are the seminorms. Within the CH class, we single out two configurations of interest for regularization: the quasi-norms, which are exactly the positive-definite members of the family, and the quasi-seminorms with null space control, which are the composition of a quasi-norm with a linear map that sets the null space. We then propose a universal parametrization of the class by conic splines, the continuous functions that are linear on each cone of a polyhedral fan. Specifically, we show that the polyhedral CH functionals are exactly the symmetric non-negative conic splines, and that these admit a stable nodal representation in a basis of conic B-splines. Finally, we determine the rates of approximation: the conic spline interpolant converges at the second-order rate $h^2\asymp n^{-2/(d-1)}$, in the $L_\infty$-norm on the hyper-sphere when the angular profile is twice differentiable, and in the $L_1$-norm when its spherical Hessian variation is bounded, which covers the polyhedral members of the class. The rate is sharp, already for the Euclidean norm. The planar case is worked out in full, with the trigonometric hat functions as basis and an $\ell_1$-norm of second differences as regularity index.

Functional Analysis.title: Dirac solitons in one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equations
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper we study a family of one-dimensional stationary cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equations with periodic potentials and linear part displaying Dirac points in the dispersion relation. By introducing a suitable periodic perturbation, one can open a spectral gap around the Dirac-point energy. This allows to construct standing waves of the NLS equation whose leading-order profile is a modulation of Bloch waves by means of the components of a spinor solving an appropriate cubic nonlinear Dirac (NLD) equation. We refer to these solutions as Dirac solitons. Our analysis thus provides a rigorous justification for the use of the NLD equation as an effective model for the original NLS equation.
Functional Analysis.comment: 41 pages, 4 Figures. Various typos corrected and short comments added, as well as additional figures. Introduction and the beginning of Section 5 have benn slightly expanded. Keywords: Dirac solitons, Dirac points, NLS equations, NLD equations, standing waves, periodic Schrödinger operators

Functional Analysis.title: Linear maps of $C^*$-algebras preserving norm parallelism
Functional Analysis.summary: Two elements $a,b$ in a normed space are parallel if $\|a+γb\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$ for some $|γ|=1$; they form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if $\|a+b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$. For finite-dimensional complex $C^*$-algebras other than $\mathbf M_2(\mathbb C)$ and $\mathbb C\oplus_\infty\mathbb C$, bijective linear maps on these algebras preserving parallel or TEA pairs are scalar multiples of isometries. For unital abelian algebras with spectra containing at least three points, preservation in both directions gives the same conclusion. We obtain corresponding results for type I factors, simple type I $C^*$-algebras, and unitarily invariant operator spaces under additional continuity and finite-rank hypotheses. All results for $C(X)$ and $B(H,K)$ hold over both real and complex fields.

Functional Analysis.title: Descriptor representations of geometric port-Hamiltonian systems on Hilbert spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish conversions in both directions between geometric and descriptor representations of linear port-Hamiltonian systems on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For the geometric-to-descriptor conversion, we represent the possibly multivalued inverse Dirac relation by a skew-adjoint operator on enlarged Hilbert spaces, retaining the original operator-domain restrictions. The construction accommodates internal and external ports. We show that the conversions preserve trajectories and the power balance. An incompressible Kelvin--Voigt solid illustrates the results.

Functional Analysis.title: On the Existence, Smoothness, and Order-Two Entire Extension of the Navier-Stokes Equations in Critical Fourier-Besov Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish global existence, smoothness, and physical energy bounds for solutions to the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \ge 3$) under a scaling-critical smallness condition in the homogeneous Fourier-Besov spaces $\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, defined as the weak space $F \dot{B}^{\frac{d}{p'}-1}_{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$ and $F \dot{B}^{-1}_{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ at the endpoint $p = 1$. By combining the nonassociative algebra of Riesz convolutions and spaces of functions dominated by Fourier-Caloric flows $\mathscr{V}(λ)$ with a Littlewood-Paley dyadic atomic decomposition, we prove that the Catalan Picard series converges globally whenever $\|\widehat{u^0}\|_{\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)} < Cν$. This threshold reaches the sharp boundary of well-posedness prior to norm inflation, strictly improves upon the classical Fujita-Kato $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ condition, and admits explicit multiscale Schwartz initial data with arbitrarily large $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $H^k(\mathbb{R}^d)$ norms. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for positive times, the velocity and pressure fields admit an analytic extension to the complex domain $\mathbb{C}^d$, forming a smooth curve of entire vector fields of order two. Finally, for arbitrary initial data outside the critical ball, we employ fractional Riesz convolutions $*_α$ ($0 < α< 1$) to derive an explicit lower bound $T_{\max}(u^0) > 0$ on the lifespan of smooth, order-two entire solutions, establishing a sharp dichotomy between global continuation via viscous re-entry into the critical ball and a scaling-invariant lower blow-up rate.

Functional Analysis.title: Perturbations of Truncated Toeplitz operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate the structure of kernels of finite-rank perturbations of truncated Toeplitz operators. By realizing a perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator on a model space as a suitable matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operator on an enlarged model space, we identify its kernel with a coordinate projection of the kernel of an associated block Toeplitz operator. This realization enables us to transfer the nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of Toeplitz kernels to the perturbed truncated setting. More precisely, for a perturbation of rank at most $n$, we show that the kernel of the perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator is nearly $S^*$-invariant with defect at most $2n+1$. We then extend the method to truncated Toeplitz operators on multiband spaces. In this setting, a perturbation of rank at most $n$ again preserves the finite-defect nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of the kernel, with the explicit upper bound $2n+2$ for the defect.
Functional Analysis.comment: 31 pages, updated version. Comments are welcome:)

Functional Analysis.title: Phase Retrievability of Super Operators and Measurements
Functional Analysis.summary:
We continue the study of Phase Retrieval in the Quantum Information setting in the style of \cite{liu2023phase}, in a manner which is more general in two primary ways: (a) Instead of only pure states we consider also states (and positive semidefinite operators) of bounded rank, as is done in Quantum Tomography; (b) We consider general super operators instead of only quantum channels.
  We show that in order to have phase retrieval with respect to positive semidefinite operators of bounded rank, it suffices to discriminate between perfectly distinguishable pairs (i.e. those with orthogonal supports). From this we prove that phase retrievability is always Lipschitz stable with respect to the trace norm, and then we use the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities to deduce stability with respect to the Bures--Wasserstein distance (thus generalizing the known stability results for phase retrieval in Frame Theory). For Hermitian-preserving super operators taking values in block-diagonal matrices, we characterize phase retrievability in terms of conditions inspired by the classical complement property from Frame Theory.

Functional Analysis.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
Functional Analysis.summary: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_α^{γ+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(ω^r)$ to $L^q(ω^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=α\in(0,1)$, and $ω\in A_{r,q}^+(γ)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_α^{γ+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for $[b,I_α^{γ+}]_k$, and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with $\inf_T\{\|[\cdot,I_α^{γ+}]_k-T\|_{L^r\to L^q}^\frac{1}{k}\}$ of $\mathrm{dist}_{\mathrm{PBMO}}(\cdot,\mathrm{PCMO})$, where the infimum is taken over all compact operators $T:L^r\to L^q$. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.

Functional Analysis.title: Empirical approximation of $L^p$ norms for $p\in (1, 2)$
Functional Analysis.summary: For $p\in[1,2]$, we prove uniform moment estimates for weighted sums \[ \sum_{j=1}^mζ_jw_j|\langle{\bf v}_j,y\rangle|^p \] of independent subgaussian random variables $ζ_j$, where the unit vectors $\{{\bf v}_j\}_{j=1}^m$ and nonnegative weights $\{w_j\}_{j=1}^m$ form an isotropic frame. This allows us to obtain optimal sampling discretization of $L_p$ norms for each fixed $p\in[1,2]$. Namely, for an $N$-dimensional space $X_N$ of bounded functions satisfying $\|f\|_\infty\le\sqrt {KN}\,\|f\|_{L_2}$ for every $f\in X_N$, we show that $m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}KN\log(2N)$ independent samples $ξ^1,\ldots,ξ^m$ provide the discretization \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(ξ^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \quad\forall f\in X_N \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This implies a corresponding weighted discretization result that, for $1<p<2$, improves Talagrand's bound on the dimension $m$ needed to embed $N$-dimensional subspaces of $L_p$ into $\ell_p^m$ with distortion at most $1+\varepsilon$, giving $m\le C\varepsilon^{-2}N\log(2N)$.

Functional Analysis.title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for some locally compact quantum groups
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we show that the usual Hausdorff--Young inequalities for locally compact quantum groups such as the quantum \(E_q(2)\), the real quantum \(az+b\), and the extended quantum \(SU_q(1,1)\), where \(0<q<1\), are sharp. Moreover, there are no group-like projections with finite Haar weight in these locally compact quantum groups. We obtain a sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality for Kahng's skew-matrix quantum groups; the optimal constant is strictly less than one for \(1<p<2\); at \(p=2\), Plancherel gives equality, and these quantum groups have no nonzero group-like projections with finite Haar weight.

Functional Analysis.title: Noncommutative weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity over locally compact quantum groups
Functional Analysis.summary: We study weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity for Hopf-von Neumann algebras and locally compact quantum groups. For a Hopf-von Neumann algebra $(M,Γ)$, we introduce the space ${\rm WAP}_{{\rm Bessel},π_u}(M_*)$ through norm convergence conditions on rows and columns of slices associated with Bessel families in the universal representation. We prove that this space is the largest $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm WAP}(M_*)$ when separately continuous lift of the co-multiplication is multiplicative, and that the two spaces coincide when $M$ is commutative. Furthermore, the algebra $\{x\in C_b(\mathbb{G}): Γ(x)\in M(C_0(\mathbb{G})\otimes C_b(\mathbb{G}))\}$ is characterized as the greatest left introverted $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ satisfying a left Bessel condition on $L^2(\mathbb{G})$. We also show that ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ is a $C^*$-algebra whenever the center of $C_0(\mathbb{G})$ contains an element on which the bounded counit is non-zero.

Functional Analysis.title: Dynamics in large scale geometry
Functional Analysis.summary:
We investigate the large scale geometry of certain metric spaces through the lens of dynamics. Our approach establishes a close connection between large scale dynamical phenomena and operator algebras by characterizing various large scale dynamic behaviors in terms of GNS representations of the uniform Roe algebras arising from natural canonical states.
  Our dynamical systems are given by the Stone-Čech boundary of metric spaces together with their inverse semigroup of partial translations. This defines a space of orbits and we characterize Hausdorffness and $T_1$-ness of this space by the failure of coarse embeddability of certain metric spaces. Surprisingly, while the orbit space has very weak separation properties, we show that it satisfies a certain ''localized version'' of Urysohn's lemma.
  We show that the topology of the space of orbits and quasi-orbits are given by the space of irreducible representations of uniform Roe algebras and by the space of their primitive ideals, respectively. As a highlight of the theory developed herein, we provide classes of spaces such that the prime ideals of their uniform Roe algebras are primitive. This is the case for instance of spaces whose orbit space is $T_1$.

Functional Analysis.title: A Hardy space approximation supporting zero-free half-planes for the $ζ$-function
Functional Analysis.summary: An equivalent version of the Báez-Duarte criterion \cite{baez} for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) by Bagchi states that the RH holds true if and only if the function $E(s) = 1/s$ belongs to the closed linear span of $G_k(s) = (k^{-s} - k^{-1})ζ(s)/s,\, k \geq 2$ in the Hardy space \( H^2(\mathbb{C}_{1/2}) \), where $\mathbb{C}_α$ denotes the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>α$. We first show that if $E$ belongs to the closure of span$(G_k)_{k\geq 2}$ in \( H^2(\mathbb{C}_α) \) for $α>1/2$, then $ζ$ is zero-free in $\mathbb{C}_α$. We then use this as the basis for a numerical analysis of the sequence \[ s_n = \left\| \sum_{k=2}^{n} μ(k) G_k - E \right\|^2_α, \] for $1/2\leq α\leq 1$, where $\left\|.\right\|_α$ is the norm in $H^2(\mathbb{C}_α)$ and $μ$ the Möbius function.
Functional Analysis.comment: This article is withdrawn by the authors. It is superseded by arXiv:2611.03924, a separate submission with a revised author list reflecting the current composition of the research team. Readers should refer to arXiv:2611.03924

Analysis of PDEs.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we prove that every complete noncompact two-sided properly embedded constant mean curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal. The result holds in every dimension. We assume no bounds on curvature or volume growth. This establishes the properly embedded case of the finite-index version of do Carmo's question.
  For nonzero mean curvature, we use the radii of inscribed balls to define a positive weight. This weight gives a polynomial bound on weighted volume, while its reciprocal satisfies a differential inequality involving the Jacobi operator. We combine these properties with stability outside a compact set to obtain finite total area. This leads to a contradiction.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the elliptic regularization of maximal slope curves
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the so-called Weighted Energy-Dissipation approximation of gradient flows in metric spaces. We prove the convergence of minimizers to maximal slope curves under assumptions that are close to those of the original existence theory for metric gradient flows. The proof relies on an energy-dissipation identity for the approximating curves and on an adaptation of a general stability result for maximal slope curves.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. Moreover, the perturbed foliation admits a common smooth calibration, hence the lifted leaves are area-minimizing. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The isoperimetric problem in the Riemannian Heisenberg $3$-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every closed weakly stable constant mean curvature surface immersed in the Riemannian Heisenberg space ${\rm Nil}_3$ is an embedded rotational sphere. As a consequence, we solve the isoperimetric problem in ${\rm Nil}_3$: the isoperimetric domains of ${\rm Nil}_3$ are exactly the regions enclosed by rotational constant mean curvature spheres, and for each prescribed volume there is a unique such domain, up to ambient isometry. For small volumes, the isoperimetric result was proved by Tomter in 1993.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gradient higher integrability for a general class of degenerate parabolic double phase systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish quantitative local higher integrability estimates for weak solutions of degenerate parabolic systems with generalized double phase growth, whose prototype is $$u_t-\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{G'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du+a(x,t)\frac{H'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du\right)=0\qquad\text{in }Ω_T.$$ Here $G$ and $H$ are Young functions satisfying suitable structural assumptions. The nonnegative coefficient $a$ is allowed to vanish and has a concave modulus of continuity $ω$ with respect to the parabolic distance. For $Ψ(z,\varkappa)=G(\varkappa)+a(z)H(\varkappa)$, we prove that solutions in $L^\infty(0,T;L^s(Ω,\mathbb{R}^N))$, $2\le s<\infty$, satisfy $Ψ(\cdot,|Du|)\in L^{1+\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, provided $$\limsup_{ρ\to 0+}ω(ρ)\frac{H(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}{G(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}<\infty.$$ For bounded solutions, the corresponding condition involves $H(ρ^{-1})/G(ρ^{-1})$. These conditions extend the known interpolative gap bounds from power growth to general growth functions and continuity moduli. In particular, for $G(\varkappa)=\varkappa^p$, $H(\varkappa)=\varkappa^q$, and $ω(ρ)\simeqρ^α$, they recover $q\le p+sα/(n+s)$ and $q\le p+α$, respectively. The proof combines an intrinsic stopping-time argument with inverse-function estimates to derive Poincaré and reverse Hölder inequalities adapted to the general growth phases.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Shock solutions of a 3D spherical piston problem for the compressible Euler equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper establishes the global well-posedness of shock solutions for a 3D spherical piston problem to the compressible Euler equations. The main mathematical challenges are the nonlinear coupling between the free shock boundary and the moving piston, alongside potential gradient catastrophes induced by spherical geometric source terms. To overcome these difficulties, we reformulate the problem using Riemann invariants and introduce a tailored directional derivative along the unperturbed piston trajectory. Then we can extend the local solution to construct a global piecewise smooth solution including a single shock under some moderate assumptions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On statistical inference for non-linear dynamical systems evolving in their global attractor
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a periodic scalar reaction-diffusion system over a two-dimensional domain under natural conditions on the reaction function and with initial condition $θ$. We show that on the global attractor $\mathcal A$ of the resulting dynamical system $(u_θ(t):t>0)$, a reverse Poincaré inequality holds true, and that as a consequence the map $θ\mapsto u_θ(t)$ satisfies an $L^2(\Om)$-Lipschitz stability estimate on $\mathcal A$ for any $t>0$ fixed. We then show that statistical recovery of an initial condition $θ$ in the attractor $\mathcal A$, as well as prediction of the states $u_θ$, is possible from discrete measurements of the system at parametric $1/\sqrt N$ convergence rates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of Extremizers and Convergence of the Euler-Lagrange Iteration for the Critical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev Inequality
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $n \ge 3$, $2 \le α< n$, and $1 < p,r < \infty$ satisfy $p^{-1}+r^{-1}=1+α/n$. We prove uniqueness, up to common translations and dilations, of the normalized nonnegative extremizing pairs for the corresponding Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality. More generally, all positive finite-energy solutions of the Euler-Lagrange system belong to a single symmetry orbit. The proof compares two solutions at different relative scales. Total positivity of order two identifies the second eigenspace of an associated compact self-adjoint operator and forces each nonzero difference to change sign exactly once. The opposite orientations obtained at the two ends of the scale parameter then yield uniqueness. The same method proves radial nondegeneracy modulo dilation. We also establish strong convergence of the normalized alternating Euler-Lagrange iteration from every nonnegative, radially nonincreasing initial datum to a fixed extremizing pair, without rescaling the iterates. Square-root mass variables reduce the exclusion of several concentration profiles to a static spectral estimate and an energy-increment argument. The analysis includes sublinear exponents and the logarithmic borderline decay regimes.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Viscosity-variational inequality solutions of fully nonlinear second-order stationary mean field games with nonseparable and nondifferentiable Hamiltonians
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We analyse stationary fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic second-order mean field games with nonseparable and nondifferentiable Hamiltonians by introducing the notion of viscosity-variational inequality solution. In this formulation of the problem, the value function is the viscosity solution of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, and the Kolmogorov--Fokker--Planck (KFP) equation for the player density is understood as a nonstandard variational inequality that no longer involves partial derivatives of the value function. The advantages of this formulation are found in its stability and continuity properties for handling weak convergence arguments, which we use to prove the existence of solutions of the problem. Furthermore, we prove the equivalence of the notion of viscosity-variational inequality solution with the notion of a partial differential inclusion solution, where the value function is a strong solution of the HJB equation and the player density is a very weak solution of the KFP equation with coefficients belonging to subdifferential sets of the Hamiltonian. Finally, we prove the uniqueness of solutions in the case of separable Hamiltonians with strictly monotone couplings.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Failure of Pólya-Szegő inequality for weighted nonlocal seminorm and on nonlocal C-K-N inequality
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We create counterexamples to show that Pólya-Szegő type of inequality fails for the weighted nonlocal seminorm \begin{equation*}
  [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} := \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \frac{|x|^{α_{1} p} |y|^{α_{2} p} |u(x)-u(y)|^{p}}{|x-y|^{d+sp}} \, dx \, dy \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} \ , \end{equation*} in all three regimes $α_1 +α_2 < 0, \, α_1 +α_2 = 0$, and $α_1 +α_2 >0$. These counterexamples are such that it completely settles the first two cases for all parameters. We also provide necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters for $ [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} < \infty$, thus extending an earlier known result of [Serena Dipierro and Enrico Valdinoci, A density property for fractional weighted Sobolev spaces]. We also provide another proof of the fractional C-K-N type inequality, for most of the parameters (Hardy and Sobolev are included), using a familiar technique which is involved in the proof of fractional Sobolev inequality of [Eleonora Di Nezza, Giampiero Palatucci, and Enrico Valdinoci, Hitchhiker's guide to the fractional Sobolev spaces, Bulletin des sciences mathematiques] together with a symmetrization technique.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gradient potential estimates for k-Hessian equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For $2\le k<n$, we prove pointwise gradient bounds for proper weak $k$-convex functions in terms of a local average and a Wolff potential of the full Hessian measure $F_k[u]$. The estimate yields local Lipschitz regularity for $F_k[u]=f$ with $f\in L^{n/k,1/k}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and for $F_k[u]=|Du|^p$ when $0<p<nk/(n-k)$. Both the Lorentz index $1/k$ and the upper bound on $p$ are sharp.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
(Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.)
  We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations.
  As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 94 pages. Updated funding info. To appear in Mem. Eur. Math. Soc

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-Isothermal Plane Couette Flow for the Boltzmann Equation in Three Dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Boltzmann equation for a non-isothermal plane Couette flow in the three-dimensional channel $\mathbb T_x\times(-1,1)_y\times\mathbb T_z$ for Maxwell molecules. For sufficiently small shear rate and wall temperature perturbations, we construct a unique steady solution near the global Maxwellian. For the corresponding unsteady boundary value problem, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions arising from small perturbations of the steady state, together with their exponential convergence to the steady state as $t\to\infty$. A major difficulty in both the steady and unsteady problems is to close the outgoing mass fluxes generated by diffuse reflection. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new boundary flux transmission framework which, in the slab geometry, yields steady and time-dependent wall flux estimates through the boundary-to-boundary transmission between the two walls. We further extend this framework to damped transport equations with diffuse reflection in general bounded $C^1$ domains, even when the damping coefficient degenerates at large velocities.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy for a critical Choquard equation with Hardy potential
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the critical Choquard equation \[ -Δu-μ|x|^{-2}u =\bigl(|\cdot|^{2-N}*|u|^p\bigr)|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^N, \] where $|\cdot|^{2-N}$ is the Newton kernel, $p=\frac{N+2}{N-2}$, and $0<μ<\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}$. For every $N\ge3$, we prove that positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb R^N)$ are radially symmetric about the origin, unique up to dilation, and nondegenerate. Our proof uses normalized logarithmic derivatives to obtain a cooperative system. The resulting monotonicity principle underlies both the uniqueness and nondegeneracy arguments, and remains effective in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$, corresponding to $N\ge7$. Consequently, the linearized quadratic form has Morse index one and the sharp inequality admits a global quadratic remainder estimate. The best constant is strictly concave in the Hardy parameter on $\bigl[0,\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}\bigr)$, is of class $C^2$ with strictly negative second derivative in the interior, and satisfies two-sided bounds that agree to first order at $μ=0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Revised exposition and expanded declaration of AI assistance

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-simple blow-up for the Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on Riemannian surfaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The existence and structure of non-simple blow-up are fundamental questions for the self-dual Chern--Simons--Higgs equation. Physically, this phenomenon describes magnetic-flux concentration in several cores whose mutual distances are much larger than their widths, although all cores approach the same vortex point. Despite substantial progress for singular Liouville equations, the existence of non-simple blow-up solutions to the full Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on closed surfaces has remained open in both the Chern--Simons (CS) and mean-field regimes.
